articles.title: FIU vs Liberty: Panthers Get Buried 49-10 in Lynchburg
articles.matchup: Final: Liberty (7-1) 49, Florida International (3-5) 10, Sat., Oct. 31, Williams Stadium (VA), Lynchburg. Next: vs Missouri State, Sat., Nov. 7, Pitbull Stadium, Miami
articles.text:
Liberty 49, FIU 10, and there is no dressing this one up. Back home, the city commission's trunk-or-treat and costume contest at the Jorge Mas Canosa Youth Center on NW 114th Avenue was handing out free candy and live music Saturday night. Up in Lynchburg, our Panthers were handing out touchdowns, seven of them, on Liberty's Homecoming.

It didn't start that way. Liberty scored first, but on our second drive JJ Kohl moved us 46 yards into Liberty territory before Jeremiah Vessel blocked the 47-yard field goal. Three plays later Shamir Sterlin intercepted Deshawn Purdie at our 40. We had the ball back at 7-0, went three plays for 4 yards and punted.

After that Liberty took over. A 14-play drive that ate 7:18. Another 77 yards in eight plays. Samuel Cohen intercepted Kohl at our 42, and Kam Davis scored his second touchdown with 41 seconds left. 28-0 at the half, then 42-0 after three.

The protection was the story. Kohl got sacked four times and lost 40 yards running, so we finished with 34 rushing yards as a team. Liberty converted five of eight third downs, and Purdie missed only three throws all day.

Credit to the kids who kept swinging. Kohl went 21 of 28 for 164 yards and capped a six-play, 72-yard drive with a 14-yard touchdown to Jojo Stone. Robert Czeremcha hit from 38 after a 14-play march. Kyle McNeal caught six for 56, Devonte Lyons ran for 52, and Andre Brown returned four kickoffs for 72. Da'Vontae Floyd, Demetrius Hill and DeAndre Boykins made eight tackles apiece, and Germaine Carter got a sack.

I made my colada before kickoff, enough for the whole block. I drank most of it myself by halftime.

We're 3-5, 1-3 in Conference USA and 0-4 on the road. Next is Missouri State at Pitbull Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 7, and we need it back home. ¡Vamos, Panthers!

articles.title: Liberty vs FIU: Flames Torch Panthers 49-10 at Homecoming
articles.matchup: Final: Liberty (7-1) 49, Florida International (3-5) 10, Sat., Oct. 31, Williams Stadium (VA), Lynchburg. Next: at New Mexico State, Sat., Nov. 7, Aggie Memorial Stadium, Las Cruces
articles.text:
Liberty 49, FIU 10, and Homecoming at Williams Stadium went exactly the way we drew it up. Friday night, lantern-lit tours at the Presbyterian Cemetery Ghost Walk on Bailey Street introduced visitors to six people from Lynchburg's past. Saturday our Flames scored seven touchdowns and sent FIU home with nothing to show until the fourth quarter.

The defense made its first big play early. FIU drove 46 yards on its second series, and Jeremiah Vessel blocked a 47-yard field goal. We gave one away right after, when Deshawn Purdie got intercepted by Shamir Sterlin, and that was the last good news the Panthers got for a long time.

Jaylon Coleman had already opened the scoring with a 14-yard run. Then came a 14-play, 81-yard drive that ate 7:18 and ended with Kam Davis plowing in from the 3. Ethan Vasko pushed in from the 1, Samuel Cohen intercepted JJ Kohl to set up the next one, and Davis scored again from 2 with 41 seconds left. 28-0 at the half.

Purdie was surgical: 16 of 19 for 227 yards, including an 11-yard touchdown to Zeke Wimbush to open the third. Vasko scored his second 1-yard touchdown, and Kanye Udoh added another from the 1 in the fourth. Makai Jackson caught six balls for 86 yards and nearly had a 68-yard punt return touchdown, called back on a holding flag.

The front was relentless. We sacked Kohl four times, with Lorenzo Payne in on two, Markus Clark and Brenton Williams getting one each, and FIU finished with 34 rushing yards. The Panthers' only points came on a 38-yard field goal and a late touchdown throw after we were up 49-3.

I teach my middle-schoolers that you finish every rep. These guys finished every rep, then asked for more.

We're 7-1 and 4-0 in Conference USA. Next is a trip to Las Cruces to face New Mexico State at Aggie Memorial Stadium on Saturday night, Nov. 7. Go Flames.

articles.title: UL Monroe vs Southern Miss: Late Rally Falls Short 35-21
articles.matchup: Final: Southern Miss (3-5) 35, UL Monroe (1-7) 21, Sat., Oct. 31, Malone Stadium, Monroe. Next: at Arkansas State, Sat., Nov. 7, Centennial Bank Stadium, Jonesboro
articles.text:
Southern Miss 35, UL Monroe 21. It was Halloween in Monroe, the Black Out Breast Cancer game, and fans were asked to wear black for Breast Cancer Awareness Month. It's also the first season under the FMOL Health St. Francis Stadium name, with an installation underway to honor Coach James Malone. The Warhawks gave the folks in black a fourth quarter worth staying for, just not a win.

Late-night radio, Delta style, optimism counter on the desk. We start at zero, because the first half was ugly. Southern Miss scored on a 33-yard run and a field goal, and we trailed 10-0 at the break. Abram Murray missed his only field-goal try.

Click one on the counter: Aidan Armenta hit Marcellus Jackson for 83 yards and a touchdown early in the third. 10-7, house alive. Then the defense gave up a 21-yard run, a 21-yard touchdown throw and a field goal, and it was 27-7.

Click two, click three. Armenta ran it in from 1 early in the fourth. Then he found Nic Trujillo from 2 with 6:47 left. 27-21, and that rally was real. Then Jamarice Wilder went 32 yards with 1:52 left, and the conversion made it 35-21.

Straight talk for the night shift. Armenta went 19 of 34 for 202 yards with two touchdowns and ran for another. We lost two fumbles and went zero for three on fourth down. Southern Miss ran for 249 yards on us. Don Chaney led us with 54 rushing yards. Noah Flemmings made 10 tackles with a half sack, and Taijh Overton added nine.

We are 1-7 and 1-3 in the Sun Belt, still hunting the first home win. Next is Arkansas State at Centennial Bank Stadium in Jonesboro on Saturday, Nov. 7, at 3 PM ET. Counter reads three. Keep the radio on. Go Hawks.

articles.title: Southern Miss vs UL Monroe: Wilder Seals Road Win 35-21
articles.matchup: Final: Southern Miss (3-5) 35, UL Monroe (1-7) 21, Sat., Oct. 31, Malone Stadium, Monroe. Next: vs James Madison, Thu., Nov. 5, M. M. Roberts Stadium, Hattiesburg
articles.text:
Southern Miss 35, UL Monroe 21. Back home, Main Street in downtown Hattiesburg hosted the sixth annual Taste of the South Food Truck Festival from 11 to 6, and the Dia de los Muertos Parade stepped off at 4. Our Golden Eagles were busy in Monroe, serving up a road win to eat with it.

Ladies, pearls on, because this was a grown-up performance for most of the day. Steven Robinson broke a 33-yard touchdown run in the second quarter and finished with 151 yards on 21 carries. Creighton Wilbanks hit from 36 before the half and from 39 late in the third, two for two. In between, Jamarice Wilder ran in from 21 and Landry Lyddy found Grant Page for a 21-yard score. That made it 27-7, and we should have been planning the after-party.

Then the chapter got sloppy. ULM scored twice in the fourth and cut it to 27-21 with 6:47 left. That's the kind of thing that gets you a stern talk at Monday's meeting. Wilder settled it with a 32-yard touchdown run with 1:52 left, and Lyddy found Mario Sanders for the two-point conversion. 35-21, pearls straight, everybody breathe.

We ran for 249 yards, and Wilder added 104 on 15 carries with two scores. We committed zero turnovers, and Malakai Murphy and Cace Reed each recovered a fumble. Landon Sylvie made 11 tackles. Kobi Albert got a sack.

Now the honest minutes. Lyddy went 15 of 30 for 130 yards. We went 5-18 on third down and took nine penalties for 87 yards. That is not how a lady carries herself in public, and James Madison will not forgive it.

We are 3-5 and 2-2 in the Sun Belt with two straight wins. James Madison comes to M. M. Roberts Stadium on Thursday, Nov. 5, at 8 PM ET. Iron the dress and polish the pearls. To the Top.

articles.title: North Dakota State vs UTEP: Bison Defense Smothers Miners 31-7
articles.matchup: Final: North Dakota State (7-2) 31, UTEP (1-7) 7, Sat., Oct. 31, Fargodome, Fargo. Next: at Hawai'i, Sat., Nov. 14, 11:00 PM ET, Clarence T.C. Ching Athletics Complex, Honolulu
articles.text:
North Dakota State 31, UTEP 7. Halloween morning, the Red River Market wrapped up its 12th season at Broadway Square downtown, with more than 60 vendors and folks in costume, and by afternoon 15,513 of us were inside the Fargodome with hotdish in our bellies. Uff da, what a start, though.

UTEP's Raymond Moore III went 57 yards on the Miners' first snap, and Kaleb Miles had already intercepted Nathan Hayes on our opening drive. 7-0 Miners. Our defense shut the door after that and didn't let them score again. Not once.

Our offense ate clock early in the second, 83 yards and 8:10 for a Drew Klein field goal from 30. 7-3. Then Hayes hit Jackson Williams deep to the 5, and DJ Scott burst in on fourth-and-goal from the 1. 10-7, our first lead in six quarters. Late in the third, Reis Kessel caught a 30-yarder to the 5 and then a 3-yard touchdown. 17-7.

The dagger came late. We converted a fourth-and-1 in our own territory, Williams caught a 48-yarder to the 2, and Hayes snuck it in from the 1. 24-7. Williams finished with 10 catches for 111 yards. Kessel had six for 85. Hayes went 22 of 32 for 240 yards.

And that defense is a brick wall. Donovan Woolen made 11 tackles with 2.5 for loss and a sack. Marion Moore intercepted Colson on third-and-10, his fifth this season, and then scooped a fumble and went 46 yards for the final score. 31-7. UTEP had 29 passing yards halfway through the fourth quarter. Will Steil grabbed an interception too, though a personal foul on the return cost us 47 yards of field position. We went 3 of 3 on fourth down all day.

We're 7-2 and 4-2 in the Mountain West. We get a week off, then fly to Hawai'i for Saturday, Nov. 14, at 11:00 PM ET. Pack the sunscreen. Go Bison.

articles.title: UTEP vs North Dakota State: Miners Strike First, Fall 31-7
articles.matchup: Final: North Dakota State (7-2) 31, UTEP (1-7) 7, Sat., Oct. 31, Fargodome, Fargo. Next: vs. Hawai'i, Sat., Nov. 7, 9:30 PM ET, Sun Bowl, El Paso
articles.text:
North Dakota State 31, UTEP 7. Back home on Halloween morning, folks were hiking the Franklin Mountains in costume at the state park's Halloween Fest, and the rest of us were packing up the Hatch-hot salsa and heading north in spirit. First trip to a dome since 2022, first game ever against the Bison. For one play, it felt like a party.

That one play was a beauty. Raymond Moore III took his first snap at quarterback, found a huge hole and went 57 yards to the house. 7-0 Miners, early in the first quarter. Kaleb Miles had already intercepted Nathan Hayes on the Bison's opening drive. We had Fargo quiet.

Then the Bison went to work, and we didn't score again. NDSU ground out an 83-yard drive for a field goal, then punched in a fourth-and-goal from the 1 for a 10-7 lead. A 3-yard touchdown throw to Reis Kessel late in the third made it 17-7. Two scores in the final two minutes made it 31-7.

The killers were turnovers. We came to Fargo with back-to-back games without a giveaway, and we left with three. EJ Colson Jr. threw two interceptions, the last one under heavy pressure on third down with about six minutes left. Then a Jaden Smith fumble went 46 yards the other way. That's how a 17-7 fight turns ugly.

Give the defense its due against the top defense in the Mountain West. Esteban Guillory made 12 tackles, double his old career best. Kode Lowe made 10, and Justin Content made nine with two tackles for loss. We ran for 147 yards. Moore had 67 of them on three carries.

We're 1-7 and 0-4 in the Mountain West. Hawai'i comes to the Sun Bowl on Saturday, Nov. 7, at 9:30 PM ET, and our last Halloween win was in 1998, against those same Warriors. Bring the green chile. Axes up, Miners.

articles.title: South Alabama vs Louisiana Tech: Jaguars Fade, Fall 35-20
articles.matchup: Final: Louisiana Tech (6-2) 35, South Alabama (4-4) 20, Sat., Oct. 31, Hancock Whitney Stadium, Mobile. Next: at Louisiana, Sat., Nov. 7, Our Lady of Lourdes Stadium, Lafayette
articles.text:
Louisiana Tech 35, South Alabama 20, and the second half played like a horror movie. Down on Dauphin Street, the Crescent Theater ran Nosferatu with a live, improvised score Friday and Saturday nights. Our Jaguars put on their own silent picture at Hancock Whitney Stadium: 20 points before halftime and not a sound after it.

The first quarter rolled like a Mardi Gras parade. Our defense sacked Blake Baker twice on Tech's opening drive, and Jared Hollins hit Anthony Eager for a 10-yard touchdown. After Tech tied it, we went 75 yards in 14 plays, burned 7:33, and Hollins found Eager again from 9. 14-7 after one.

The second quarter is where the float lost a wheel. Tech scored three touchdowns in under 10 minutes, and one came right after we turned it over on downs near midfield. Keenan Phillips gave us an 11-yard touchdown run, but the extra point failed, and Baker found Marcus Calwise Jr. from 35 to make it 28-20 at the half.

Then nothing. Seven second-half drives, zero points. Phillips fumbled at our 6 late in the third, and Tech scored two plays later. We came up empty on fourth down twice more, the last on a throw to Eager broken up in the end zone, and Janard Lockhardt intercepted Hollins at the Tech 5 with 1:40 left.

Honest numbers: we outgained Tech 397 to 315, won the ground game 205 to 121 and held the ball for 33:23. But 12 penalties for 100 yards, two turnovers and a 1-of-4 day on fourth down will sink anybody. Hollins finished 14 of 31 for 192 yards with two touchdowns and the interception.

Credit where it's due. Eager caught seven balls for 102 yards and both scores. PJ Martin ran for 82 on 12 carries, and Phillips added 62 on the ground and 68 on kick returns. Seidrion Langston made eight tackles, and Masey Lewis and Xavious Anderson Jr. each had a sack.

I blew my float-builder's whistle so hard in the first quarter that the row behind me checked on me. By the fourth it stayed in my purse.

We're 4-4 and 2-2 in the Sun Belt. Next is a trip to Lafayette to face Louisiana at Our Lady of Lourdes Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 7. Go Jags.

Keenan Phillips gave us an 11-yard touchdown run, but the extra point failed, and Baker found Marcus Calwise Jr. from 35 to make it 28-20 at the half.

Then nothing. Seven second-half drives, zero points. Phillips fumbled at our 6 late in the third, and Tech scored two plays later. We came up empty on fourth down twice more, the last on a throw to Eager broken up in the end zone, and Janard Lockhardt intercepted Hollins at the Tech 5 with 1:40 left.

Honest numbers: we outgained Tech 397 to 315, won the ground game 205 to 121 and held the ball for 33:23. But 12 penalties for 100 yards, two turnovers and a 1-of-4 day on fourth down will sink anybody. Hollins finished 14 of 31 for 192 yards with two touchdowns and the interception.

Credit where it's due. Eager caught seven balls for 102 yards and both scores. PJ Martin ran for 82 on 12 carries, and Phillips added 62 on the ground and 68 on kick returns. Seidrion Langston made eight tackles, and Masey Lewis and Xavious Anderson Jr. each had a sack.
I blew my float-builder's whistle so hard in the first quarter that the row behind me checked on me. By the fourth it stayed in my purse.
We're 4-4 and 2-2 in the Sun Belt. Next is a trip to Lafayette to face Louisiana at Our Lady of Lourdes Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 7. Go Jags.

articles.title: Louisiana Tech vs South Alabama: Bulldogs Roll in Mobile 35-20
articles.matchup: Final: Louisiana Tech (6-2) 35, South Alabama (4-4) 20, Sat., Oct. 31, Hancock Whitney Stadium, Mobile. Next: at Troy, Sat., Nov. 7, Veterans Memorial Stadium, Troy
articles.text:
Louisiana Tech 35, South Alabama 20, and we're 4-0 in the Sun Belt. Halloween morning back home started with the Depot Dash, a costumed 5K through downtown Ruston and along the Greenway. By 2 o'clock in Mobile our Bulldogs were running their own race, and they finished it out front with nobody gaining in the second half.

It started rough. Our first drive went backward with Blake Baker sacked twice, and South Alabama went up 7-0 on a 10-yard Jared Hollins throw to Anthony Eager. We answered in four plays. Baker hit Rayshun Hurt on a short throw that turned into a 67-yard catch-and-run to the Jaguars 4, and Andrew Burnette punched it in from there.

South Alabama went back up 14-7 with a 14-play drive that ate 7:33. Then we hung 21 on them in the second quarter. Hurt broke a 30-yard run and Baker found Marcus Calwise Jr. for a 22-yard touchdown. After a fourth-down stop, Trey Kukuk threw 27 yards to Jalen Mickens for the lead. The Jaguars answered with an 11-yard Keenan Phillips run but missed the extra point, and Baker hit Calwise again from 35. 28-20 at the half.

The second half belonged to the defense. South Alabama had seven drives after the break and scored on none of them. MJ Moultrie II knocked the ball away from Phillips at the Jaguars 6, Alonzo Jackson Jr. recovered, and two plays later Baker found Luke Watkins for a 4-yard touchdown. The Jaguars came up empty on fourth down twice, and Janard Lockhardt intercepted Hollins at our 5 with 1:40 left.

Baker went 10 of 16 for 167 yards and three touchdowns, and we didn't turn it over once. Jackson led us with nine tackles and the fumble recovery, Taeden Rogers had seven tackles and a sack, and Emmanuel Oguns added another. South Alabama got flagged 12 times for 100 yards.

Out at the farm we grade peaches by feel, and this one's firm all the way through. Peachy!

We're 6-2 and unbeaten in league play. Next is a trip to Troy and Veterans Memorial Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 7. Go Dawgs.

articles.title: Louisville vs Stanford: Isaac Brown's Four Scores Rule 52-24
articles.matchup: Final: Louisville (5-3) 52, Stanford (4-5) 24, Sat., Oct. 31, L&N Federal Credit Union Stadium, Louisville. Next: at Georgia Tech, Sat., Nov. 7, Bobby Dodd Stadium, Atlanta
articles.text:
Louisville 52, Stanford 24. Homecoming at L&N Federal Credit Union Stadium, presented by Kentucky Tourism, and the Cardinals threw a party worthy of the best hat in the house. Isaac Brown scored four touchdowns, the first Louisville player to do it since Lamar Jackson ran for four against Florida State in 2016. Put that on the mantel.

It was not a smooth party early. Brown ran in from 5 in the first quarter, but Stanford kept answering. Davis Warren hit for 41 and 75 yards in the second quarter, and the visitors led 17-14. Carson Hilbert tied it with a 35-yard field goal, and Lincoln Kienholz found TreyShun Hurry for 22 yards with 15 seconds left. 24-17 at the half. Then Stanford tied it 24-24 early in the third.

That was the last time the guests got a seat at the table. Louisville scored the final 28 points. Kienholz hit Brown for an 18-yard touchdown. Tayon Holloway scooped a Stanford fumble and ran it back 31 yards. Brown went 23 yards for another score late in the third, then 75 yards early in the fourth to finish it.

Brown carried nine times for 139 yards and added three catches. Kienholz went 20 of 28 for 250 yards with two touchdowns and ran nine times for 62 yards and a score. Tre Richardson caught 10 balls for 140 yards. We piled up 545 yards, 296 on the ground at 9.0 a carry. Jabari Mack grabbed an interception and Stanquan Clark made eight tackles. Stanford went 2-16 on third down.

The honest part, because a hostess notices the stains on the tablecloth. Stanford hit three long touchdown throws, including that 75-yarder, and Hilbert missed one field goal. Clean that up before the road trip.

We are 5-3 and 4-2 in the ACC, and that's three wins in a row. Next is Georgia Tech at Bobby Dodd Stadium in Atlanta on Saturday, Nov. 7, at 7:30 PM ET. Pack the good hat. Go Cards.

articles.title: Stanford vs Louisville: Cardinal Tied at 24, Then Fall 52-24
articles.matchup: Final: Louisville (5-3) 52, Stanford (4-5) 24, Sat., Oct. 31, L&N Federal Credit Union Stadium, Louisville. Next: at Virginia Tech, Sat., Nov. 14, Lane Stadium, Blacksburg
articles.text:
Louisville 52, Stanford 24. On campus Saturday night, Cardinal Nights turned White Plaza into a Halloween arcade from 8 to 11 p.m., with pinball, air hockey, a claw machine and nine holes of mini golf. Our Cardinal got crushed in Kentucky hours earlier. At least the arcade games back home give you another quarter.

For one half, the product worked. Emmet Kenney hit a 48-yard field goal, and Davis Warren found Nico Brown for 41 yards and a touchdown. Then Warren hit Aiden Black for 75 yards on one throw, and we led 17-14. Louisville answered with a field goal and a touchdown with 15 seconds left in the half, but when Warren found Micah Ford for 40 yards early in the third, it was 24-24 on the road.

Then the whole system crashed. Louisville scored the last 28 points. The worst bug: Nico Brown caught a ball, fumbled, and Tayon Holloway returned it 31 yards for a touchdown. Brown still finished with six catches for 109 yards, and he deserved a better ending. Isaac Brown ran through us for 139 yards and three rushing scores, the last one from 75.

Post-mortem, no spin. Warren went 23 of 37 for 270 yards with three touchdowns and an interception. We ran for 81 yards. We were 2-16 on third down and 4 of 8 on fourth down, which means we lived on fourth down all day. We gave up 545 yards and 296 on the ground. Jay Green made eight tackles and broke up two throws. Darrius Davis also had eight.

We are 4-5 and 2-4 in the ACC, and still winless in four road games. A week ago we beat NC State at home. Consistency is the feature we have not built yet.

Next is a week off, then Virginia Tech at Lane Stadium in Blacksburg on Saturday, Nov. 14. Fix the roadmap, debug the defense, and push the next release. Go Card.

articles.title: San José State vs New Mexico: Spartans Fall Short 21-16
articles.matchup: Final: New Mexico (7-1) 21, San José State (4-5) 16, Sat., Oct. 31, CEFCU Stadium, San José. Next: vs. Northern Illinois, Sat., Nov. 7, CEFCU Stadium, San José
articles.text:
New Mexico 21, San José State 16, and our last drive died in the end zone with 11 seconds left. CEFCU Stadium did Halloween right: Trick or Treat with the Spartans and Youth Spirit Day, the Spartan Boo Bash with trick-or-treat stations and pumpkin decorating in the Simpkins Stadium Center, and local youth dance and cheer groups on the field at halftime. The kids shipped a clean release. The football team shipped a bug.

Let me file the incident report. Our defense was ready. Trajan Sinatra hit field goals from 25, 24 and 28 yards, and we trailed only 14-9 at the half after two Scottre Humphrey touchdown runs. New Mexico pushed it to 21-9 in the third on a 20-yard throw to Cade Keith.

Then Tuli Tagovailoa-Amosa pushed the hotfix. He intercepted Toa Fa'avae and ran it back 89 yards for a touchdown with 10:47 left. 21-16. Justin Stearns blocked a 51-yard field goal try later in the fourth. Dylan Lee and Brian Dukes Jr. also intercepted Fa'avae. Three takeaways, and Lee led us with seven tackles.

Here is the bug. Our offense ran 35 times for 48 yards, and you cannot ship a product with that kind of latency. Luke Weaver threw two interceptions, the first on our series right after that interception return. Late in the fourth we drove into New Mexico territory and failed on fourth down at 1:23. We got the ball back, Weaver hit Anthony Ivey for 39 yards to the New Mexico 34 with 16 seconds left, and the next throw got intercepted in the end zone. Rollback.

Weaver finished 16 of 23 for 190 yards. Carson Clark caught eight balls for 91 yards, and Jabari Bates carried 22 times for 63. New Mexico ran for 231 yards, and its first win in San José since 1969 came against us. That stings.

We are 4-5 and 2-3 in the Mountain West. Northern Illinois comes to CEFCU Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 7. Patch the run game, run the tests, and ship it to prod, Spartans.

articles.title: New Mexico vs San José State: Lobos End 57-Year Wait 21-16
articles.matchup: Final: New Mexico (7-1) 21, San José State (4-5) 16, Sat., Oct. 31, CEFCU Stadium, San José. Next: at Nevada, Fri., Nov. 6, Mackay Stadium, Reno
articles.text:
New Mexico 21, San José State 16, and the Lobos won in San José for the first time since Nov. 1, 1969. Back home, Old Town Albuquerque was getting its plazas ready for Halloween trick-or-treating, 4 to 7 p.m., music and costumes all over the historic district. While the kids filled their bags, the Lobos ended a streak older than most of the people in those plazas.

Fifty-seven years. My abuela was a teenager the last time this happened. This team does not care about the history, and I love that about them. Scottre Humphrey ran in from 1 yard and then from 7 yards in the second quarter, and we led 14-9 at the half. Kiefer Sibley ran 12 times for 102 yards, Humphrey added 87, and New Mexico ran for 231 yards as a team. That ground game was hotter than Hatch green chile.

In the third quarter, we went 89 yards in nine plays and Toa Fa'avae hit Cade Keith for a 20-yard touchdown. 21-9. Then my chile went cold. Fa'avae threw three interceptions, and Tuli Tagovailoa-Amosa took one back 89 yards for a touchdown with 10:47 left to make it 21-16. Our 51-yard field goal try got blocked too. I am not going to pretend that was pretty.

But this defense flies like a balloon at dawn on Fiesta morning, steady and high. Jayden Flaker intercepted Luke Weaver on San José State's next series. Darren Agu sacked Weaver twice in the game. San José State drove into our territory late, and Mercury Swaim hurried Weaver into a fourth-down incompletion at 1:23. Then the Spartans hit a 39-yard throw with 16 seconds left, and Austin Brawley intercepted Weaver in the end zone with 11 seconds to go. Game over. Ormanie Arnold and Swaim each made seven tackles, and San José State ran for just 48 yards on 35 carries.

New Mexico is 7-1 and 4-0 in the Mountain West. Next we go to Nevada at Mackay Stadium on Friday, Nov. 6. Red, green, or Christmas, Lobos. Just keep winning.

articles.title: Georgia State vs Coastal Carolina: Panthers Rally Late, Fall 31-20
articles.matchup: Final: Coastal Carolina (3-5) 31, Georgia State (4-4) 20, Sat., Oct. 31, Center Parc Stadium, Atlanta. Next: at App State, Sat., Nov. 7, Kidd Brewer Stadium, Boone
articles.text:
Coastal Carolina 31, Georgia State 20. Halloween at Center Parc Stadium had everything we asked for: a wear-black call, a pumpkin carving station at the Panther Pregame, kids trick-or-treating all over the stadium. The one thing missing was a team that showed up before the fourth quarter.

We got on the board first. Samer Layous hit a 32-yard field goal late in the first. Then traffic stopped dead. Coastal scored 17 straight in the second quarter, two touchdowns from Deuce Bailey and a 53-yard field goal. Layous kicked another 32-yarder as time ran out, and we went in down 17-6. Two more Coastal touchdowns in the third and it was 31-6. That's the Downtown Connector at 5 p.m. on a Friday.

The defense did get its hands on the ball. We intercepted Bailey twice. Alex Mullings took the second one to the Coastal 1, where Bailey knocked it loose, and it went for a touchback. We got the ball back and handed it right back to them.

The fourth quarter was the express lane. Ayden Pereira hit Grant Hollier for 9 yards and then found Qwantavius Wiggins for two. Antonio Wesley recovered a Bailey fumble at the Coastal 18, and Pereira finished the drive with an 18-yard touchdown to DJ Riles. 31-20 with 7:38 left. The two-point throw failed. Then we turned it over on downs at 3:12 and took a sack on the last snap.

Real numbers. Pereira went 20 of 37 for 200 yards and two touchdowns. Wiggins ran 11 times for 96 yards with a 58-yard burst. We ran for 160 yards. We drew nine penalties for 96 yards and went 5 of 15 on third down. Coby Owens made nine tackles with two for loss, and Tyson McCrary added eight.

Three straight losses. We are 4-4 and 1-3 in the Sun Belt.

Next is App State at Kidd Brewer Stadium in Boone on Saturday, Nov. 7, at 2:30 PM ET. Long drive up the mountain. Start the engine early this time. Let's go, Panthers.

articles.title: Coastal Carolina vs Georgia State: Coppock Rules Atlanta 31-20
articles.matchup: Final: Coastal Carolina (3-5) 31, Georgia State (4-4) 20, Sat., Oct. 31, Center Parc Stadium, Atlanta. Next: vs. Old Dominion, Sat., Nov. 7, Brooks Stadium, Conway
articles.text:
Coastal Carolina 31, Georgia State 20. Back in Conway, downtown has been the City of Halloween all month, and trick-or-treat ran from 5:30 to 8:30 p.m. Saturday. The Chanticleers had the best treat in the bag before the first porch light came on.

The tide came in during the second quarter and never went back out. Georgia State kicked a field goal in the first. Then Deuce Bailey found Clayton Coppock Jr. for 21 yards, Nico Cavanillas Alti drilled a 53-yarder, his fourth from 50 or longer this season, and Bailey hit Zach Courtney for 25 yards on an 80-yard drive. Seventeen straight points. We led 17-6 at the half.

Coppock is from Atlanta, and he played like he wanted the whole city to hear about it. His 31-yard touchdown in the third quarter capped another 80-yard drive, and he finished with six catches for a career-high 100 yards and two scores. Jaden Allen-Hendrix ran in from 2, and it was 31-6 after three quarters.

Bailey had a strange, gritty day. He went 22 of 32 for 297 yards and three touchdowns, and he threw two interceptions. On the second one, the Georgia State defender carried it all the way to our 1, and Bailey chased him down and knocked the ball loose. Touchback. Our ball. That's a quarterback who refuses to let a mistake stand.

Now the part I won't sugarcoat. Bailey got sacked and fumbled at our 18 in the fourth, and Georgia State scored right after. We ran for 73 yards on 35 carries, drew eight penalties and let a 31-6 lead shrink to 31-20 with 7:38 left. My granddad would call that leaving the nets out in weather.

The defense pulled them back in. Georgia State turned it over on downs with 3:12 left, and Jesse Powell II and a teammate sacked Ayden Pereira on the last snap. Ja'Marion Wayne made 11 tackles and broke up two throws. We went 2 for 2 on fourth down.

We are 3-5 and 2-2 in the Sun Belt. Old Dominion comes to Brooks Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 7, at 1 PM ET. Back to the dock. Chant it loud.

articles.title: East Carolina vs Temple: Pirates Run, Intercept Way to 17-9 Win
articles.matchup: Final: East Carolina (4-4) 17, Temple (2-6) 9, Sat., Oct. 31, Dowdy-Ficklen Stadium, Greenville. Next: vs. South Florida, Fri., Nov. 6, 7:30 PM ET, Dowdy-Ficklen Stadium, Greenville
articles.text:
East Carolina 17, Temple 9. Halloween at Dowdy-Ficklen meant Fan Appreciation Day: $10.31 tickets, a Pirate Walk with the team handing out candy, a costume parade behind the players, and brand-new white helmets with marching PeeDee on the side. The crew dressed sharp and played tough. Hoist the colors.

The opening broadside came late in the first quarter. We went 77 yards on 13 plays, and Ashton Gray hammered it in from the 1. 7-0. Noah Perez added a 20-yard field goal with 10 seconds left in the half, and we took a 10-3 lead to the locker room.

Then came the real cannon fire. We took the second-half kickoff and went 75 yards on 14 plays, and TJ Engleman Jr. ripped off a 19-yard touchdown run. 17-3. Engleman finished with 107 yards on 16 carries. We ran for 222 yards as a crew on 45 carries, and that's how Pirates win a fistfight.

The defense flew the black flag. Angelo Ross intercepted Ajani Sheppard right after Temple stopped our fake punt. The secondary intercepted another at our own 3 in the fourth quarter. Ashton Levells-Mitchell grabbed the third with 3:49 left. Kamaurri McKinley had a sack and six tackles. Temple never found the end zone and managed three field goals.

Now, a fair-minded pirate admits a few leaks in the hull. Mitch Griffis threw for only 130 yards, and he threw an interception that gave Temple life late. We also came up empty on a fourth-down try in the red zone in the first half. But we converted a late fourth-and-one to run out the clock, and the Owls never saw the ball again.

We're 4-4 and 2-2 in the American, back at .500 and climbing. South Florida comes to Dowdy-Ficklen on Friday, Nov. 6, at 7:30 PM ET. Bring the tricorns. Hoist the colors, Pirate Nation.

articles.title: Temple vs East Carolina: Owls Grind but Fall 17-9 in Greenville
articles.matchup: Final: East Carolina (4-4) 17, Temple (2-6) 9, Sat., Oct. 31, Dowdy-Ficklen Stadium, Greenville. Next: at Navy, Sat., Nov. 7, 3:30 PM ET, Navy-Marine Corps Memorial Stadium, Annapolis
articles.text:
East Carolina 17, Temple 9. On Halloween night back on North Broad, Temple Theaters ran Alice by Heart at the Randall Theater on 13th Street, a story about kids pushing through the London Blitz on grit and imagination. Down in Greenville, our Owls spent the afternoon doing the same thing on a football field. Grit we had. Finishing we didn't.

Real talk from the gym floor: the defense did its reps. ECU went 77 yards on 13 plays for a 1-yard score late in the first quarter, and after that the Owls dug in. We stuffed a fourth-down try in the red zone in the first half, stopped a fake punt in the third, and held the Pirates to 4 of 12 on third down. Curly Ordonez made 14 tackles. Jayvant Brown and Saboor Karriem each made nine.

Carl Hardin carried the scoreboard by himself. He hit from 41 before halftime, from 46 late in the third and from 41 again with 10:12 left, a career-high three field goals. That cut a 17-3 hole to 17-9, one possession. That's Temple Made: you get knocked down, you get back on the bar.

Then came the part that keeps me up at night. Right after the fake punt stop, an interception on the next snap gave it right back. Late in the fourth, Karriem gave us a lifeline with his first career interception at our 21. Two snaps later, we threw another one. Three interceptions in all. You can't leave three reps on the floor and expect to win.

Ajani Sheppard ran for 69 yards on 15 carries and threw for 118. Keveun Mason added 51 on eight carries, and Temple has now run for 100-plus yards in all eight games. JoJo Bermudez caught three balls for 48 yards and broke a 33-yard punt return.

We're 2-6 and 1-3 in the American. Navy is next, on the road Saturday, Nov. 7, at 3:30 PM ET at Navy-Marine Corps Memorial Stadium in Annapolis. Chalk up, Owls. Temple Made.

articles.title: Colorado vs Kansas State: Buffs Win Halloween OT Thriller 27-24
articles.matchup: Final (OT): Colorado (3-5) 27, Kansas State (4-4) 24, Sat., Oct. 31, Folsom Field, Boulder. Next: at Arizona State, Sat., Nov. 7, Mountain America Stadium, Tempe
articles.text:
Colorado 27, Kansas State 24 in overtime, and the five-game skid is dead. Down on Pearl Street, Halloween meant Munchkin Masquerade, kids 12 and under in costume working downtown shops from 3 to 6. Up at Folsom Field, the Buffs handed out the best treat in Boulder: our first Big 12 win of the year.

Richard Young was the engine. He scored from 2 in the first quarter, his first touchdown as a Buff, and finished with 120 yards on 24 carries. JaQuail Smith ripped off a 47-yard touchdown run in the third, and our ground game piled up 222 yards and three scores.

The best drive started late in the third. Pinned at our own 4, we went 96 yards in 10 plays. Isaac Wilson hit Joseph Williams for 38, and Young cut left and ran 22 yards for the touchdown. 21-14 with 12:27 left. K-State then drove deep and missed a 43-yard field goal at 6:52.

Then the gut punch. Blake Barnett went 62 yards in 53 seconds, and his 8-yard throw to Garrett Oakley with six seconds left tied it 21-21. I stared at the Flatirons and did some quiet math on entropy.

Overtime flipped it back. K-State got to our 7, and Cree Thomas and Boo Carter broke up back-to-back throws in the end zone to force a 25-yard field goal. We took the ball, Young ran for 9 and 4, and on third down Wilson found Charlie Williams from 11 yards out. Ralphie's running, folks.

Wilson finished 14 of 21 for 185 yards with the winner, and Williams caught five balls for 89. Gideon Lampron was everywhere with 15 tackles, two sacks and four tackles for loss. Yamil Talib added two more sacks, and Damon Greaves pinned three punts inside the 20. We did cough one up when DeKalon Taylor fumbled through the end zone at the end of a 30-yard run in the second quarter, and that was our only turnover all day.

I celebrated the only way a physicist from Boulder knows how: a cold kombucha in the hammock and one very loud yell.

We're 3-5 and 1-4 in the Big 12. Next is Arizona State at Mountain America Stadium in Tempe on Saturday, Nov. 7. Sko Buffs.

articles.title: Kansas State vs Colorado: Wildcats Fall in OT, 27-24
articles.matchup: Final (OT): Colorado (3-5) 27, Kansas State (4-4) 24, Sat., Oct. 31, Folsom Field, Boulder. Next: vs. Oklahoma State, Sat., Nov. 7, Bill Snyder Family Stadium, Manhattan
articles.text:
Colorado 27, Kansas State 24 in overtime, and I'm going to need a minute. Back in Manhattan, Midwest Dream Car Collection on Anderson Avenue threw Haunted Horsepower on Halloween afternoon, free trick-or-treating among more than 65 cars. Our Wildcats brought plenty of horsepower to Folsom Field too. We just ran out of road one possession short.

The early going was a dry spell. Our first three drives went three-and-out, Blake Barnett took over late in the first quarter, and Luis Rodriguez missed from 49. Colorado led 7-0 until Barnett went 80 yards in 11 plays and found Josh Manning for a 28-yard touchdown with 2:25 left in the half.

From there it was haymakers. JaQuail Smith ran 47 yards for a Colorado score, and Barnett answered with a four-play drive capped by a 33-yard strike to Linkon Cure. Colorado went 96 yards and Richard Young scored from 22. We marched 12 plays into Colorado territory, took a delay penalty, and Rodriguez missed from 43 with 6:52 left.

Then came the drive I'll be telling the grandkids about. Down seven, ball at our 38, 55 seconds left. Barnett hit Manning for 23, Manning again for 5, and Jaron Tibbs for 31 down to the 3. A spike, a delay flag back to the 8, and with six seconds left Barnett found Garrett Oakley in the end zone. Review upheld it. 21-21. You can't rush a harvest, but that one came in at 53 seconds flat.

Overtime gave us the ball first. We got to the 7, two throws got broken up in the end zone, and Rodriguez hit from 25. Colorado needed five plays, and Isaac Wilson found Charlie Williams from 11 on third down. Game over.

Honest numbers: Barnett went 18 of 28 for 224 yards and three touchdowns with no turnovers. Rodney Fields Jr. ran 12 times for 65, Logan Bartley made nine tackles, and Simon McClannan averaged 53.7 yards on six punts. But Colorado ran for 222 yards, and two missed field goals left points on the turf.

I named that final drive the Winter Wheat, because it got planted late and came up anyway. Shame the season's first frost hit in overtime.

We're 4-4, 1-4 in the Big 12 and 0-3 on the road. Oklahoma State comes to Bill Snyder Family Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 7, and the Wabash Cannonball better be loud. Go Cats.

articles.title: Utah State vs Colorado State: Hillstead Leads Aggies 31-14
articles.matchup: Final: Utah State (3-5) 31, Colorado State (3-5) 14, Sat., Oct. 31, Maverik Stadium, Logan. Next: vs. Fresno State, Sat., Nov. 7, Maverik Stadium, Logan
articles.text:
Utah State 31, Colorado State 14, and the Aggies led 24-0 before the Rams found the end zone in Logan. Friday night the Taggart Student Center and Fieldhouse hosted the annual Howl, the USU Halloween bash with a live haunted house, laser tag, karaoke and a dance floor that sold out. Saturday the haunted house moved to Maverik Stadium, and Colorado State got lost in it.

McCae Hillstead got his first start since the season opener, and he played like a man who had been waiting all fall for the keys. He was 17 of 22 for 173 yards and a touchdown, and he ran 11 times for 79 yards and another score. Anthony Garcia was his go-to target: 11 catches for 121 yards. Then Garcia threw a 44-yard throwback right back to Hillstead, and a few snaps later Hillstead ran in from 18 yards. I have milked cows at 4 a.m. for 20 years, and I have never seen a better play in Cache Valley.

Nehemiah Washington broke a 31-yard touchdown run on the opening drive. Kian Afrookhteh made a 25-yard field goal. Javen Jacobs scored from 12 yards in the third, and Hillstead hit Kaina Watson for a 7-yard touchdown in the fourth. Utah State ran for 247 yards and had zero turnovers.

The defense was the real story. David Kabongo strip-sacked Hauss Hejny at our 30 in the third quarter, and Carson Tujague fell on it. Early in the fourth, Tevita Tuha punched the ball loose from Durell Robinson and James Jennette recovered at our 29. Kabongo made seven tackles with two tackles for loss, and Tujague also got a sack. Colorado State finished with 263 yards.

The honest note: the Rams scored 14 points late, and Afrookhteh missed one field goal. That is cleanup work, not a crisis.

We are 3-5 and 2-2 in conference play, and that makes three wins at Maverik Stadium. Fresno State comes to Logan on Saturday, Nov. 7. I am buying a double scoop of Aggie Ice Cream tonight, and I am not sharing.

articles.title: Colorado State vs Utah State: Rams Fall Behind Early 31-14
articles.matchup: Final: Utah State (3-5) 31, Colorado State (3-5) 14, Sat., Oct. 31, Maverik Stadium, Logan. Next: vs. Boise State, Sat., Nov. 7, Canvas Stadium, Fort Collins
articles.text:
Utah State 31, Colorado State 14, and we were down 24-0 before we scored a point. On Friday morning, costumed preschoolers in Fort Collins trick-or-treated through Old Town Square for Tiny Tot Halloween, collecting candy from nearly 100 downtown businesses. Those little ones moved through more ground before lunch than our offense did in the first half in Logan.

I run the foothills trails every morning, and I know what it feels like when the climb beats you. This was that. Utah State opened with a six-play, 75-yard drive and a 31-yard touchdown run by Nehemiah Washington. Kian Afrookhteh added a field goal. Then the Aggies ran a throwback trick play, Anthony Garcia hitting McCae Hillstead for 44 yards, and a few snaps later Hillstead ran in an 18-yard score. It was 17-0 at halftime, and we had nothing on the board.

Hillstead, making his first start since the season opener, carved us up: 17 of 22 for 173 yards and a touchdown, plus 79 rushing yards. Garcia caught 11 balls for 121 yards. Utah State ran for 247 yards and held the ball for 36:08.

The fight showed up late, I will give the boys that. Durell Robinson ran in a 6-yard touchdown at the end of the third quarter, and Hauss Hejny hit Cedric Ross for a 21-yard score and then hit the two-point try with 2:31 left. But we fumbled twice in Aggie territory. Hejny got stripped on a sack at the Utah State 30, and Robinson coughed it up at the 29 in the fourth. Those are points left on the mountain.

Hejny finished 19 of 30 for 186 yards. Terrence Smith Jr. and RJ Vick each caught five balls, and Jayden Fox returned five kickoffs for 126 yards. Oumar Diomande made nine tackles, and Tre'Shawn Moore and Robby Harrison each made eight. Nathan Sutcliffe averaged 45 yards a punt.

We are 3-5 and 1-3 in conference play. Boise State comes to Canvas Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 7, and that is a home climb we have to make. Lace up, Rams. Ram tough.

articles.title: Old Dominion vs Marshall: Homecoming Spoiled in 36-23 Loss
articles.matchup: Final: Marshall (5-3) 36, Old Dominion (2-7) 23, Sat., Oct. 31, S.B. Ballard Stadium, Norfolk. Next: at Coastal Carolina, Sat., Nov. 7, 1:00 PM ET, Brooks Stadium, Conway
articles.text:
Marshall 36, Old Dominion 23, and the royal court has to report a Homecoming gone wrong. It was Halloween in Norfolk, and the palace rules at S.B. Ballard Stadium were clear: costumes welcome, face paint welcome, masks and toy weapons banned. The Monarchs came dressed for a party. Marshall came dressed as a wrecking crew.

The opening ceremony collapsed on the second snap. Jaxon Potter was stripped, Marshall recovered at our 26, and four plays later it was 7-0. A 49-yard run made it 14-0. Maurki James restored some dignity with a 6-yard touchdown run, and Andrew Nelms hit a 21-yard field goal to make it 17-10.

Then came the moment that will stay in the court records. With four seconds left in the half, we tried a field goal, and Marshall returned it 100 yards for a touchdown. 27-10 at the break. A crown dropped on the ballroom floor.

Brandon Crutchfield answered for the crown early in the third. He intercepted Marshall at its own 44 and took it 44 yards to the end zone, and it was 27-17. Jackson Forrest led the defense with 12 tackles, and Lucas Struck added nine. Mario Thompson, Ahmaad Foster and Malachi Harris each recorded a sack, and the defense held Marshall to 2 of 14 on third down and 142 passing yards. But the Herd kept kicking. Their kicker made five field goals, and our offense threw three interceptions and turned it over on downs twice.

Potter threw for 329 yards on 23 of 44, and Josh Rodriguez was the brightest jewel in the crown with nine catches for 143 yards. Kendall Harris added four for 79. James punched in a 14-yard score late for his second touchdown of the day.

We're 2-7 and 1-5 in the Sun Belt. The court travels to Coastal Carolina on Saturday, Nov. 7, at 1:00 PM ET at Brooks Stadium. Long live the Monarchs.

articles.title: Marshall vs Old Dominion: Herd Ruin ODU Homecoming 36-23
articles.matchup: Final: Marshall (5-3) 36, Old Dominion (2-7) 23, Sat., Oct. 31, S.B. Ballard Stadium, Norfolk. Next: at Georgia Southern, Sat., Nov. 7, 3:30 PM ET, Allen E. Paulson Stadium, Statesboro
articles.text:
Marshall 36, Old Dominion 23, and we crashed somebody else's Homecoming on Halloween. Back in Huntington, Healing Halloween ran free kids activities from 4 p.m. and a recovery fundraiser on Vernon Street that night. As a nurse, I call that real medicine for a town that knows hard times. Down in Norfolk, the Herd was handing out its own treatment. We Are.

Triage came fast. On the second snap of the game, Kenyatta Hardge knocked the ball loose, and Cannon Lewis recovered at the ODU 26. Four plays later, TJ Lester scored from 4 yards. Then Lester burst 49 yards off the left side, and it was 14-0 before the Monarchs had a pulse. Hardge finished with seven tackles and two sacks.

Now the part I'll be telling every patient on my floor this week. With four seconds left in the half, ODU lined up for a field goal, and Xayvion Turner-Bradshaw took it back 100 yards for a touchdown. It was the first return of a field goal try in Marshall history and only the fifth 100-yard score ever by the Herd. That made it 27-10 at halftime instead of a one-score game.

Jorge Diaz Nicolas made the record book on his own. He hit field goals from 35, 30, 34, 30 and 24 yards and became the first Marshall player ever with five in a game. Judah Price led a 196-yard ground game with 82 yards, and Lester added 76 and two scores.

The defense took four turnovers. Charles McCartherens intercepted one in the end zone and tipped another that Caleb Clark-Glover caught. Daytione Smith added a fourth-quarter interception. Brayden Hall made 11 tackles. I'll be honest on the chart: we threw only 8 of 18 for 142 yards, gave up an interception return for a score and drew 12 penalties for 94 yards. That needs treatment before Statesboro.

We're 5-3 and 2-2 in the Sun Belt, and 11-1 all-time against Old Dominion. Next is Georgia Southern on the road, Saturday, Nov. 7, at 3:30 PM ET at Allen E. Paulson Stadium. Scrub in. We Are Marshall.

articles.title: Western Michigan vs Bowling Green: Broncos Win Senior Day 23-10
articles.matchup: Final: Western Michigan (6-3) 23, Bowling Green (2-7) 10, Sat., Oct. 31, Stafford-Smith Field at Waldo Stadium, Kalamazoo. Next: at Akron, Tue., Nov. 10, InfoCision Stadium, Akron
articles.text:
Western Michigan 23, Bowling Green 10, and Senior Day ended the right way. Before kickoff at Stafford-Smith Field at Waldo Stadium, 18 seniors were honored, and then the Broncos played their 12th Halloween game in program history and finally beat a Bowling Green team that had won the last three meetings. Order the full stack. We earned it.

Bowling Green scored first on a 7-yard touchdown. Fine. Cole Cabana answered about four minutes later, 82 yards straight through the Falcons and into the end zone. He finished with 110 yards on just seven carries. In the second quarter Broc Lowry found Ryan Brotherton from 6 yards out. Bowling Green kicked a 48-yarder at the horn, and we went in up 14-10.

The second half belonged to the defense and the kicking game. Three interceptions, by Daeh McCullough, Amarian Louis and Justyce Betts. Coming in, the whole defense had four all season. Our kicker went 3 for 3 from 32, 50 and 46 yards, the last one with 15 seconds left. Bowling Green did not score after halftime. Joey Pope had two tackles for loss.

Aveion Chenault caught five balls for 109 yards, topping the career-high 105 he posted the week before. Jalen Buckley, one of the seniors honored before the game, carried 24 times for 77 tough yards. Ryan Millmore punted five times for a 51.4 average and pinned three inside the 20.

Now the honest part, because syrup doesn't hide a burnt pancake. We lost two fumbles. Lowry went 9 of 18 for 146 yards with a touchdown. We went 4-14 on third down, and Bowling Green held the ball for 32:18. A short stack of offense won't hold up every week.

We are 6-3 and 4-1 in the MAC. Next is Akron at InfoCision Stadium on Tuesday, Nov. 10, at 7 PM ET. Pour it on, Broncos. Row the boat.

articles.title: Bowling Green vs Western Michigan: Turnovers Sink Falcons 23-10
articles.matchup: Final: Western Michigan (6-3) 23, Bowling Green (2-7) 10, Sat., Oct. 31, Stafford-Smith Field at Waldo Stadium, Kalamazoo. Next: vs. Kent State, Tue., Nov. 10, Doyt L. Perry Stadium, Bowling Green
articles.text:
Western Michigan 23, Bowling Green 10. The Falcons were finished in Kalamazoo by midafternoon, hours before porch lights came on across Bowling Green for citywide trick-or-treat from 6:30 to 8 p.m. Every porch in town handed out more than our offense did after halftime.

We started like a team that came to win. Jay Kastantin found Kentrell White for a 7-yard touchdown and a 7-0 lead. Then Cole Cabana went 82 yards on one carry and the building woke up. Broc Lowry hit Ryan Brotherton from 6 yards out, and Travis Kenner banged a 48-yard field goal as the half ended. Down 14-10. Very much alive.

Then we went to the penalty box and never came out. Zero points in the second half. Three interceptions, two from Kastantin and one on a Brennan Ridley throw. I play goal on the club team. When the guys in front of you keep giving the puck away, the goalie can only stop so much, and our defense stopped a lot.

Look at what the defense did. Dorian Pringle made 12 tackles with a sack. Kade Kostus and Andrew Hines III each fell on a Western Michigan fumble. We held the ball for 32:18. The Broncos went 4-14 on third down and threw for 146 yards. Their kicker went 3 for 3, including a 50-yarder, and that's what kept pulling the game away.

The offense has to own this one. Kastantin went 20 of 31 for 149 yards, a touchdown and two interceptions. That is not how you win on the road in the MAC. Nakai Amachree ran 11 times for 61 yards. We went 7-16 on third down and came up empty on our one fourth-down try. Kenner missed one field goal. Isaiah Dawson gave us field position on returns, 78 yards on five tries, and we wasted it.

Four straight losses now. We are 2-7 and 2-3 in the MAC.

Kent State comes to Doyt L. Perry Stadium on Tuesday, Nov. 10, at 7 PM ET. Home ice, weeknight, no excuses. Clear the crease and let's go, Falcons.

articles.title: Air Force vs UConn: Hodges Runs for 4 Scores 35-26
articles.matchup: Final: Air Force (6-2) 35, UConn (4-4) 26, Sat., Oct. 31, Falcon Stadium, Colorado Springs. Next: at Army, Sat., Nov. 7, Michie Stadium, West Point
articles.text:
Air Force 35, UConn 26, and the Falcons did not complete a single throw. Did not need one. It was Space Force Day at Falcon Stadium, a Black Out with the team in its Space Force uniforms to honor the USSF, and the Falcons flew one ground mission after another: 74 carries, 366 rushing yards, five rushing touchdowns.

Call sign for today: Kemper Hodges, Workhorse. Thirty-five carries, 200 yards, four touchdowns. He scored from 7 yards and then broke a 62-yarder in the first quarter, punched in a 3-yarder in the second, and closed the show from a yard out with 3:09 left. Owen Allen added 70 yards on 18 carries, and Gage LaDue scored from 4 yards in the third quarter.

I logged a lot of hours as an instructor pilot, and I know a long sortie when I see one. UConn cut it to 28-26 on Kenji Christian's 46-yard run on the first play of the fourth quarter. Then our offense took the ball for 19 plays, 75 yards and 11:37 of clock. That is a full mission profile, briefed, flown and debriefed, while UConn's offense sat and watched. Air Force held the ball for 41:49 and went 5 for 6 on fourth down.

The defense earned its wings at the end. After Hodges' last score, UConn threw on every snap. Blake Fletcher and Roger Jones Jr. broke up throws, the Huskies turned it over on downs, and Isaac Hubert and Jake Kepler shared a sack on the final snap. Max Mustell led the team with eight tackles, and Fletcher and Hubert each got a sack.

Honest debrief: Kalieb Osborne hit us for 263 yards and two long scoring strikes, and the defense has to clean that up. Will Duncan also averaged 56.3 yards on three punts. That is altitude.

Air Force is 6-2 and bowl eligible for the first time since 2023. Next we go to West Point to face Army at Michie Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 7. Fly, fight, win.

articles.title: UConn vs Air Force: Huskies Ground Down by Falcons 35-26
articles.matchup: Final: Air Force (6-2) 35, UConn (4-4) 26, Sat., Oct. 31, Falcon Stadium, Colorado Springs. Next: vs. North Carolina, Sat., Nov. 7, Pratt & Whitney Stadium at Rentschler Field, East Hartford
articles.text:
Air Force 35, UConn 26, and the Falcons ran the ball 74 times to get it done. Back in Storrs, WHUS Radio was throwing its Mischief After Dark Halloween concert in the Student Union Ballroom, with Ovlov and Whisper Doll on stage and a costume contest. The real mischief happened at 7,000 feet, and we were on the wrong end of it.

I count possessions. I am a point guard, it is what we do. Air Force held the ball for 41:49. We had it for 18:06. You do not win a game where the other team gets the ball for more than two-thirds of the clock, and that is the whole story.

Kemper Hodges ran 35 times for 200 yards and four touchdowns, including a 62-yarder in the first quarter. We were down 14-0 before we touched the end zone. Then this offense showed real fight. Trey Cornist scored from a yard out, Kalieb Osborne hit Ryder Treadway for a 2-yard score before the half, and Osborne found Alex Godavitarne for a 55-yard touchdown in the third. Kenji Christian broke a 46-yard touchdown run on the first play of the fourth quarter, and we were down 28-26.

That is where it slipped away. The extra point after Godavitarne's touchdown failed, and the two-point try after Christian's run failed too. Then Air Force took the ball and went 19 plays and 75 yards over 11:37. Nineteen plays. The Falcons went 5 for 6 on fourth down, and Hodges finished the drive from a yard out with 3:09 left. We got one more shot, and it died on a fourth-down incompletion.

articles.title: South Florida vs UAB: Hicks Sacks Four, Bulls Roll 30-10
articles.matchup: Final: South Florida (6-2) 30, UAB (4-4) 10, Sat., Oct. 31, Raymond James Stadium, Tampa. Next: at East Carolina, Fri., Nov. 6, Dowdy-Ficklen Stadium, Greenville
articles.text:
South Florida 30, UAB 10, on Halloween at Raymond James Stadium. Busch Gardens was running the final weekend of Howl-O-Scream, haunted houses and scare zones and all, but the scariest act in Tampa was C.J. Hicks, who sacked Ryder Burton four times and tied a USF record.

It did not start pretty. UAB went 67 yards for a touchdown on the opening drive, kicked a field goal on its next trip, and we were down 10-0 in the first quarter. Our first drive went backward, and our second died when a fourth-and-1 throw fell incomplete.

Then Michael Van Buren Jr. left the game hurt, Luke Kromenhoek came in, and the whole stadium woke up. On first-and-19 he broke tackles for 42 yards to set up a 31-yard Nico Gramatica field goal. Next drive he ran for 25 to the UAB 10, and Jason Collins Jr. scored from 6 to tie it with 47 seconds left. On UAB's very next snap, Hicks blasted Burton, the ball came out, and Asani Redwood scooped it and scored from 6. Fourteen points in 10 seconds. 17-10 at the half.

The second half belonged to the defense. UAB had seven drives and scored on none of them. Early in the fourth, on third-and-10, Hicks did it again, and Grayson Howard scooped the loose ball and went 13 yards for the score. Howard finished with eight tackles and two sacks. Gramatica added kicks from 30 and 33 and went 3 for 3.

The numbers look like a pirate raid. We outrushed UAB 191 to 17, piled up six sacks and 11 tackles for loss, and did not turn it over for the fourth straight game. Kromenhoek ran 15 times for a career-best 92 yards, and D.J. Crowther added 60 on 16 carries.

I wore the full Gasparilla getup to the stadium, eyepatch and all, and it stays on until Greenville.

We're 6-2, 2-2 in the American and bowl eligible for the fourth straight season. Next up is East Carolina on Friday, Nov. 6, at Dowdy-Ficklen Stadium in Greenville, N.C., with a 7:30 p.m. kickoff. Go Bulls.

articles.title: UAB vs South Florida: Blazers Go Cold in Tampa, Fall 30-10
articles.matchup: Final: South Florida (6-2) 30, UAB (4-4) 10, Sat., Oct. 31, Raymond James Stadium, Tampa. Next: vs. Charlotte, Sat., Nov. 7, Protective Stadium, Birmingham
articles.text:
South Florida 30, UAB 10, and it stings worse because we were up 10-0. Back home on Friday night, Sloss Furnaces opened the Historic No. 2 Casting Shed for Bowl Night: Molten & Mysterious, a cast iron bowl class plus a night tour of the old blast furnace. Iron goes in hot and comes out hard. Our Blazers went in hot at Raymond James Stadium and cooled off way too fast.

The start was pure Birmingham. We took the opening kickoff and went 67 yards in seven plays, with Ryder Burton hitting CJ Smith for 41 yards to the USF 3 and Rod Robinson II running it in from 5. Next time out we reached the USF 8, and Jonah Delange kicked a 30-yard field goal. 10-0 in the first quarter.

Then Delange missed from 41 early in the second, USF lost its starting quarterback to injury, and Luke Kromenhoek came in and flipped the afternoon. He broke tackles for 42 yards to set up a field goal, then ran for 25 more to set up Jason Collins Jr.'s 6-yard touchdown. 10-10 with 47 seconds left. On our very next snap, C.J. Hicks sacked Burton at our 17, the ball came out, and Asani Redwood scooped it and scored. Fourteen points in 10 seconds. 17-10 at the half.

It happened again early in the fourth. Hicks hit Burton on third-and-10 at our 19, the ball popped loose, and Grayson Howard took it 13 yards for a touchdown. Hicks finished with four sacks, tying a South Florida record. Burton went down six times and ended the day with minus-37 rushing yards.

Honest numbers: 33 carries for 17 yards, 4 of 16 on third down, 10 first downs, 177 yards of offense. After those first two drives we never scored again. A 16-play, 61-yard march in the fourth ended with Delange missing from 32. Burton finished 13 of 27 for 149.

The defense deserved a better ending. Jeremiah Jordan and Jo'Tavion Pierce made 11 tackles apiece, Marlin Dean had 2.5 sacks, and USF threw for just 46 yards all day. Oliver Straw boomed four punts at 49.8 yards a pop.

My granddaddy spent his working life around Birmingham steel, and he had one rule for a bad shift: you clock back in. Forged, not given.

We're 4-4, 2-2 in the American and 0-4 on the road. Charlotte comes to Protective Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 7, and Blaze better be breathing fire. Go Blazers.

articles.title: Maryland vs Illinois: Terps Fall 20-17 on Final-Play Kick
articles.matchup: Final: Illinois (5-3) 20, Maryland (2-6) 17, Sat., Oct. 31, SECU Stadium, College Park. Next: at Purdue, Sat., Nov. 7, 12:30 PM ET, Ross-Ade Stadium, West Lafayette
articles.text:
Illinois 20, Maryland 17, and it ended on a kick with no time left. SECU Stadium hosted a home game on Halloween for the first time since 1992, and the Terps came out in red helmets, black jerseys and black pants, a look not worn since Nov. 9, 1991, at Baltimore Memorial Stadium. Back in black, back in it, and still on the wrong end. That one stings like a crab pinch.

This was the first game under interim head coach Aazaar Abdul-Rahim, and the effort was real. Messiah Delhomme intercepted Illinois on the opening drive, his fourth career interception, and set us up at the Illinois 12. We gave it back with a fumble at the 1. Then Malik Washington ran 21 yards to get us back in the red zone and scored on an 8-yard keeper. Maryland 7-0.

Illinois tied it before halftime. Our offense opened the third quarter with a seven-play, 65-yard drive. Washington went 5 for 5 for 44 yards on it, and DeJuan Williams ran in from 17. 14-7 Terps. Illinois answered with a 45-yard field goal, and then Javari Barnett broke a 64-yard touchdown run on the first snap of the fourth.

Sean O'Haire answered with a season-long 46-yard field goal to tie it 17-17 with 10:16 left. That was his 30th field goal as a Terp. Then Illinois took the ball at its own 26 with 5:45 left, ran 13 plays for 67 yards, drained every second and kicked a 26-yarder on the final play.

Lavain Scruggs led the defense with 10 tackles. Chris Durr Jr. caught six balls for 58 yards. Washington threw for 190 yards and ran for a score. We drew one penalty all day for five yards, our fewest since 2022. That's clean, disciplined football. A student also won a free semester of tuition on the field in the fourth quarter, so somebody in College Park left a winner.

We're 2-6 and 0-5 in the Big Ten. Purdue is next on the road, Saturday, Nov. 7, at 12:30 PM ET in Ross-Ade Stadium. Pack the Old Bay. Fear the Turtle.

articles.title: Illinois vs Maryland: Moczulski Walk-Off Kick Wins It 20-17
articles.matchup: Final: Illinois (5-3) 20, Maryland (2-6) 17, Sat., Oct. 31, SECU Stadium, College Park. Next: vs. Nebraska, Fri., Nov. 6, 8:00 PM ET, Gies Memorial Stadium, Champaign
articles.text:
Illinois 20, Maryland 17, and Ethan Moczulski made the bell ring with zero on the clock. Back home, Krannert Center had Sinfonia da Camera's Halloween concert, Spellbound, booked for 7:30 that night, with Night on Bald Mountain to close it. Our Fighting Illini wrote their own spooky finish in College Park hours earlier. Oskee-wow-wow.

Get out your notebooks, class, because the first quarter was a pop quiz we nearly failed. Katin Houser threw an interception on our opening drive, and Maryland started at our 12. James Kreutz answered by forcing a fumble at the 1, and Tanner Heckel later intercepted one in the red zone. Two takeaways inside our 20 kept the score at 7-0. Houser came back from a one-game absence, and Brayden Trimble caught his first career touchdown from 16 yards with 27 seconds left in the half. 7-7.

Maryland went back in front in the third, Moczulski hit from 45, and then came the chalkboard moment. On the first snap of the fourth quarter, freshman Javari Barnett busted a 64-yard touchdown run. It was his career long, and he finished with 80 yards on six carries. Illinois 17-14.

Maryland tied it with a field goal at 10:16. Then the lesson plan. We took over at our own 26 with 5:45 left and went 13 plays and 67 yards. We converted on third down near midfield, and Collin Dixon made a 15-yard grab. Jordan Anderson carried four straight times into the red zone and took a knee inside the 5 to set up the kick. Moczulski's 26-yarder went through as time expired. Grade for the whole class: A.

Dixon finished with six catches for 103 yards, his fourth 100-yard game this season. Houser threw for 223 yards and a touchdown. The defense held Maryland to three points and 99 yards over the final 26:10. That is the stat on my classroom wall this week.

That's three straight wins, and we're 5-3 and 3-2 in the Big Ten, one win from a bowl. Nebraska comes to Gies Memorial Stadium on Friday night, Nov. 6, at 8:00 PM ET for the Hail to the Blue Out. Wear blue. Oskee-wow-wow.

articles.title: Rutgers vs Michigan: Knights Rally, Fall Late at SHI 28-21
articles.matchup: Final: Michigan (5-3) 28, Rutgers (2-6) 21, Sat., Oct. 31, SHI Stadium, Piscataway. Next: at Wisconsin, Sat., Nov. 7, Camp Randall Stadium, Madison
articles.text:
Michigan 28, Rutgers 21, and it hurts because we had them tied with 11:43 to play. Halloween On the Banks turned the Rutgers Boardwalk into a trick-or-treat route, with a costume contest, a mechanical pumpkin and a haunted halftime show from the Marching Scarlet Knights. The scary part came after halftime.

Listen to me. For three quarters this team looked like it wanted a fight with a big Michigan program, and I loved every minute. Dane Pizzaro hit from 46 yards to get us on the board. Then AJ Surace launched one deep to Jourdin Houston, and Houston was gone for an 80-yard touchdown, the first of his career. Pizzaro added a 32-yarder before the half, and we trailed only 14-13. Down here we invented college football, and that throw looked like a first edition.

Michigan went up 21-13 in the third. Then the break we needed came early in the fourth. A kick-catch interference flag on Michigan gave us the ball back at our 37, and three snaps later Antwan Raymond ripped off a 54-yard run to the 3. Clay Thevenin ran it in from a yard out, Surace found Ben Black III for the two-point try, and it was 21-21. I bought a six-foot sub on the spot to celebrate. Big mistake.

Michigan took over at its own 2 and ground out 11 plays and 75 yards over 7:19, finishing with Tommy Carr's 9-yard run at 4:24. We got the ball back and went three-and-out. That was the ballgame.

The honest box score: we had nine first downs and 249 yards, and Surace completed three of 12 throws, even if those three went for 123 yards. Michigan converted 12 of 16 third downs and held the ball for 39:06. Our defense was out there forever. JJ Conyers and Moses Walker each made nine tackles, Devonte Anderson and Sean Allison made eight apiece, and Sekou Kromah got a sack. Raymond finished with 85 yards on 11 carries.

We are 2-6 and 1-4 in the Big Ten, and nobody on the Turnpike is hiding that. Next week we go to Wisconsin at Camp Randall Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 7. Bring that fourth-quarter fight for all four quarters, Scarlet Knights. The sub can wait.

articles.title: Michigan vs Rutgers: Carr Runs in Late Winner 28-21
articles.matchup: Final: Michigan (5-3) 28, Rutgers (2-6) 21, Sat., Oct. 31, SHI Stadium, Piscataway. Next: vs. Michigan State, Sat., Nov. 7, Michigan Stadium, Ann Arbor
articles.text:
Michigan 28, Rutgers 21, and Tommy Carr played the whole song on Halloween in Piscataway. Back in Ann Arbor, the University Symphony and Philharmonia Orchestras packed Hill Auditorium for the annual Halloween Concert, with Danse Macabre and the William Tell Overture on the program. Carr gave us our own overture, and he finished it with the trumpets blaring.

articles.title: NC State vs California: Pack Heat Up After Half, Win 31-10
articles.matchup: Final: NC State (4-4) 31, California (3-6) 10, Sat., Oct. 31, Carter-Finley Stadium, Raleigh. Next: vs. Duke, Sat., Nov. 7, Carter-Finley Stadium, Raleigh
articles.text:
NC State 31, California 10. Homecoming closed out Red & White Week at Carter-Finley Stadium, Todd Goebbel coached his first game as interim head coach, and the Pack put a second-half shutout on the Golden Bears in front of 52,933. Good day to come home to Raleigh.

The start ran hot. CJ Bailey found Deandre Desinor for a 49-yard touchdown on the fourth snap of the game. Kanoah Vinesett added a 43-yard field goal. Then the burners went cold. Bailey lost an exchange at our 19 and Cal kicked a 38-yarder as the half ended. Ten all at halftime, with the grill thermometer stuck on warm.

Second half, full heat. Three straight drives, three touchdowns. Bailey hit Chance Robinson for 38 yards. Darius Johnson punched in a 2-yard run for his first career touchdown. Davion Gause scored from 6 after a long Victor Snow catch. Gause finished with 19 carries for 104 yards, his first 100-yard game since his first college game at UNC. The last two quarters went 21-0, Pack.

The defense was the real fire. Popo Aguirre made 16 tackles with two for loss. Michael Tate made seven. Ziggy Moore and Josh Warren Jr. each got a sack, and Chase Bond and Isaiah Shirley split one. Moore also dropped a Cal receiver short on a fourth-down try in the fourth quarter. Jaren Sensabaugh grabbed an interception late. Cal finished 5-18 on third down and ran for 73 yards all day.

Honest part. Bailey went 13 of 25 for 192 yards and two touchdowns, with that one lost fumble. We ran for 135 yards on 40 carries, and the first half was too slow. A brisket doesn't care how good the bark looks at noon. It's done when it's done, and this one was done by the fourth quarter. Awoooo.

We are 4-4 and 2-3 in the ACC, and we have now won both meetings ever with Cal. Duke comes to Carter-Finley Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 7, at 12:30 PM ET for Military Appreciation Day. Keep the heat on. Go Pack.

articles.title: California vs NC State: Bears Blanked After Half in 31-10 Loss
articles.matchup: Final: NC State (4-4) 31, California (3-6) 10, Sat., Oct. 31, Carter-Finley Stadium, Raleigh. Next: at Virginia, Sat., Nov. 14, Scott Stadium, Charlottesville
articles.text:
NC State 31, California 10, and the second half in Raleigh was a blank page. Back in Berkeley, the Fourth Street Halloween Festival ran from 3 to 5 p.m. with trick-or-treating at 80 merchant shops. Our kickoff was at 9 a.m. Pacific, so the Bears were done hours before the first kid in a costume hit Fourth Street. Some of those kids got more out of the day than we did.

The first half was a real argument. NC State scored on its fourth snap, a 49-yard catch-and-run by Deandre Desinor, and added a field goal. We answered. Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele hit Chase Hendricks for 30 yards and a touchdown with a grab worth framing. Solomon Williams fell on a fumbled exchange at the NC State 19, and we came away with nothing when a 40-yard kick drifted wide right. Towns McGough made up for it with a 38-yarder as time ran out. Ten all at the break. I had my sign ready: WE CAN WIN THIS.

Then the premise collapsed. NC State scored on its first three drives of the second half, and the final two quarters went 21-0. Per the Wolfpack's own count, we gained 121 yards after halftime and 11 of them on the ground. Chance Robinson caught a 38-yard touchdown, Darius Johnson scored from 2 and Davion Gause from 6. Gause finished with 104 yards on 19 carries.

The honest audit. Sagapolutele went 29 of 45 for 196 yards, a touchdown and an interception. We ran for 73 yards as a team. We were 5-18 on third down and 1 of 3 on fourth down, and one of those misses came in our own territory in the fourth quarter. Hendricks caught seven balls for 67 yards. Odera Okaka made 11 tackles and AJ Tuitele made nine. Angus Davies punted seven times for a 45.0 average, which says plenty about the afternoon.

A philosopher would call this a three-game losing streak with a decent first act. I call it unacceptable.

We are 3-6 and 2-4 in the ACC. There's a week off, then Virginia at Scott Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 14. Fix the second half. Go Bears.

articles.title: Oregon vs Northwestern: Ducks Rally From 20-6 Hole to Win 34-26
articles.matchup: Final: Oregon (5-3) 34, Northwestern (6-2) 26, Sat., Oct. 31, Autzen Stadium, Eugene. Next: at Ohio State, Sat., Nov. 7, 3:30 PM ET, Ohio Stadium, Columbus
articles.text:
Oregon 34, Northwestern 26. Halloween at Autzen Stadium for the first time since 2009, and the Ducks dressed for it: black helmets with white feathers for the first time ever, black jerseys with gray numbers and white pants. Uniform of the week gets a ten. For one half, the execution got about a four, and then it hit ten too.

Let me review the first half like a runway show where the shoes fell apart. Northwestern scored on its first four drives. Aidan Chiles hit Griffin Wilde for 64 yards, Chiles ran in a 5-yard bootleg, and we were down 20-6 in our own house on Halloween. Gage Hurych kept us alive with field goals from 27 and 44, and with 49 seconds left before the break, Dylan Raiola found Dakorien Moore for a 10-yard touchdown. 20-13. Breathe.

Moore lost a fumble on the first drive of the second half, and the Wildcats kicked it to 23-13. Then the new look finally fit. Raiola drove us 80 yards in seven plays and hit Jamari Johnson for 17 yards. The defense got a stop, Brandon Smith ripped off big runs, and on fourth-and-goal from the 2, Smith punched it in for our first lead, 27-23.

Northwestern kicked it to 27-26, and Moore answered on the very next snap. Raiola dropped it in, Moore cut back halfway there, and he went 75 yards to the end zone. Autzen lost its mind. Moore finished with seven catches for 128 yards and two touchdowns. Raiola went 22 of 31 for 336 yards and three scores with no interceptions. Evan Stewart and Jalen Lott each made big grabs downfield.

Defensive tailoring: Nasir Wyatt sacked Chiles to force a field goal, and D'Antre Robinson got him on third down late. We gave up 456 yards, so the seams need work, but the red zone stops were the difference. One penalty all day. Pressed and clean.

We're 5-3 and 3-2 in the Big Ten. Next comes the big runway: at Ohio State on Saturday, Nov. 7, at 3:30 PM ET in Ohio Stadium. Pack the good shoes. Go Ducks.

articles.title: Northwestern vs Oregon: Wildcats Blow 20-6 Lead, Fall 34-26
articles.matchup: Final: Oregon (5-3) 34, Northwestern (6-2) 26, Sat., Oct. 31, Autzen Stadium, Eugene. Next: vs. Iowa, Sat., Nov. 7, Ryan Field, Evanston
articles.text:
Oregon 34, Northwestern 26. Back in Evanston, New Ryan Field threw open its gates Saturday afternoon for a free Family Halloween Festival, with candy, costumes and the Northwestern Wildcats at Oregon on the big screen. Those kids watched us own Autzen Stadium for a half and then watched the Ducks take it back. Footnote: we were in control. Footnote to the footnote: control is not a final score.

On our first trip to Eugene, we scored on our first four drives. Aidan Chiles found Griffin Wilde behind the whole secondary for a 64-yard touchdown, Jackson Kleather hit from 37 twice, and Chiles kept it on a 5-yard bootleg for a 20-6 lead in the second quarter. Wilde finished with five catches for a season-high 146 yards. Chiles went 22 of 38 for 281 yards and ran 14 times for a career-high 93.

Here is the investigative finding, and I filed it with a heavy heart. We kept knocking on the door and kicking field goals. Raiola hit Dakorien Moore for 10 yards before halftime, and it was 20-13. Braydon Brus ripped the ball from Moore on the first drive of the third, Damon Walters fell on it, and we got only a 49-yard Kleather kick out of it. Then Oregon went 80 yards for one touchdown and 76 for another, and we trailed 27-23.

Kleather drilled another 49-yarder to make it 27-26. One snap later, Dylan Raiola hit Moore for 75 yards. Kleather's 42-yard try with 5:14 left missed, his only miss in five, and the Ducks closed it out. Oregon outscored us 21-6 after halftime.

The data on the defense is not all bad. Alijah Jones made eight tackles, and Brus, Montae Pate and Kobie McKinzie had six each. We had zero turnovers and held the ball for 35:54. But Raiola threw for 336 yards and three touchdowns, and that stat sits in the margin and hurts.

We're 6-2 and 3-2 in the Big Ten, and the correction desk opens Monday. Iowa comes to Ryan Field on Saturday, Nov. 7, and that game matters in the standings. Go 'Cats.

articles.title: Duke vs Boston College: Sheppard Scores Five in Rout 47-2
articles.matchup: Final: Duke (6-2) 47, Boston College (4-4) 2, Sat., Oct. 31, Wallace Wade Stadium, Durham. Next: at NC State, Sat., Nov. 7, Carter-Finley Stadium, Raleigh
articles.text:
Duke 47, Boston College 2, and Nate Sheppard just rewrote the Duke record book on Halloween. Wallace Wade Stadium went full Blue Devil Halloween, with $10.31 tickets for Durham residents, trick-or-treating on the concourse, a halftime costume celebration and candy buckets for the first 750 kids in costume. Sheppard handed out touchdowns the same way.

Allow me to cite my sources. Footnote one: a 10-play, 80-yard drive capped by a 1-yard Sheppard plunge, with Javen Nicholas grabbing a 44-yard throw on third-and-5. Footnote two: Kobe Smith sacked the quarterback, KD Cotton returned the punt 18 yards, and Sheppard scored from 2 yards. Footnote three: a 54-yard Sheppard run, the longest of his career. Footnote four: Walker Eget's 5-yard touchdown throw to tight end Jeremiah Hasley with 2:14 left in the half. That was 27-2 at the break, peer-reviewed.

The third quarter added two more footnotes. Sheppard scored from 4 yards and then from 1 yard on the first two drives of the half. Five rushing touchdowns, a Duke single-game record, on 20 carries for 97 yards. Gavin Strange closed it with two field goals in the fourth quarter, including a 41-yarder, the longest of his career.

Now the defense, which deserves its own dissertation. Boston College got 213 yards. The Eagles went 0 for 6 on third down in the first half, 0 for 4 on fourth down all day, and they lost two fumbles. Duke sacked them six times, with Bradley Gompers, Bryce Davis, Kobe Smith and Owen Wafle each getting a full one. Nick Morris Jr. and Kobe Smith each fell on a fumble. The two points the Eagles scored came on a returned extra point. Their offense never found the scoreboard. That is the fewest points by a Duke conference opponent since 1989.

My one grade of incomplete: the failed extra point Carter Davis took 100 yards the other way, and an interception off Dan Mahan late in the third. Minor revisions. The rest of the paper gets an A.

Duke is 6-2 and 3-2 in the ACC, and bowl eligible for the fifth straight season. Pre-bowl, pre-November, pre-everything. Next we go to NC State at Carter-Finley Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 7. Pack the pens. We are writing more.

articles.text:
Duke 47, Boston College 2, and the court will note for the record that our only points came on a 100-yard sprint by Carter Davis after a failed Duke extra point. Back home in Newton, nearly 500 kids had spent last weekend painting Halloween scenes on more than 150 storefront windows across seven village centers. I have argued losing cases in moot court. I have never argued one this hopeless. Duke punted on its first drive, we punted on ours, and then Nate Sheppard went to work.
