Sheppard scored twice more in the third quarter for five rushing touchdowns, a Duke school record set on our watch.

Exhibit A for the prosecution: we went 2 for 13 on third down and 0 for 4 on fourth down, and we were flagged 15 times for 129 yards. Fifteen. I could not get fifteen objections sustained in a full semester. Duke sacked our quarterbacks six times. Mason McKenzie was 9 of 17 for 87 yards and ran 13 times for 24 more, and we lost two fumbles. We finished with 213 yards.

Exhibit B for the defense, because there is one. Carter Davis was everywhere. He took that extra point the length of the field, he intercepted Dan Mahan in the third quarter, and he had two tackles for loss. Anthony Palano made nine tackles. Marcus Upton made eight more and returned four kicks for 81 yards. Bryce LaFollette punted six times for a 42.8-yard average, and Jackson Wade hauled in a 36-yard grab. That defense spent way too long on the field and still kept swinging.

My verdict is guilty on all counts, and I am sentencing myself to a double order at the Court of Iced Coffee before the bus gets home. articles.title: Iowa vs Wisconsin: Hawkeyes Blank Badgers on Homecoming 30-0
articles.matchup: Final: Iowa (6-2) 30, Wisconsin (5-3) 0, Sat., Oct. 31, Kinnick Stadium, Iowa City. Next: at Northwestern, Sat., Nov. 7, Ryan Field, Evanston
articles.text:
Iowa 30, Wisconsin 0, on Homecoming weekend at Kinnick Stadium. Friday night the Homecoming Parade rolled through downtown Iowa City, west on Washington and around to Iowa Avenue, and on Halloween afternoon the Hawkeyes gave a crowd of 69,250 the best float of the weekend: the Heartland Trophy, staying put.

Hank Brown was close to perfect. He went 16 of 18 in the first half and finished 20 of 24 for 222 yards and two touchdowns, both 4-yard throws, one to DJ Vonnahme and one to Tony Diaz. Seven different Hawkeyes caught a ball.

But you know me. I came for the defense. Wisconsin went 86 yards in 12 plays in the second quarter and got to our 1. On fourth-and-goal, Jayden Montgomery and Cam Buffington stopped Abu Sama III for a 1-yard loss. Then the offense went 98 yards in seven plays, and Brown found Diaz with 1:30 left. Montgomery recovered a fumble for his first career takeaway, and Caden Buhr hit from 28 as time expired. 20-0.

Vonnahme added a 2-yard touchdown run in the third, the first rushing score by a Hawkeye tight end since 2018, and Buhr drilled a 54-yarder, the longest of his career. In the fourth, Jacob Wallace intercepted Ryan Hopkins at our 21, and Zach Lutmer knocked a 57-yard catch loose at our 12 for a touchback. Wisconsin got close twice and left with nothing both times.

The Badgers finished with 235 yards, 52 on the ground, and nine first downs. Buffington led us with eight tackles and a sack, Xavier Williams carried 20 times for 78 yards, and we were flagged twice all day. It is our third shutout of the season, the first time that has happened in the Kirk Ferentz era, and our fifth straight win over Wisconsin.

My wife keeps telling me the black-and-gold sweater needs retiring. After a Homecoming shutout? It just earned another full season.

We're 6-2, 3-2 in the Big Ten and bowl eligible for the 14th straight season. Next is Northwestern at Ryan Field in Evanston on Saturday, Nov. 7. Go Hawks.

articles.title: Wisconsin vs Iowa: Badgers Blanked at Kinnick, Fall 30-0
articles.matchup: Final: Iowa (6-2) 30, Wisconsin (5-3) 0, Sat., Oct. 31, Kinnick Stadium, Iowa City. Next: vs. Rutgers, Sat., Nov. 7, Camp Randall Stadium, Madison
articles.text:
Iowa 30, Wisconsin 0, and the Heartland Trophy stays in Iowa City. Back home on Halloween, the Madison Ballet was opening its 45th season with a world-premiere Jekyll & Hyde at Madison Youth Arts. Our Badgers spent the afternoon at Kinnick Stadium playing Mr. Hyde on offense, and nobody in Madison bought a ticket for that show.

Iowa scored on its first two drives, a Caden Buhr field goal and a 4-yard Hank Brown throw to DJ Vonnahme, and it was 10-0 before we moved the sticks once.

Then came the drive that still stings. Colton Joseph hit Chris Brooks Jr. for 18 and Jaylon Domingeaux for 41, down to the Iowa 8. Joseph carried it to the 1. On fourth-and-goal, Abu Sama III got stopped for a 1-yard loss. Twelve plays, 86 yards, zero points. Iowa answered with a 98-yard touchdown drive, Joseph fumbled at our 16 with 45 seconds left, and Buhr kicked a field goal at the horn. 20-0 at the half.

The second half brought no rescue. Vonnahme ran one in from 2, Buhr drilled a 54-yarder, and Ryan Hopkins took over late in the third. Jacob Wallace intercepted Hopkins at the Iowa 21. Later Hopkins found Tyrell Henry for 57 yards, but the ball got punched loose at the Iowa 12 and rolled through the end zone for a touchback. Even the big play ended in a goose egg.

Honest numbers, because a fullback doesn't hide from contact: 52 rushing yards on 24 carries, 4 of 13 on third down, nine first downs, three turnovers. Joseph went 5 of 14 for 90 yards, and Hopkins went 8 of 13 for 93 with the interception. Iowa held the ball for 36:21.

The defense kept swinging the whole way. Cooper Catalano made 16 tackles and recovered a fumble. Mason Posa had 13, Matthew Jung had 12, Sebastian Cheeks sacked Brown, and Sean West punted six times at 46.5 yards a pop. But Brown still went 20 of 24, and that is too clean for anybody's liking in Dane County.

No polka tonight. I ate a brat in thoughtful silence. Then I ate another one.

We're 5-3 and 3-2 in the Big Ten, and Iowa has now won five straight in this series. Rutgers comes to Camp Randall Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 7, and that crowd will be ready to jump. On, Wisconsin.

articles.title: Texas Tech vs Arizona: Red Raiders Run Down Wildcats 34-26
articles.matchup: Final: Texas Tech (7-1) 34, Arizona (6-2) 26, Sat., Oct. 31, Galaxy Stadium, Lubbock. Next: vs. West Virginia, Sat., Nov. 7, Galaxy Stadium, Lubbock
articles.text:
Texas Tech 34, Arizona 26. Thirteen straight home wins. That ties the program record. Raider Alley opened in the Engineering Key at 7 a.m. with George Ducas on the stage, the Red Raider Club got its appreciation game, and 59,131 showed up under a cloudy sky at 55 degrees. Loud. Long day. Worth it.

Arizona came to throw. Noah Fifita threw for 417 yards. Isaiah Mizell got loose for 94 in the second quarter. We trailed 17-10 at the half. Fine. Halftime is not the finish.

Second half, we ran. Thomas Castellanos got the start and ran 19 times for 117 yards, and his 8-yard run tied it 17-17. Arizona scored again, but Ansel Nedore blocked the extra point. Big play. Castellanos then hit Kenny Johnson for 27 yards on fourth-and-2, and we led 24-23. Stone Harrington drilled a 42-yarder 17 seconds into the fourth. 27-23.

Defense held on the big one. Arizona went for it on fourth-and-1 at our 18 and the throw sailed into the Lubbock air. Then J'Koby Williams took a handoff 64 yards with 2:05 left. Gone, and he finished with 175 yards on 14 carries. We ran for 328 yards as a team on 47 carries, 7.0 a pop. That is how Lubbock plays in the wind.

Honest part. We turned it over once, a Cameron Dickey fumble. Castellanos went 11 of 24 through the air for 144 yards and two touchdowns, Terrance Carter Jr. caught the first one, and we gave up big chunks. Arizona only ran for 12 yards, though. Austin Romaine made 14 tackles. Ben Roberts had 11. John Curry got a sack and three tackles for loss.

After a field goal with 22 seconds left, Quinten Joyner fell on the onside kick. Over.

We are 7-1, 4-1 in the Big 12 and 5-0 at home. West Virginia comes to Galaxy Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 7. Win and the home streak becomes the record. Guns up.

articles.title: Arizona vs Texas Tech: Fifita's 417 Not Enough in Lubbock 34-26
articles.matchup: Final: Texas Tech (7-1) 34, Arizona (6-2) 26, Sat., Oct. 31, Galaxy Stadium, Lubbock. Next: vs. TCU, Fri., Nov. 6, Casino Del Sol Stadium, Tucson
articles.text:
Texas Tech 34, Arizona 26, and the five-game winning streak is over in Lubbock. Back home on Saturday, 40 Arizona high school bands filled Casino Del Sol Stadium for the 73rd U of A Band Day with the Pride of Arizona. Tucson played loud. We needed that kind of noise on the road and only got it in bursts.

The bursts were big. Michael Salgado-Medina opened the scoring from 35 yards. In the second quarter Noah Fifita hit Isaiah Mizell for 94 yards, the kind of throw that makes a whole desert stand up, and Kedrick Reescano punched in a 5-yard run. We went to the half up 17-10 in their building.

Then the ground game dried up like an August wash. We ran 30 times for 12 yards. Twelve. Fifita carried the whole offense on his arm, 33 of 45 for 417 yards and a touchdown with zero interceptions, and we had zero turnovers. Mizell finished with seven catches for 182 yards, his third straight 100-yard game, and Giovanni Richardson added six for 90.

Texas Tech answered on the ground. Thomas Castellanos ran it in from 8 to tie it 17-17. Reescano scored again from a yard out, but the extra point got blocked, and that missing point hung over the rest of the night. Castellanos found Kenny Johnson for 27 yards on fourth-and-2, and we trailed 24-23. Their kicker made it 27-23 from 42 early in the fourth.

We had our shot. Fourth-and-1 at the Tech 18, and the throw sailed. Later Dwight Bootle II jumped on a Cameron Dickey fumble, the one gift of the night. Then J'Koby Williams broke a 64-yard run with 2:05 left, and that was the dagger. Salgado-Medina hit from 22 with 22 seconds left, Texas Tech recovered the onside kick, and we were done.

Credit where it's due. Tech ran for 328 yards, and Williams had 175 of them on 14 carries. Malcolm Hartzog Jr. made 10 tackles trying to plug it. A saguaro takes decades to grow an arm. This team grew a passing game in one afternoon. Now it needs legs.

We are 6-2 and 3-2 in the Big 12. TCU comes to Casino Del Sol Stadium on Friday, Nov. 6, at 10:15 PM ET. Home crowd, Friday night, back to work. Bear Down.

articles.title: Syracuse vs SMU: Orange Stun No. 19 Mustangs Late 30-27
articles.matchup: Final: Syracuse (4-4) 30, SMU (6-2) 27, Sat., Oct. 31, JMA Wireless Dome, Syracuse. Next: vs. Clemson (Homecoming), Sat., Nov. 7, JMA Wireless Dome, Syracuse
articles.text:
Syracuse 30, SMU 27, and the ranked visitors from Dallas got tricked on Halloween. Before kickoff, kids in costumes walked the same Quad route our team walks into the JMA Wireless Dome, the suites handed out candy, and for the first time ever the Orange wore helmets with Otto on the side. After today, that helmet belongs in a trophy case.

Steve Angeli set the tone on the opening drive with a 26-yard touchdown run, a full foot of fresh snow before lunch. SMU answered with a field goal and a Kevin Jennings touchdown throw, and we trailed 10-7 after one. Then Demetres Samuel Jr. punched the ball out of Jalen Hale's hands, Davien Kerr scooped it up, and Tripp Woody kept splitting the uprights. Ahmad Miller plunged in from a yard out with 22 seconds left in the half, and we went in up 20-10.

The fourth quarter tested every one of us. Pinned at our own 8, we gave up a safety, Kendrick Raphael scored, the two-point try went in, and we were down 27-20 with 9:04 to play. That felt like the plow truck sliding into the ditch on Erie Boulevard.

This team does not sit in the ditch. Angeli moved us into range and Woody hit from 26 yards, his third field goal of the day. Tunmise Adeleye sacked Jennings to kill the next SMU drive. Then Angeli went to work from our 32 with 3:35 left, hitting Umari Hatcher, David Clement, Calvin Russell III and Daunte Bacheyie, and on the 11th play he flipped a 2-yard touchdown to Noah Meyers with 17 seconds left. Woody's kick made it 30-27. Chase Geter fell on one more SMU fumble on the final play.

Angeli finished 21 of 34 for 200 yards with no interceptions. Hatcher caught six balls for 65 yards. Samuel made 10 tackles, Keyshawn Johnson had two sacks, and Jimmy Gregg boomed four punts for a 52.8-yard average. We had zero turnovers, and we went 4 for 4 on fourth down.

That's a two-foot lake-effect dump of a WIN, and I am celebrating with a whole bag of salt potatoes. We are 4-4 and 2-4 in the ACC. Clemson comes to the Dome for Homecoming on Nov. 7. Pack it again, Orange Nation.

articles.text:
Syracuse 30, SMU 27. Back home in Dallas, NorthPark Center's Pumpkin Patch was in its final weekend in Center Park, gnome village and mythical maze included, and I had my Monday photo shoot planned around it. Up in the JMA Wireless Dome, the Syracuse Orange wore Otto on their helmets for the first time ever, and with 17 seconds left on Halloween, that big orange pumpkin of a mascot got the last laugh.

I am not hiding it. We had this one. Kevin Jennings was close to flawless, 29 of 36 for 351 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions. He hit Jalen Hale from 9 yards out at the end of the first quarter, found Yamir Knight for a 14-yard score in the third, and Knight finished with six catches for 80 yards. Yannick Smith caught five for 95. That is a throwing game you frame and hang in the shop window.

Then the fourth quarter got loud. Wade McSparron's punt pinned Syracuse at its own 8, their drive went backward, and we took a safety, 20-19. Kendrick Raphael ran it in from 13 yards, Jennings threw the two-point try to Derrick McFall, and we led 27-20 with 9:04 left. I was reaching for the confetti.

Put it back in the box. Syracuse kicked a field goal, our next drive went three plays backward with a sack in the middle of it, and Steve Angeli marched the Orange 11 plays down the field. His 2-yard throw to Noah Meyers with 17 seconds left was the dagger. Our last gasp ended in a fumble.

The honest fitting-room mirror: two lost fumbles, nine penalties for 90 yards and 70 rushing yards on 31 carries. Hale's fumble in the second quarter, forced by Demetres Samuel Jr., set up a Syracuse field goal, and Jennings got sacked four times. Syracuse went 4 for 4 on fourth down. We outgained them 421 to 338 and still flew home with the loss. Sael Reyes made 10 tackles and the defense pinned Syracuse deep all day. They deserved better.

So yes, I am wearing the biggest sunglasses I own on the flight home. We are 6-2 and 4-2 in the ACC, and nothing is lost that a Friday night on the Boulevard cannot fix. Virginia Tech comes to Gerald J. Ford Stadium on Friday, Nov. 6. Pony up.

articles.title: Navy vs Notre Dame: Mids Rule First Half, Fall 35-13
articles.matchup: Final: Notre Dame (7-1) 35, Navy (2-6) 13, Sat., Oct. 31, Gillette Stadium, Foxborough. Next: vs. Temple, Sat., Nov. 7, 3:30 PM ET, Navy-Marine Corps Memorial Stadium, Annapolis
articles.text:
Notre Dame 35, Navy 13. Saturday in Annapolis meant the Day of the Dead Festival at Maryland Hall on Chase Street, with altars, music and dancing from 3 to 8 p.m. Up in Foxborough, the Midshipmen took on fifth-ranked Notre Dame. For one half, Navy had the Irish looking like they'd seen a ghost.

Plot the first-half chart and it reads like a perfect patrol. We held the ball for 23:33 of the first 30 minutes and scored on our first three possessions. The opener went 14 plays and 8:17, and Nolan Bartley, a freshman, drilled a career-long 38-yard field goal. The next one went 16 plays and 8:43, our longest drive of the season, and Bartley hit from 26. Then Jackson Gutierrez finished an 11-play march with a 2-yard keeper, and we led 13-7 with 1:52 left in the half. Anchors aweigh.

Then the weather turned. Nolan James Jr. broke a 52-yard run with 55 seconds left, and Notre Dame went in up 14-13. The Irish opened the second half with a 78-yard drive and never looked back. We came up short on fourth down at our own 43 late in the third, and CJ Carr turned that into a 31-yard touchdown throw on the first play of the fourth. Twenty-eight straight points. Eight penalties for 86 yards put us in first-and-long too many times, and an option offense can't sail into that wind.

Steady as she goes, because there is plenty worth keeping. Gutierrez ran 28 times for 110 yards and a touchdown, his fourth straight 100-yard day. Michael Barrow added 65 yards on 11 carries. We ran for 212 yards on 48 carries against a defense that came in allowing 67.3 a game on the ground, and the big guys up front didn't allow a sack. Giuseppe Sessi and MarcAnthony Parker made eight tackles each, and we had zero turnovers.

We also wore the 1926 throwbacks, with nine chevrons for the nine wins of that national title team. It was a fine way to honor a century of Navy football.

We're 2-6 and 1-4 in the American. Course correction comes at home. Temple visits Navy-Marine Corps Memorial Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 7, at 3:30 PM ET. Beat Temple. Go Navy.

articles.title: Notre Dame vs Navy: Irish Score 28 Straight to Sink Navy 35-13
articles.matchup: Final: Notre Dame (7-1) 35, Navy (2-6) 13, Sat., Oct. 31, Gillette Stadium, Foxborough. Next: vs. Miami, Sat., Nov. 7, 7:30 PM ET, Notre Dame Stadium, Notre Dame
articles.text:
Notre Dame 35, Navy 13. Back home, the Library Lawn is set for HalloweenFest tonight, with a custom haunted house, carnival rides and food trucks, and the Fighting Irish are bringing the campus a fitting Halloween story: a first half that gave us a real scare and a second half that buried it. I would posit, for the record, that the scare was earned.

Proposition one: Navy's option is not a gimmick, it is a clock-eating machine. The Midshipmen held the ball for 23:33 of the first half and scored on their first three trips. Jackson Gutierrez carried 28 times for 110 yards, Nolan Bartley hit field goals from 38 and 26, and Gutierrez's 2-yard run put Navy up 13-7 with 1:52 left in the half. Our offense had the ball for 6:27 before the break. Six minutes. You cannot grade an offense that never gets to the exam.

Proposition two: when Nolan James Jr. gets a crease, the argument is over. With 55 seconds left in the half he broke a 52-yard touchdown run, and we went to the locker room up 14-13. James finished with 107 yards and two scores on nine carries. Nine.

Proposition three: the second half was the thesis. We took the opening kickoff 78 yards in 11 plays, and Jonaz Walton punched it in from 3. James went 23 yards for 28-13. Navy went for it on fourth down at its own 43 and came up short, and two plays later CJ Carr found Jerome Bettis Jr. for a 31-yard touchdown on the first snap of the fourth quarter. That's 28 unanswered. Navy held the ball for 9:07 after halftime and never scored again.

Carr went 19 of 29 for 210 yards and two touchdowns, with an 11-yard strike to Micah Gilbert for our first score. Bettis caught six balls for 78 yards. We had zero turnovers and two penalties. Luke Talich made 10 tackles, and Jaiden Ausberry added eight.

Peer review, because honesty is the whole discipline: Navy ran for 212 yards on 48 carries, the most anyone has run on this defense all season. The defense adjusted, but the first half needs a footnote in red ink.

That's nine straight wins over Navy, and we're 7-1. Next is Miami at Notre Dame Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 7, at 7:30 PM ET. Defense rests. Go Irish.

articles.title: Ole Miss vs Auburn: Rebels Pull Away on Halloween, Win 45-15
articles.matchup: Final: Ole Miss (6-2) 45, Auburn (4-4) 15, Sat., Oct. 31, Vaught-Hemingway Stadium, Oxford. Next: vs. Georgia, Sat., Nov. 7, Vaught-Hemingway Stadium, Oxford
articles.text:
Ole Miss 45, Auburn 15. On Halloween, the Party in the Sip called for powder blue, and 67,041 of us filled Vaught-Hemingway Stadium to watch the Rebels write a fourth quarter that Mr. Faulkner would have needed three hundred pages to finish. Auburn hung around into the late third quarter. The ending belonged to Oxford.

Every great novel opens slow. Our first drive went 16 plays and ran out of quarter at the Auburn 1. On the first snap of the second, Will Echoles plowed in for the first rushing touchdown of his career, capping a 17-play, 89-yard march that was our longest drive of the season.

The middle chapters had twists. Jehiem Oatis blocked Auburn's extra point, and Jaylon Braxton carried it 92 yards to the Auburn 5. Chambliss was intercepted on the first play of our next drive, but Jamarious Brown answered two plays later with the first fumble recovery of his career, and Shekai Mills-Knight finished an 86-yard drive from a yard out. Auburn crept to 17-15 late in the third. A false start pushed its two-point try back five yards, and our defense slammed the door.

Then came the finale, 28 straight points. Trinidad Chambliss ran 26 yards for a touchdown, his seventh rushing score of the season. In the fourth quarter he threw 6 yards to Caleb Cunningham and 28 yards to Horatio Fields, and Deuce Knight closed it with a 17-yard run. Chambliss finished 22 of 34 for 263 yards and two touchdown throws, plus 65 rushing yards and the score on the ground. He went over 6,000 career passing yards at Ole Miss and has now thrown a touchdown in 21 straight games, one shy of the school record.

The defense was the plot. A season-high 10 tackles for loss. Suntarine Perkins and Tah'j Butler had two sacks each, and Perkins climbed to fourth on the Ole Miss career list with 22. Keaton Thomas led us with eight tackles, Anthony Robinson III forced a late fumble and Dante Core fell on it. Auburn ran for 63 yards all day, and we converted 13 of 16 third downs.

I delivered my victory monologue under the nearest chandelier. It ran three paragraphs. No regrets.

That is 16 straight home wins, tied for the second-longest active streak in FBS, and three straight over Auburn. We're 6-2 and 4-2 in the SEC. Georgia comes to the Vaught on Saturday, Nov. 7. Hotty Toddy.

articles.title: Auburn vs Ole Miss: Tigers Fade Late on Halloween, Fall 45-15
articles.matchup: Final: Ole Miss (6-2) 45, Auburn (4-4) 15, Sat., Oct. 31, Vaught-Hemingway Stadium, Oxford. Next: vs. Arkansas, Sat., Nov. 7, Jordan-Hare Stadium, Auburn
articles.text:
Ole Miss 45, Auburn 15, on Halloween afternoon in Oxford. Back home on Friday, the 38th Annual Pumpkin Carve lit up Dudley Courtyard with 200 pumpkins, and Aubie worked the crowd until the leftovers were auctioned off at 8:30. By Saturday evening, the only thing glowing on the Plains was my phone, full of texts I refuse to answer.

For a half, this was a fight. Byrum Brown led a 14-play, 75-yard drive and found Chas Nimrod for a 21-yard touchdown, then Ole Miss blocked the extra point and ran it back 92 yards to our 5. AnQuon Fegans intercepted Trinidad Chambliss on the first play of the next Rebel drive. That was the good news. Two plays later we fumbled it right back, and Ole Miss went 86 yards to make it 14-6. Alex McPherson hit from 29 with five seconds left, and we went in down 14-9.

Coming out of the break, Brown did it with his legs, capping a 10-play, 75-yard drive with a 7-yard touchdown run. We trailed 17-15 with 6:20 left in the third, and the whole Plains was on its feet. Then a false start pushed the two-point try back five yards, the try came up empty, and the afternoon went sideways.

From there Ole Miss scored the last 28 points. Chambliss ran 26 yards for one score and threw two more touchdowns in the fourth quarter, and Deuce Knight added a 17-yard run with 3:27 left. Sam Turner lost a fumble after that. The Rebels converted 13 of 16 third downs, and I need to lie down just typing it.

Honest film session: Brown went 25 of 38 for 195 yards and a touchdown, but his 13 carries netted 5 yards, and as a team we ran for 63 yards on 27 tries. Ole Miss piled up 10 tackles for loss, four of them sacks, and rolled up 487 yards. Champ Anthony, Bryce Deas and Kaleb Harris made eight tackles apiece, and Nimrod and DeShawn Spencer each caught four balls for 62 yards. We were 7 of 14 on third down. That part I will defend at any tailgate.

Bless their hearts, the Rebels earned it. I am sipping my lemonade with every ounce of dignity I have left, and I promise you it is not much.

We're 4-4, 2-4 in the SEC and 1-2 on the road. Arkansas comes to Jordan-Hare Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 7, and Toomer's Corner has waited long enough for its next roll. War Eagle.

articles.title: Penn State vs Purdue: Wallace, Hansen Run Lions Past Boilers 31-17
articles.matchup: Final: Penn State (4-4) 31, Purdue (3-5) 17, Sat., Oct. 31, Beaver Stadium, University Park. Next: at Washington, Sat., Nov. 7, Husky Stadium, Seattle
articles.text:
Penn State 31, Purdue 17, and on All-U Day, with Commonwealth Campus students set for the halftime spotlight at Beaver Stadium, the Nittany Lions gave every campus something to cheer about. It is our first Big Ten win of the season, and it snapped a four-game losing streak. We Are!

Former setter talking here: this was a game about getting the ball to the right hitters, and Rocco Becht kept setting up his runners. Cam Wallace ran 22 times for 135 yards and a touchdown, including a 48-yard burst that set up Becht's own 6-yard touchdown run. Carson Hansen added 96 yards and a 1-yard score on fourth-and-goal. We ran 51 times for 269 yards and held the ball for 43:27.

The opening drive told you everything: 12 plays, 96 yards, capped by Becht's 4-yard touchdown throw to Andrew Rappleyea. Becht finished 16 of 24 for 175 yards, and Benjamin Brahmer caught four balls for 58, including a 33-yarder on the 85-yard drive that ended with Wallace scoring from 2 out for a 31-14 lead.

Now the Creamery Rankings. This defense was a big scoop of Death by Chocolate today. Purdue had 175 yards, nine first downs and 33 rushing yards. Jamison Patton and Jeremiah Cooper each intercepted Ryan Browne, Yvan Kemajou got a sack, and Patton's interception set up Ryan Barker's 44-yard field goal for a 24-14 lead.

Honest part, because I don't sell melted ice cream. Purdue blocked one of our punts and Jalil Hall returned it 31 yards for a touchdown toward our Halloween-decorated student section, which tied it 14-14. Xavier Townsend beat us for a 33-yard score. Barker also missed two field goals. Those mistakes have to go before Seattle.

Still, 12 straight wins over Purdue, and a team that went 3 for 3 on fourth down. That is a group that kept swinging.

We're 4-4, 1-4 in the Big Ten and 3-2 at home. Next up: at Washington, Saturday, Nov. 7, at Husky Stadium in Seattle.

articles.title: Purdue vs Penn State: Boilers Tie It, Then Fade at Beaver 31-17
articles.matchup: Final: Penn State (4-4) 31, Purdue (3-5) 17, Sat., Oct. 31, Beaver Stadium, University Park. Next: vs. Maryland, Sat., Nov. 7, Ross-Ade Stadium, West Lafayette
articles.text:
Penn State 31, Purdue 17. West Lafayette set its trick-or-treat hours for 6 to 8 p.m. on Halloween, and by the end of this one I was ready to hand out every piece of candy in the house just to think about something else. The Boilermakers hung with Penn State for a half in Beaver Stadium, then ran out of fuel.

Let me open the Blueprint, because the first half had real engineering in it. After Penn State scored on its opening drive, Ryan Browne hit Asaad Waseem for 38 yards and then Xavier Townsend for a 33-yard touchdown. Four plays, 75 yards, tied 7-7. In the second quarter, Bisi Owens blocked a Penn State punt and Jalil Hall scooped it up and ran 31 yards for the score that tied it 14-14. That was the best special teams play we have made all year.

Then the design flaw showed up. Penn State ran 51 times for 269 yards and held the ball for 43:27. Its 15-play drive before the half ended with a 1-yard touchdown on fourth down, and in the third quarter Jamison Patton intercepted Browne to set up a field goal. Cam Wallace finished with 135 rushing yards. You cannot build a machine that only runs for 16 minutes.

Our defense spent all night on the field and still fought. Justin Denson made 15 tackles, Jojo Hayden made 10, and Curt Neal had two sacks. Jacobo Echeverria Lozano hit a 49-yarder in the fourth quarter after Browne converted a fourth down with a 24-yard throw.

The honest numbers are ugly. We finished with 175 yards, nine first downs and 33 rushing yards. Browne went 10 of 29 for 142 yards with a touchdown and two interceptions. Penn State has now won 12 straight in this series, and we have not beaten them since 2004.

My model Boilermaker Special has a cracked wheel tonight. I'll fix it in the garage this week, same as this team needs to fix its run game.

We're 3-5 and 2-3 in the Big Ten. Maryland comes to Ross-Ade Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 7. Boiler up!

articles.title: UCLA vs Nevada: Bruins Pitch Halloween Shutout, Go 8-0, 27-0
articles.matchup: Final: UCLA (8-0) 27, Nevada (3-5) 0, Sat., Oct. 31, Rose Bowl, Pasadena. Next: at Minnesota, Sat., Nov. 7, Huntington Bank Stadium, Minneapolis
articles.text:
UCLA 27, Nevada 0, at the Rose Bowl, and we're 8-0 for the sixth time in program history and the first time since 2005. It was Halloween in Pasadena, with kids in costume trick-or-treating at the Court of Champions, and our defense showed up dressed as a horror movie. Three interceptions in the first quarter. Roll credits early.

Cold open: on Nevada's first snap, Scooter Jackson intercepts Luke Duncan, and Mateen Bhaghani turns it into a 26-yard field goal. Scene two: Jalen Woods intercepts Duncan at our 16. Scene three: Derrick Barksdale intercepts Duncan and takes it 26 yards to the end zone. 10-0 with 7:33 left in the first quarter. You can't storyboard it better than that.

The offense needed a few takes. Then Ty Dieffenbach directed a 10-play, 71-yard drive and finished it himself with a 4-yard run with 1:20 left in the half. In the third quarter he led a 13-play, 75-yard march and hit Wayne Knight from 12 for a 24-0 lead. Bhaghani added a 38-yarder in the fourth, and Ty Lee closed the show with a fourth interception and a 27-yard return with 45 seconds left.

Dieffenbach went 16 of 30 for 178 yards with zero turnovers. Knight ran 11 times for 53 yards on top of his touchdown catch, Jalen Saint Paul caught three balls for 52, and Semaj Morgan had five for 32. The defense held Nevada to 176 yards, 65 on the ground on 35 carries, and 5 of 16 on third down. Sahir West had nine tackles and 1.5 sacks, Aiden Gobaira had seven tackles, 1.5 sacks and three tackles for loss, and Trent Hendrick made eight stops.

That's a shutout, a defensive touchdown and an unbeaten record into November. Greenlit.

We're 8-0, 5-0 in the Big Ten. Next is Minnesota on Saturday, Nov. 7, at Huntington Bank Stadium in Minneapolis. Location shoot in the cold. Pack the parka. Go Bruins.

articles.title: Nevada vs UCLA: Wolf Pack Shut Out at the Rose Bowl, Fall 27-0
articles.matchup: Final: UCLA (8-0) 27, Nevada (3-5) 0, Sat., Oct. 31, Rose Bowl, Pasadena. Next: vs. New Mexico, Fri., Nov. 6, Mackay Stadium, Reno
articles.text:
UCLA 27, Nevada 0, at the Rose Bowl, and this was a powder day that went sideways before the first chair loaded. Back home in Reno, Reno Public Market on Plumb Lane opened its food hall to trick-or-treaters from 4 to 7 on Halloween, kids in costume working the vendor stalls. The Pack went trick-or-treating in Pasadena and came home with an empty bag.

On our first snap of the day, Scooter Jackson intercepted Luke Duncan at our 30, and UCLA kicked a 26-yard field goal. Our next drive reached the UCLA 16 before Jalen Woods intercepted Duncan there. One drive later, Derrick Barksdale intercepted Duncan and ran it back 26 yards for a touchdown. Three interceptions, and 7:33 still left in the first quarter. 10-0.

Credit the defense for digging in after that. UCLA's next three drives ended in punts. Ty Dieffenbach finally ran it in from the 4 with 1:20 left in the half, and Mateen Bhaghani missed from 51 at the gun. 17-0.

The third quarter is where we needed a turn and never got it. UCLA went 13 plays and 75 yards, Dieffenbach throwing 12 yards to Wayne Knight. We answered with a 10-play drive, and Joe McFadden missed from 48. Bhaghani hit from 38 in the fourth, and Ty Lee intercepted Reeve Slone with 45 seconds left.

The defense kept us upright. EJ Smith made nine tackles, Larry Turner-Gooden had eight and broke up two throws, and Dylan LaBarbera shared a sack and broke up two more. UCLA finished with 303 yards. Ewan Baulch punted five times for a 44.4 average. But we threw four interceptions, ran 35 times for 65 yards and finished with 176 yards and 10 first downs. Marshaun Brown caught three balls for 51 yards, and AJ Bianco went 6 of 13 for 71.

Some days the mountain wins. You pack it in, wax the board and come back meaner.

We're 3-5, 2-2 in the Mountain West. New Mexico comes to Mackay Stadium on Friday night, Nov. 6, and Reno gets its own team back. Go Pack.

articles.title: TCU vs Kansas: Jaden Craig Leads Frogs Back From 13-0, Win 22-16
articles.matchup: Final: TCU (4-4) 22, Kansas (3-5) 16, Sat., Oct. 31, Amon G. Carter Stadium, Fort Worth. Next: at Arizona, Fri., Nov. 6, Casino Del Sol Stadium, Tucson
articles.text:
TCU 22, Kansas 16, and the Haunting at the Carter lived up to the name. The Frogs blacked out Amon G. Carter Stadium for their first home game on Halloween since 2009, and for one half it felt like the lights went out on us, too. Then the second half came, and we scared the Jayhawks out of Fort Worth.

No excuses for the first 30 minutes. We punted seven times in our first eight possessions, Kansas led 13-0 at the break, and we got stopped inside the Kansas 1 with three seconds left in the half. That was the first time since the 2018 Cheez-It Bowl that we went scoreless in a first half. Somebody up the road in Dallas was surely laughing.

Running a defense is like moving cattle: you lose a few strays early, but you keep the herd together and push. Kansas drove to our 2 in the third quarter, and our guys held on fourth-and-goal. A few minutes later, Max Carroll intercepted Cole Ballard on fourth down and ran 60 yards for a touchdown. Ace Theus broke a 28-yard touchdown run with 26 seconds left in the third, and we had our first lead at 14-13.

Kansas kicked ahead 16-14 with 4:59 left, after Jamel Johnson's 94-yard interception return was wiped out by a flag. That is when Jaden Craig grabbed this game by the horns. He led a 13-play, 84-yard drive, ran it in from 17 yards with 1:11 to go, and threw the two-point conversion to Jordan Dwyer. Ballard's last heave fell incomplete. Yeehaw!

Craig threw for 141 yards and ran for 87 more on 15 carries. Johnson made 10 tackles, Kylin Jackson had two tackles for loss, Koron Hayward forced a fumble with a sack that Markis Deal recovered, and the defense piled up eight tackles for loss. John Hoyet Chance punted eight times and averaged 43.5 yards.

Honest note: Kansas outgained us by 165 yards. But we finally won a one-score game after four losses by eight points or fewer, and we outscored Kansas 22-3 after halftime.

We're 4-4, 2-3 in the Big 12 and 3-2 at home. Next up: at Arizona, Friday, Nov. 6, at Casino Del Sol Stadium in Tucson. Go Frogs.

articles.title: Kansas vs TCU: Jayhawks Lead 13-0, Fall Late in Fort Worth 22-16
articles.matchup: Final: TCU (4-4) 22, Kansas (3-5) 16, Sat., Oct. 31, Amon G. Carter Stadium, Fort Worth. Next: vs. UCF, Sat., Nov. 7, David Booth Kansas Memorial Stadium, Lawrence
articles.text:
TCU 22, Kansas 16, and that one is going to haunt me longer than anything on Massachusetts Street tonight. Downtown Lawrence Trick or Treat ran from 5 to 8 p.m., thousands of us on Mass Street, and I spent most of it staring at my phone replaying a fourth quarter in Fort Worth.

For a half, the Jayhawks owned the place. Martin Connington kicked field goals from 34 and 42 yards, Keaton Kubecka ripped off a 40-yard run, and on the next snap Cole Ballard hit Cam Pickett for a 29-yard touchdown. Then our defense stopped TCU inside our 1 with three seconds left in the half. We went to the locker room up 13-0 with the Frogs held without a first-half point.

Here is the Lawrence translation for my hoops friends: Kansas outgained TCU by 165 yards and held the ball for 38:57. In basketball terms, we owned the boards all night and lost on a late three. That is a very Kansas football sentence, and I hate typing it.

The third quarter turned on two plays. We drove 71 yards and got stopped on fourth-and-goal at the TCU 2, with Ballard a yard short. A few minutes later, on fourth down, Max Carroll intercepted Ballard and went 60 yards the other way. Ace Theus scored from 28 out with 26 seconds left in the quarter, and it was 14-13 TCU.

We answered. Nahzae Cox caught a 50-yard bomb, TCU's Jamel Johnson had a 94-yard interception return wiped out by an interference flag, and Connington hit from 27 for a 16-14 lead with 4:59 left. Then TCU went 84 yards in 13 plays, Jaden Craig ran it in from 17 and threw the two-point conversion, and our last drive went nowhere.

Cox finished with 145 yards on five catches. Pickett caught 10 for 113. Ballard threw for 285 yards and a touchdown, and Trey Lathan made seven tackles. But we lost the turnover battle, missed a 26-yard field goal and came away empty from the 2. Close is not a win, and we are now 0-6 in Fort Worth since TCU joined the Big 12.

We're 3-5 and 1-4 in the Big 12. UCF comes to David Booth Kansas Memorial Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 7. Rock Chalk, and somebody please win me a close one.

articles.title: Cincinnati vs Utah: Bearcats Buried Early on Halloween, 49-25
articles.matchup: Final: Utah (8-0) 49, Cincinnati (5-3) 25, Sat., Oct. 31, Nippert Stadium, Cincinnati. Next: at Houston, Sat., Nov. 7, TDECU Stadium, Houston
articles.text:
Utah 49, Cincinnati 25, at Nippert Stadium, and this one goes down as plain spaghetti. No chili, no cheese, no onions. The program asked us to wear black for Breast Cancer Awareness and invited the kids to come in Halloween costumes, and Clifton showed up dressed for it. The stands looked right. The scoreboard did not.

We hung with them early. Stephen Rusnak hit from 47 to make it 7-3. Then Utah ran 13 yards for a score, and the second quarter got ugly: Gi'Bran Payne lost a fumble that Utah returned 51 yards for a touchdown, Rusnak missed from 35, and Daniel Bray ran 30 yards for another.

We caught a break when Bray fumbled the kickoff after Rusnak's 39-yarder, but Utah fell on it and went 95 yards anyway. Then JC French IV was intercepted and Elijah Davis took it 39 yards for six. 42-6 at the half, a week after we beat Texas Tech on our 100th Homecoming.

The third quarter was at least a three-way. Jacob Finley jumped a Devon Dampier throw at our 21 and ran 79 yards for a touchdown. Cole Tabb ripped off a 48-yard touchdown run. French ran in from the 2 early in the fourth. We won the second half, and nobody on Calhoun Street is handing out trophies for that.

Tabb ran 14 times for 131 yards. French went 16 of 30 for 263 yards. JV Gibson caught five balls for 76, and Malachi Henry had a 63-yard grab. Finley made 10 tackles on top of his touchdown, Antwan Peek Jr. had eight, and Patrick Bauer forced and recovered a fumble in the fourth. We put up 456 yards. Utah put up 534 and scored twice on defense.

Utah is 8-0 for a reason. Credit to them, and now we get back to work.

We're 5-3, 2-3 in the Big 12. Next is a trip to Houston on Saturday, Nov. 7, at TDECU Stadium. Five-way or nothing. Go Bearcats.

articles.title: Utah vs Cincinnati: Utes Bury Bearcats Early, Move to 8-0, 49-25
articles.matchup: Final: Utah (8-0) 49, Cincinnati (5-3) 25, Sat., Oct. 31, Nippert Stadium, Cincinnati. Next: vs. BYU, Sat., Nov. 7, Rice-Eccles Stadium, Salt Lake City
articles.text:
Utah 49, Cincinnati 25, on Halloween at Nippert Stadium, and we're 8-0. Back home on the hill in Salt Lake City, Officers Hollow filled Officers Circle in Fort Douglas from noon to 3 with trick-or-treating, face painting and pumpkin carving, a U tradition since 2004. While those kids were carving pumpkins, our offense was carving up Cincinnati.

Clean run through the first gates. Devon Dampier found Hunter Andrews for a 4-yard touchdown, and after a Cincinnati field goal, Wayshawn Parker ran 13 yards for another with 14 seconds left in the first quarter. 14-3.

Then the avalanche. Ethan Day forced a fumble, and Rabbit Evans scooped it and went 51 yards. Daniel Bray ran 30 for a score. Bray fumbled a kickoff at our 3, Nate Ritchie jumped on it, and we went 95 yards anyway, capped by Dampier's 3-yard touchdown throw to Bray. Then Elijah Davis intercepted JC French IV and ran it back 39 yards with 34 seconds left. 42-6 at the half. That's the whole mountain coming down.

The third quarter had one wipeout. Jacob Finley intercepted Dampier and ran it back 79 yards, and Cole Tabb broke a 48-yard touchdown run. Dampier answered with 28 seconds left in the third, a 59-yard strike to Andrews. 49-19. Cincinnati scored once more, and the gates were closed.

Dampier went 22 of 29 for 260 yards and ran for 45 more. Andrews caught five balls for 112 yards. Parker ran seven times for 82 with a 64-yard burst, and Bray had 75 on eight carries. We piled up 534 yards, 268 on the ground, converted 7 of 11 third downs and held the ball for 35:30. Kash Dillon and Ritchie made seven tackles each, and Karson Kaufusi and Elijah Reed got sacks.

Two defensive touchdowns, five offensive ones and one 79-yard crash we'll study on film. A racer takes that run every single Saturday.

We're 8-0, 5-0 in the Big 12 and 3-0 on the road. BYU comes to Rice-Eccles Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 7. Rivalry week in the Wasatch. Go Utes.

articles.title: Wake Forest vs Virginia: Deacons Roll the Cavaliers 51-7
articles.matchup: Final: Wake Forest (7-1) 51, Virginia (4-5) 7, Sat., Oct. 31, Allegacy Federal Credit Union Stadium, Winston-Salem. Next: vs. Merrimack, Sat., Nov. 7, Allegacy Federal Credit Union Stadium, Winston-Salem
articles.text:
Wake Forest 51, Virginia 7. DEACTOWN dressed up for Halloween, with a pumpkin patch at Gate 5, the Golden Knights on the parachute schedule for the anthem and Thriller on the halftime bill for the Spirit of the Old Gold and Black. Then the Demon Deacons went out and scared the Cavaliers right out of Winston-Salem. Roll the Quad!

Resolved: this was the most complete game of the season. I will argue the affirmative. Exhibit A is the opening drive, set up by a 30-yard punt return from Kam Shanks and a 33-yard strike from Gio Lopez to Carlos Hernandez, finished by a 2-yard Ty Clark III touchdown. Exhibit B is Braylon Johnson's interception on a Virginia fourth down, which led to a 45-yard field goal from Connor Calvert. The defense rests? Hardly.

Clark scored three touchdowns, all on short runs. Lopez went 13 of 21 for 229 yards, hit Hernandez for a 10-yard score after a 64-yard Shanks punt return, and found Drayden Dickmann for 47 on another drive. Hernandez finished with eight catches for 136 yards. Calvert went 3 for 3 on field goals and 6 for 6 on extra points, good for 15 points by himself.

Exhibit C is the third quarter, when we outscored Virginia 24-7. Jamar Searcy broke a 55-yard run and finished the drive with a 7-yard score. Kyndall McCaleb added a 27-yard touchdown run in the fourth. We piled up 538 yards, ran for 309, went 9 of 14 on third down and did not turn it over once.

Rebuttal time, because a fair debater admits the other side's best point. Virginia's Da'Shawn Martin beat us for a 47-yard touchdown late in the third quarter, and that cost us the shutout. Still, our defense stood up on fourth-and-1 at our own 6, where Zach Lohavichan stuffed the run, and again on fourth-and-goal in the fourth quarter. Camden Hardy and Dallas Afalava each got a sack, and Virginia finished with 16 rushing yards.

Closing argument: that is five straight wins, and the second-biggest margin we have ever put on Virginia in this series. I move that we keep winning. Motion carries.

We're 7-1. Merrimack comes to Winston-Salem on Saturday, Nov. 7. Go Deacs.

articles.title: Virginia vs Wake Forest: Cavaliers Run Over in Winston-Salem 51-7
articles.matchup: Final: Wake Forest (7-1) 51, Virginia (4-5) 7, Sat., Oct. 31, Allegacy Federal Credit Union Stadium, Winston-Salem. Next: bye, then vs. California, Sat., Nov. 14, Scott Stadium, Charlottesville
articles.text:
Wake Forest 51, Virginia 7, and I will not dress it up. While the Lawn residents and some 70 student groups were handing out candy from the 54 Lawn rooms and the Range on the Grounds from 5 to 7 p.m., our Cavaliers were taking the worst trick of the night in Winston-Salem. Mr. Jefferson built a place for learning, and we learned plenty.

The trouble started on special teams and never left. Kam Shanks returned punts for 94 yards, including a 64-yarder that set up a touchdown. Ty Clark III scored three times on short runs, Connor Calvert made all three of his field goals, and the Deacons ran for 309 yards on 51 carries. We ran for 16 yards on 19 tries. That gap is the game.

We had our chances early. Braylon Johnson intercepted Beau Pribula on a fourth-down throw in the first quarter, and Calvert turned it into a 45-yarder. In the second quarter we drove 13 plays to the Wake 6 and came away empty when Zach Lohavichan stopped Xay Davis on fourth-and-1. We trailed 20-0 at the half, and we never got closer.

There were honest bright spots. Pribula threw for 212 yards on 20 of 29, and with 50 seconds left in the third quarter he found Da'Shawn Martin for a 47-yard touchdown. Martin finished with nine catches for 119 yards and kept fighting all night. Montino Williams made 10 tackles, Christian Ellis made nine, and Kam Robinson and Matthew Fobbs-White each got a sack. Eli Holstein came in and went 12 of 16.

But 1 of 12 on third down is not a number that wins on the road. Wake went 9 of 14. We are 0-3 away from Charlottesville this year, and the third straight loss stings.

A note for the group chat: anyone who calls our campus a campus this week owes me a bagel. I am collecting. It is the only thing I won on Saturday.

We're 4-5 and 2-4 in the ACC. A bye week comes first, then California visits Scott Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 14. Wahoowa.

articles.title: Indiana vs Minnesota: Hoosiers Win Homecoming in OT 23-16
articles.matchup: Final/OT: Indiana (8-1) 23, Minnesota (5-3) 16, Sat., Oct. 31, Memorial Stadium (Bloomington, IN), Bloomington. Next: vs. USC, Sat., Nov. 14, Memorial Stadium (Bloomington, IN), Bloomington
articles.text:
Indiana 23, Minnesota 16, in overtime, and Homecoming weekend in Bloomington got the ending it deserved. Friday night the Homecoming Parade rolled from Washington Street down Kirkwood Avenue to the Sample Gates, and Saturday the Hoosiers rewarded the 54,400 inside Memorial Stadium for every nervous minute. My rhinestone clicker is down to its last few rhinestones.

This was no pageant walk. Minnesota kicked a 37-yard field goal first, and our answer came off a takeaway: Josh Burnham recovered a fumble at the Minnesota 26, and Josh Hoover hit Nick Marsh for a 9-yard touchdown. Then Drake Lindsey threw 39 yards to Roman Voss, Hoover was intercepted, and we went to the half down 10-7.

Grant Wilson took over at quarterback in the second half and steadied the room. Nico Radicic tied it from 46 in the third and again from 34 with 3:05 left. Then Minnesota's kicker hit from 60 with 19 seconds left, and I forgot how to breathe.

Nineteen seconds. Wilson threw deep to Charlie Becker for 33 yards, and Paddy McAteer walked out and drilled a 60-yarder of his own as time ran out. 16-16. My 40-tab model has no tab for that. It does now.

Overtime took one snap. Wilson to Becker, 25 yards, touchdown. Then the defense took the crown. Minnesota got to our 3, and Jeff Utzinger and Tobi Osunsanmi sacked Lindsey on back-to-back plays to end it at our 9. Talent portion, evening gown and interview, all in two snaps.

Becker finished with eight catches for 149 yards. Wilson went 9 of 17 for 156 yards and ran for 26 more. Lee Beebe Jr. ran 15 times for 84 yards, and Marsh caught four for 59. We outgained Minnesota 419 yards to 215 and won the first-down count 21 to 10. Preston Zachman made nine tackles, and Byron Baldwin Jr. had seven and a sack.

We're 8-1, 5-1 in the Big Ten. After a week off, USC comes to Memorial Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 14. Sash on, clicker reloaded. Go Hoosiers.

articles.title: Minnesota vs Indiana: Gophers Drop OT Kicking Duel 23-16
articles.matchup: Final/OT: Indiana (8-1) 23, Minnesota (5-3) 16, Sat., Oct. 31, Memorial Stadium (Bloomington, IN), Bloomington. Next: vs. UCLA, Sat., Nov. 7, Huntington Bank Stadium, Minneapolis
articles.text:
Indiana 23, Minnesota 16, in overtime in Bloomington, and I'll keep my voice down, because that's how we do it up north. Back home on Halloween night, BareBones Puppet Theatre ran its 33rd Halloween Extravaganza at Powderhorn Park, giant puppets and fire under the theme "Hum, Honk, Howl: As Above, So Below," with folks bringing tarps to sit on the cold ground. Grandpa calls that ice-house training.

We had this one. Luke Drzewiecki hit from 37 to open the scoring. A Drake Lindsey fumble at our 26 handed Indiana a short field and a 9-yard touchdown, but Lindsey answered in the second quarter with a 39-yard strike to Roman Voss. Jaxon Howard intercepted Josh Hoover, and we went to the half up 10-7.

Indiana tied it in the third. Drzewiecki made it 13-10 from 51 early in the fourth, and after Indiana tied it again with 3:05 left, Darius Taylor broke a 19-yard run to get us into Hoosier territory. Drzewiecki stepped up from 60 with 19 seconds left and drilled it. 16-13. Cold enough for ya, Bloomington?

Then 19 seconds turned into a long winter. Grant Wilson, who took over at quarterback for Indiana in the second half, hit Charlie Becker for 33 yards, and Paddy McAteer matched our kicker with a 60-yarder of his own as time ran out. In overtime, Wilson found Becker from 25 on the first snap.

Our turn. Lindsey hit Noah Jennings for 17 yards to the Indiana 8 and ran it to the 3 himself. Then Jeff Utzinger and Tobi Osunsanmi got home on back-to-back sacks, and it ended at the Indiana 9.

Lindsey went 20 of 37 for 120 yards and the Voss touchdown. TJ Thomas caught six balls for 54 yards, and Javon Tracy had seven for 40. Maverick Baranowski made 10 tackles, Kerry Brown seven, and TJ Bush Jr. got a sack. Tom Weston punted seven times for a 48.6 average. We had 215 yards and 10 first downs and still had Indiana beat with 19 seconds left. Drzewiecki went 3 for 3 with a 60-yarder. That man owes nobody a thing.

Some days on the lake you sit eight hours and catch nothing. This was one of those days, except we had a fish on the hook with 19 seconds left. I'll get over it by Thursday, maybe.

We're 5-3, 3-2 in the Big Ten. UCLA comes to Huntington Bank Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 7, and they're bringing an unbeaten record into November in Minneapolis. Bring the good coat. Ski-U-Mah.

articles.title: BYU vs Arizona State: Cougars Sack Sun Devils Six Times, Win 27-20
articles.matchup: Final: BYU (7-1) 27, Arizona State (4-4) 20, Sat., Oct. 31, LaVell Edwards Stadium, Provo. Next: at Utah, Sat., Nov. 7, Rice-Eccles Stadium, Salt Lake City
articles.text:
BYU 27, Arizona State 20. On Halloween afternoon, Center Street in Downtown Provo was handing out treats from 3 to 6 p.m., and at LaVell Edwards Stadium, 63,332 of us were handing out sacks. Six of them. The Cougars are 7-1, and oh my heck, they made us earn every bit of it.

The defense set the tone right away. Arizona State's quarterback fumbled on the third snap of the game, Isaiah Glasker pounced on it at the Sun Devil 29, and on that drive Sione Moa scooped up our own fumble inside the 1 and carried it in for a touchdown nobody drew up. Faletau Satuala blocked a field goal, and the Sun Devils needed a penalty to get three points out of that trip. Matthias Dunn hit from 28, and Bear Bachmeier threaded a 13-yard touchdown to Kyler Kasper for a 17-3 lead.

Then the third quarter took the trail I never ride. Arizona State scored twice, a Kasper fumble flipped field position, and it was 17-17 with 1:15 left in the quarter. My trail map had a big red X on it.

Here is where this team showed me something. Dunn drilled a 45-yarder for a 20-17 lead. Then we went 95 yards in 11 plays. Bachmeier hit Legend Glasker for 53 yards, converted two fourth downs, and Moa plowed in from a yard out with 2:09 left. Moa's second touchdown is the one I'll be telling my grandkids about.

Bachmeier went 19 of 30 for 236 yards and a touchdown. Walker Lyons caught five balls and Glasker finished with 87 yards on four grabs. Six different Cougars got a sack: Isaiah Glasker, Cade Uluave, Nusi Taumoepeau, Ace Kaufusi, Miles Hall and Bodie Schoonover. Satuala led us with nine tackles. I'd love to see more than 47 rushing yards next time, but I am not returning this win.

Why did the Cougar defense skip the haunted house? It already had six scares of its own. I'll show myself out.

We're 7-1, 4-1 in the Big 12 and 5-0 at home. Next up, the big one: at Utah, Saturday, Nov. 7, at Rice-Eccles Stadium in Salt Lake City. Rise and shout.

articles.title: Arizona State vs BYU: Sun Devils Rally, Fall Late in Provo 27-20
articles.matchup: Final: BYU (7-1) 27, Arizona State (4-4) 20, Sat., Oct. 31, LaVell Edwards Stadium, Provo. Next: vs. Colorado, Sat., Nov. 7, Mountain America Stadium, Tempe
articles.text:
BYU 27, Arizona State 20, and the Sun Devils dragged No. 8 BYU into a fourth quarter it did not want. Back in Tempe, the trombones, tubas and euphoniums of the Happy How-Low-Ween Concert were booked for Nelson Fine Arts Plaza at 5 p.m., and I wanted that brass playing a victory song. It played a sad one instead, and it played it loud.

Jake Fette made his first career start in Provo, and the first quarter was rough. He fumbled on the third snap of our opening drive, and BYU scored when Sione Moa scooped up a Cougar fumble at the goal and took it in. In the second quarter, Faletau Satuala blocked a field goal, we got new life on a Cougar personal foul, and still settled for a 24-yarder from Carson Smith. Down 17-3 at the half, six sacks taken by the end of the day. Ouch.

Then the third quarter happened, and it was all maroon and gold. Fette led a 13-play, 81-yard march and hit Omarion Miller from 20 yards out. Owen Long punched the ball out of Kyler Kasper's hands, Adrian Wilson fell on it at the BYU 39, and we converted two fourth downs on the way to Fette's 1-yard touchdown throw to Anthony Miller. Seventeen all, with 1:15 left in the third, and 63,332 people in Provo got very quiet.

Cardae Mack was the engine all day: 123 rushing yards on 23 carries plus five catches for 47 more, 170 yards of pure Tempe toughness. Long finished with 10 tackles, and Montana Warren intercepted Bear Bachmeier right before the half. Smith hit both of his field goals, including a 44-yarder with 57 seconds left that pulled us within seven.

The honest film session hurts. BYU went 95 yards in 11 plays to put it away, Bachmeier found Legend Glasker for 53 on the big one, and Moa scored from a yard out with 2:09 left. Fette went 22 of 42 for 166 yards and two touchdowns with no interceptions, but we were 6 of 17 on third down, and that is the whole story.

So, a quick sip of water, a long exhale, and the truth: we won the third quarter 14-0 on the road against a top-10 team. That is a group with fight in it.

We're 4-4 and 2-3 in the Big 12. Colorado comes to Mountain America Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 7. Forks up.

articles.title: Georgia vs Florida: Dawgs Defense Takes Six Straight, Wins 27-8
articles.matchup: Final: Georgia (7-1) 27, Florida (5-3) 8, Sat., Oct. 31, Mercedes-Benz Stadium, Atlanta. Next: at Ole Miss, Sat., Nov. 7, Vaught-Hemingway Stadium, Oxford
articles.text:
Georgia 27, Florida 8, on Halloween in Atlanta, and that's six straight in this series for the Dawgs. Back in Athens, the 18th Wild Rumpus Parade stepped off at 8 p.m. outside Creature Comforts on W. Hancock Ave., and downtown partied into the night. So did our defense, about four hours earlier.

First time this rivalry ever came to Atlanta, and the set list opened with a skipped track: Peyton Woodring missed from 43 on our first drive. Then the defense dropped the needle. Ellis Robinson IV intercepted Aaron Philo's underhand flip, a roughing penalty on our punt handed us new life, and Nate Frazier went in from the 1 for a 7-0 lead.

Demello Jones intercepted Philo and brought it back 23 yards, and Woodring hit from 28. Bo Walker capped a 10-play, 81-yard drive with a 1-yard run. Then the headliner: Quintavius Johnson sacked Tramell Jones Jr., the ball came out, and Chris Cole ran it 66 yards to the house with 29 seconds left in the half. 24-0. That's the closer you save for the encore, and we played it before intermission.

The second half was a B-side, I'll admit it. Talyn Taylor lost a fumble, and Florida turned it into eight points. But Braylon Conley intercepted Jones in the end zone with 4:50 left in the third to keep Florida off the board, and Woodring added a 21-yarder with 3:34 left to close it at 27-8.

Our ground game ran 42 times for 217 yards. Frazier had 67 and a touchdown, Dwight Phillips Jr. had 67 with a 26-yard burst, and Gunner Stockton went 13 of 23 for 101 while running for 45 more. Cole led us with nine tackles and added a sack on top of the touchdown. Raylen Wilson had eight. Four takeaways turned into 17 points, and Florida ran for 48 yards on 28 carries.

Album review: four takeaways, four sacks, one fumble-return encore. Ten out of ten. Play it loud on the drive home.

We're 7-1, 5-1 in the SEC. Next up is Ole Miss on Saturday, Nov. 7, at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium in Oxford. Pack the headphones and bring the defense. Go Dawgs.

articles.title: Florida vs Georgia: Gators Give Away Four Turnovers, Fall 27-8
articles.matchup: Final: Georgia (7-1) 27, Florida (5-3) 8, Sat., Oct. 31, Mercedes-Benz Stadium, Atlanta. Next: vs. Oklahoma, Sat., Nov. 7, Ben Hill Griffin Stadium, Gainesville
articles.text:
Georgia 27, Florida 8, on Halloween afternoon in Atlanta, and the Reptile Index has a new entry for the Bulldogs: apex predator, feeds on turnovers. Back home in Gainesville, Carson Springs Wildlife Foundation ran its Halloween Safari Drive-Thru from 1 to 3 that afternoon, rare animals and spooky displays before kickoff. That was the last thing all day that behaved the way it was supposed to.

This was the first time our rivalry game was ever played in Atlanta, and we spent the first half handing Georgia the keys. Aaron Philo, back under center, got chased on our opening drive and flipped the ball underhand right to Ellis Robinson IV. A roughing penalty on the punt kept Georgia alive, and Nate Frazier went in from the 1. In the second quarter a ball bounced off our receiver's hands to Demello Jones, and Peyton Woodring made it 10-0.

Tramell Jones Jr. came in and Georgia kept feeding. Bo Walker scored from the 1 to make it 17-0. Then, with 29 seconds left before the break, Quintavius Johnson sacked Jones, the ball came loose, and Chris Cole ran it back 66 yards. 24-0 at the half. In herpetology terms, that is a monitor lizard cleaning out the whole nest.

We had our shot in the third. Jones drove us to the Georgia 3, and Braylon Conley intercepted him in the end zone with 4:50 left. DJ Coleman punched the ball loose from Talyn Taylor early in the fourth, Myles Graham recovered, and Jones finally put us on the board with a 2-yard run and a two-point conversion with 6:59 to go. Woodring answered with a 21-yard field goal.

The honest numbers: Jones went 18 of 25 for 172 yards. Bailey Stockton caught eight balls for 76 yards. Alec Clark averaged 51.3 yards on four punts. Coleman made eight tackles, Graham seven, and Emmanuel Oyebadejo got a sack. But we turned it over four times, ran for 48 yards on 28 carries, and Jadan Baugh, an Atlanta native, got 38 on 17. Georgia ran for 217. Eight penalties for 78 yards finished the job.

The Bulldogs earned it, and I'm saying that through clenched teeth. The Reptile Index files them as a species that lives off other animals' mistakes, and we served them a buffet.

We're 5-3, 3-3 in the SEC. Oklahoma comes to Ben Hill Griffin Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 7, the first time the Sooners have ever played in the Swamp. Gainesville gets its team back, and the Swamp gets its noise back. Go Gators.

articles.title: Oklahoma vs South Carolina: Sooners Fall on Homecoming, 42-25
articles.matchup: Final: South Carolina (5-3) 42, Oklahoma (4-4) 25, Sat., Oct. 31, Memorial Stadium (Norman, OK), Norman. Next: at Florida, Sat., Nov. 7, Ben Hill Griffin Stadium, Gainesville
articles.text:
South Carolina 42, Oklahoma 25, and it stings worse because it happened on homecoming. Saturday was also Native American Heritage Appreciation Day in Norman, with the Osage Nation teaming up with OU Football for the Halloween game, and Owen Field deserved a better show from the home side than the one we put on.

The day began right. The Sooner Schooner led the Walk of Champions, the Student-Athlete Advisory Committee handed out candy at Party at the Palace, and I hollered at the team buses until my voice cracked. Then Sellers ran 15 yards for a touchdown on South Carolina's second drive, and our first four drives all ended in punts.

Kip Lewis gave this town a jolt early in the second quarter. He jumped a Sellers throw and rumbled 30 yards for a touchdown, 7-7, and the whole stadium shook. It did not last. South Carolina scored touchdowns on its next three drives, including an 84-yard strike on third-and-12, and Tate Sandell's 52-yard field goal was our only reply. It was 28-10 at the break.

Michael Boganowski intercepted Sellers at our 18 in the third quarter, and that is the fight I want from this defense every snap. But Sellers ran in from 11 yards out late in the third, and after John Mateer found Ivan Carreon for a 34-yard touchdown to open the fourth, South Carolina answered with a 79-yard bomb three plays later. That one hurt all the way down to my boots.

Mateer finished 26 of 43 for 244 yards and two touchdown throws, both to Carreon, who caught five balls for 88 yards. The second score, from 10 yards out with 2:59 left, made it 42-25. Both two-point tries failed. Sandell also hit from 34. Markel Ford intercepted a South Carolina throw in the end zone late, and we did not turn it over once all day.

Here is the honest part, rodeo rules: you cannot win a barrel race if the horse will not turn. South Carolina ran for 212 yards, piled up 521 and converted 8 of 14 third downs. We ran for 115 on 31 carries and went 7 of 16 on third down. Owen Heinecke and Courtland Guillory made 10 tackles apiece and never quit.

We're 4-4, 2-3 in the SEC and 2-2 at home. Next is a trip to Florida on Saturday, Nov. 7, at Ben Hill Griffin Stadium in Gainesville. Chin up, Norman. We roll the Schooner again. Boomer! (Sooner!)

articles.title: South Carolina vs Oklahoma: Sellers Runs Wild in Norman 42-25
articles.matchup: Final: South Carolina (5-3) 42, Oklahoma (4-4) 25, Sat., Oct. 31, Memorial Stadium (Norman, OK), Norman. Next: vs. Texas A&M, Sat., Nov. 7, Williams-Brice Stadium, Columbia
articles.text:
South Carolina 42, Oklahoma 25, on Halloween in Norman, so somebody cue the music. Back home on Friday night, Finlay Park ran the Halloween Edition of Finlay Fridays with the Vinyl Junkies on stage, and Columbia warmed up the speakers. On Saturday, LaNorris Sellers turned them all the way up at Memorial Stadium.

The opening act came fast. Sellers took a no-huddle snap and ran 15 yards for a touchdown midway through the first quarter. Then came the plot twist nobody ordered: early in the second, Kip Lewis jumped a Sellers throw and returned it 30 yards for an Oklahoma score, 7-7. A lesser show folds right there. Ours answered with a six-play, 75-yard drive, and Christian Clark plowed in from a yard out.

Then the spotlight hit. On third-and-12 from our own 16, Sellers found DJ Black deep down the middle for an 84-yard touchdown, 21-7. After a Tate Sandell 52-yard field goal, Sellers marched us 75 yards in eight plays and hit Nyck Harbor from 8 yards out with 16 seconds left in the half. It was 28-10 at the break, and I was standing on a chair.

In the third quarter, Sellers capped a 12-play, 75-yard march with an 11-yard touchdown run, 35-10. Oklahoma scored to open the fourth, and three plays later Sellers dropped a 79-yard strike on Mazeo Bennett Jr. to make it 42-16. Somewhere in Columbia, Sandstorm cranked up on its own.

Sellers finished 19 of 24 for 301 yards and three touchdown throws, plus 96 rushing yards and two more scores on 13 carries. That is five touchdowns from one man at somebody else's homecoming. Bennett caught four balls for 107 yards. We piled up 521 yards, 212 of them on the ground, and converted 8 of 14 third downs.

The defense earned its own curtain call. Fred Johnson made 11 tackles and a sack, Tomiwa Durojaiye added a sack, and Troy Pikes and Anthony Addison split another. Oklahoma ran for 115 yards on 31 tries. Honest review, because I keep receipts: Sellers threw two interceptions, Cutter Woods threw one late, and we drew nine flags for 90 yards. That gets fixed before the next show.

Shane Beamer coached in Norman from 2018 through 2020, and he came back on Halloween and won in that building. We're 5-3, 3-3 in the SEC and 2-1 on the road. Texas A&M comes to Williams-Brice Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 7. Lights down. Music up. Forever to thee.

articles.title: Georgia Southern vs App State: White Out Defense Wins 19-3
articles.matchup: Final: Georgia Southern (4-4) 19, App State (5-3) 3, Sat., Oct. 31, Allen E. Paulson Stadium, Statesboro. Next: vs. Marshall, Sat., Nov. 7, Allen E. Paulson Stadium, Statesboro (Homecoming)
articles.text:
Georgia Southern 19, App State 3, on Erk Russell's 100th birthday celebration at a White Out Paulson Stadium, and it was Erk's kind of night. The Eagles unveiled Eagle Legends busts of Tracy Ham, Adrian Peterson and Paul Johnson at Parrish-Scoggins Plaza at 3 p.m., the "One More Time" exhibit sat on the Bishop Fieldhouse Patio, and the costume contest had a Best Dressed as Erk Russell category. Then our defense played the kind of football Erk built this place on.

It started on App's third snap. Brandon Tyson hurried Malachi Singleton, and Chace Calicut intercepted him at our 32. Max Johnson and the offense went to work with a 14-play, 73-yard drive. Weston Bryan converted a fourth-and-1 at the App 6, and Tripp Bryant kicked a 25-yarder. Next time out, Bryan threw 7 yards to Josh Dallas on fourth-and-1, and Taeo Todd ran it in from 5, 10-0.

App got a 51-yard kickoff return and a missed 35-yarder, and James London hit from 33 at the end of the half, 10-3. That was all the Mountaineers got. Bryant kicked a 35-yarder for 13-3, then a 34-yarder at the end of a 14-play drive that burned 7:25 off the clock, 16-3.

articles.matchup: Final: Georgia Southern (4-4) 19, App State (5-3) 3, Sat., Oct. 31, Allen E. Paulson Stadium, Statesboro. Next: vs. Georgia State, Sat., Nov. 7, Kidd Brewer Stadium, Boone
articles.text:
Georgia Southern 19, App State 3, and Halloween in Statesboro turned into a long, cold climb with no summit. Back home, Boone BOO! filled King Street from 4 to 6:30 p.m., with the costume contest at 5 in front of the Jones House. Kickoff came at 6:30, right as the last kids headed home. Downtown Boone had the better night.

It went sideways on the third snap. Malachi Singleton got hurried by Brandon Tyson and Chace Calicut intercepted him at the Georgia Southern 32. Sam Pickett III ripped off a 45-yard catch on the next drive, but we punted. The Eagles answered with a 14-play, 73-yard grind that ended in a Tripp Bryant field goal, then a 12-play, 81-yard march that ended with a Taeo Todd 5-yard run, 10-0.

We had our chances. Ja'Quez Cross brought a kickoff back 51 yards to the Georgia Southern 40, and James London missed from 35. Before the half, Singleton converted a fourth-and-1 to Dillon Galloway, found Pickett for 10, and London hit from 33 with three seconds left, 10-3. That was the last time we scored.

The second half was a slow whittle down to nothing. Bryant kicked from 35 to make it 13-3 and from 34 to make it 16-3, and that second kick capped a 14-play drive that ate 7:25. On our next series, Singleton got sacked on back-to-back snaps, the second by Ethan Johnson for 10 yards. Then Singleton coughed up the ball at our 29, Anthony Bynum fell on it, and Bryant hit from 48, 19-3. We drove 75 yards in five plays to the Georgia Southern 2 and watched Singleton get intercepted in the end zone at 3:02.

Singleton went 15 of 28 for 215 yards with two interceptions and finished with minus-13 rushing yards. Pickett caught four balls for 86 yards, and Chris Lofton caught five for 82. Colton Phares made 12 tackles, and Juan Berchal had 10 with two throws broken up. Honest trail report: we ran for 6 yards on 16 carries, had the ball for 16:06 against 43:54, went 2 of 9 on third down and turned it over three times.

We're 5-3 and 2-2 in the Sun Belt. Georgia State comes to Kidd Brewer Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 7. Come home to the mountain and get loud. Go Apps.

articles.title: San Diego State vs Washington State: Kinnard Runs Aztecs 26-20
articles.matchup: Final: San Diego State (4-5) 26, Washington State (1-8) 20, Sat., Oct. 31, Snapdragon Stadium, San Diego. Next: vs. Utah State, Sat., Nov. 14, Snapdragon Stadium, San Diego
articles.text:
San Diego State 26, Washington State 20, on Halloween at Snapdragon Stadium, and the Aztecs gave the whole River Park a treat. The River Park Block Party opened at 11 a.m., kids paraded around the Yellow Lot right after the Warrior Walk, our student-athletes handed out candy, and the students got the green light to wear costumes to the game. Then Javion Kinnard put on his work boots.

Kinnard set the tone early. After our defense stuffed the Cougars on fourth-and-1 at our 21, he capped an eight-play, 79-yard drive with a 9-yard touchdown run. Washington State tied it, and Kinnard went right back to work, finishing an 11-play, 79-yard march from 10 yards out, 14-7. The Cougars tied it again, so Cooper DiLeva drilled a 36-yarder. Before the half, Sione Hala hurried Owen Eshelman and Kai Wallin jumped the throw at our 28. Gnarly. 17-14 at the break.

The third quarter turned into a big swell for the defense. Stone Saunders got intercepted on our first series, and the Cougars had a short field. A Cougar personal foul pushed them back 15 yards, they gained six on four plays, Djibril Rahman hurried Eshelman on fourth-and-4, and the throw fell incomplete. DiLeva banged home a 45-yarder, 20-14. Krishna Clay then dropped Eshelman for a 14-yard loss, and the 53-yard try that followed sailed no good.

Here's the wave I'll be talking about at Ocean Beach for a month. Fourth-and-goal at the Cougar 2, a 15-play drive that ate 7:11, and Bert Emanuel Jr. took the ball and threw a touchdown to Jackson Ford, 26-14. Washington State answered, missed the extra point, and got one last shot. On fourth-and-10 from their 48 with 38 seconds left, Mike Lindsay broke up the deep throw. Paddle in, dudes.

Lucky Sutton ran 18 times for 115 yards, with a 46-yard burst. Kinnard added 87 yards and both rushing scores on 17 carries. We ran for 202 yards on 37 tries. Tainoa Lave made nine tackles, Clay had 1.5 sacks, and the defense sacked Eshelman three times and stopped all three Cougar fourth-down tries. Honest surf report: Saunders went 12 of 21 for 102 yards with an interception, Eshelman threw for 299 on us, and the Cougars converted 9 of 14 third downs. That water gets cleaned up.

We're 4-5, 3-2 in the Pac-12 and 4-1 at Snapdragon. After the open week, Utah State comes to Snapdragon Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 14. Wax the board. Go Aztecs.

articles.title: Washington State vs San Diego State: Cougars Fall Short 26-20
articles.matchup: Final: San Diego State (4-5) 26, Washington State (1-8) 20, Sat., Oct. 31, Snapdragon Stadium, San Diego. Next: vs. Colorado State, Sat., Nov. 14, Martin Stadium, Pullman
articles.text:
San Diego State 26, Washington State 20, and the Aztecs pulled the one real Halloween trick of the night. Back home on Saturday afternoon, the Downtown Pullman Association ran its trick-or-treat from 3 to 6 p.m., and kickoff at Snapdragon Stadium landed right in the middle of it. Main Street handed out the candy. Our Cougars came home with a bag of rocks.

We came out hungry. The opening drive went 11 plays into Aztec territory before Kirby Vorhees got stopped on fourth-and-1 at their 21. Javion Kinnard ran in from 9, and Owen Eshelman answered with a 4-yard keeper, 7-7. Kinnard scored again from 10, and Vorhees bulled in from 2 to finish a 12-play drive, 14-14. Then Kai Wallin intercepted Eshelman at the Aztec 28, Cooper DiLeva kicked a 36-yarder, and it was 17-14 at the half.

The third quarter is where this crop got hailed on. Jaylen Thomas intercepted Stone Saunders on the first series of the half, but a personal foul on our side moved the ball back 15 yards, we managed six yards in four plays, and we turned it over on downs at their 30. DiLeva hit from 45, 20-14. Our next drive ran 13 plays, then a 14-yard sack shoved us back to their 35, and Jack Stevens missed from 53.

Then came the gut punch. On fourth-and-goal at our 2, Bert Emanuel Jr. took the ball and threw a touchdown to Jackson Ford, 26-14, finishing a 15-play march that burned 7:11. We fought back. Eshelman found Daniel Blood for 43 yards, Blood lost the ball at the 10 and fell on it himself at the 4, and Eshelman ran in from 2. The extra point failed, so the last drive needed a touchdown, not a kick. On fourth-and-10 from our 48 with 38 seconds left, his deep throw for Branden Ganashamoorthy was broken up.

Eshelman went 30 of 42 for 299 yards and ran for both of his touchdowns. Blood caught eight balls for 105 yards. Keith Brown made 11 tackles, and Linus Zunk had 2.5 tackles for loss. We outgained them 367 yards to 306, held the ball for 33:05 and converted 9 of 14 third downs. Honest harvest report: we went 0 for 3 on fourth down, ran for 68 yards on 30 carries, and gave up 202 on the ground, 115 of them to Lucky Sutton.

We're 1-8, 0-5 in the Pac-12 and 0-5 on the road. This tape is not going in the shoebox. After the open week, Colorado State comes to Martin Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 14. Fly Ol' Crimson high, Pullman. Go Cougs.

articles.title: Texas vs Mississippi State: Biles and the Defense Rule 31-3
articles.matchup: Final: Texas (6-2) 31, Mississippi State (4-4) 3, Sat., Oct. 31, DKR-Texas Memorial Stadium, Austin. Next: at Missouri, Sat., Nov. 7, Memorial Stadium, Columbia
articles.text:
Texas 31, Mississippi State 3. As forecast. Austin shut Sixth Street to cars for Halloween night and Pumpkin Nights ran its final night in town, but the best show in the city was at DKR, where our defense ran the Bulldog offense through a hostile takeover.

The first acquisition closed fast. On third-and-9, Arch Manning hit Cam Coleman for 47 yards, then found him again for a 14-yard touchdown. Four plays, 62 yards, 7-0.

Then the defense took over the boardroom. Mississippi State drove 12 plays to our 18 and walked away with a missed 38-yarder. Gianni Spetic drilled a 45-yarder for 10-0. With 1:13 left in the half, Rasheem Biles sacked AJ Swann at our 39, the ball came loose, and Maraad Watson scooped it up and ran 61 yards for a touchdown. 17-0 at the break. That is how you merge two departments into one end zone.

The second half had one messy page of paperwork. Manning got sacked twice on one series and lost the ball at our 28, and the Bulldogs turned it into a 30-yard field goal. Our response: seven plays, 75 yards, a 37-yard strike to open it and a 4-yard touchdown throw to Raleek Brown, 24-3. Early in the fourth, the defense stopped a fourth-and-2 at our 40. Then on third-and-1, Manning hit Emmett Mosley V deep for a 42-yard touchdown. 31-3. Close the books.

Caro Bucks report. Biles: three sacks, four tackles for loss, eight tackles, top of the portfolio. Watson: a defensive touchdown, and he just earned a corner office. Manning went 16 of 20 for 220 yards and three touchdowns, Mosley caught four balls for 98 yards, and Jelani McDonald led us with nine tackles. Seven sacks as a team, and the Bulldogs finished with 187 yards and 68 on the ground. The audit flags are real: 60 rushing yards on 32 carries, five sacks allowed and a lost fumble. That's tomorrow's board-meeting agenda.

We're 6-2, 3-2 in the SEC and 5-1 at DKR. Next up, a trip to Missouri on Saturday, Nov. 7. Hook 'em.

articles.text:
Texas 31, Mississippi State 3, and the cowbell went in the sock before halftime. Back home, the Starkville Community Trick-or-Treat Map wrapped up on Halloween, with Bulldog Burger, Mugshots and Bluto's among the six stops handing out free candy. Starkville gave away treats all day. Austin gave us seven sacks.

It went sideways on the fourth snap. On third-and-9, Arch Manning found Cam Coleman for 47 yards, then hit him for a 14-yard touchdown. Four plays, 62 yards, 7-0 with 12:59 still left in the first quarter.

We had our chances in the first half and let them walk out of the hen house. A 12-play drive reached their 18, Anthony Evans III lost six yards on a run, and Kyle Ferrie missed from 38. Gianni Spetic made his from 45. Then, with 1:13 left before the break, Rasheem Biles sacked AJ Swann at the Texas 39, the ball squirted loose, and Maraad Watson scooped it and ran 61 yards for a touchdown. 17-0. I wrote that one on a receipt and folded it very small.

Our defense gave us a pulse in the third. Jaray Bledsoe sacked Manning, and Zakari Tillman fell on the loose ball at the Texas 28. Biles then dropped Evans for a 15-yard loss, and we settled for Ferrie's 30-yarder, 17-3. Texas answered with a seven-play, 75-yard drive capped by Manning's 4-yard touchdown throw to Raleek Brown. Early in the fourth we went for it on fourth-and-2 at their 40, and Parker Puckett's throw to Evans fell incomplete. Manning hit Emmett Mosley V for a 42-yard touchdown on third-and-1, 31-3.

Here's what the feed-store receipt says. Our defense held Texas to 60 rushing yards on 32 carries and sacked Manning five times. Tillman had a sack, 2.5 tackles for loss and that fumble recovery, and Fatt Forrest made seven tackles. We held the ball 32:28. Now the honest half of the receipt: 187 yards of offense, 68 rushing yards on 41 carries, 6 of 18 on third down, seven sacks allowed. Swann went 12 of 15 for 97 yards, Puckett 3 of 10 for 22, and Fluff Bothwell ran 17 times for 49. Marquis Johnson caught six balls for 61 yards. You can't grow a crop on 187 yards.

We're 4-4 and 2-4 in the SEC. Vanderbilt comes to Davis Wade Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 7, and the cowbell stays in the sock until then. Hail State.
