It went sideways on the fourth snap. On third-and-9, Arch Manning found Cam Coleman for 47 yards, then hit him for a 14-yard touchdown. Four plays, 62 yards, 7-0 with 12:59 still left in the first quarter.

We had our chances in the first half and let them walk out of the hen house. A 12-play drive reached their 18, Anthony Evans III lost six yards on a run, and Kyle Ferrie missed from 38. Gianni Spetic made his from 45. Then, with 1:13 left before the break, Rasheem Biles sacked AJ Swann at the Texas 39, the ball squirted loose, and Maraad Watson scooped it and ran 61 yards for a touchdown. 17-0. I wrote that one on a receipt and folded it very small.

Our defense gave us a pulse in the third. Jaray Bledsoe sacked Manning, and Zakari Tillman fell on the loose ball at the Texas 28. Biles then dropped Evans for a 15-yard loss, and we settled for Ferrie's 30-yarder, 17-3. Texas answered with a seven-play, 75-yard drive capped by Manning's 4-yard touchdown throw to Raleek Brown. Early in the fourth we went for it on fourth-and-2 at their 40, and Parker Puckett's throw to Evans fell incomplete. Manning hit Emmett Mosley V for a 42-yard touchdown on third-and-1, 31-3.

Here's what the feed-store receipt says. Our defense held Texas to 60 rushing yards on 32 carries and sacked Manning five times. Tillman had a sack, 2.5 tackles for loss and that fumble recovery, and Fatt Forrest made seven tackles. We held the ball 32:28. Now the honest half of the receipt: 187 yards of offense, 68 rushing yards on 41 carries, 6 of 18 on third down, seven sacks allowed. Swann went 12 of 15 for 97 yards, Puckett 3 of 10 for 22, and Fluff Bothwell ran 17 times for 49. Marquis Johnson caught six balls for 61 yards. You can't grow a crop on 187 yards.
We're 4-4 and 2-4 in the SEC. Vanderbilt comes to Davis Wade Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 7, and the cowbell stays in the sock until then. Hail State.

articles.title: Arkansas vs Missouri: Hogs Give It Away on Halloween, 34-10
articles.matchup: Final: Missouri (6-2) 34, Arkansas (3-5) 10, Sat., Oct. 31, Donald W. Reynolds Razorback Stadium, Fayetteville. Next: at Auburn, Sat., Nov. 7, Jordan-Hare Stadium, Auburn
articles.text:
Missouri 34, Arkansas 10, and it hurts to write it on the first Halloween on the Hill since 2015. Woooo, Pig. The 105th Homecoming Week ended with trunk-or-treating in the tailgate lots, a Hog Walk at Maple and Razorback, a trick-or-treat trailgating parade at 5:45 and a halftime laser show. The Hill brought the party. We brought four turnovers.

Hog Call, then the hard stat: four giveaways, 24 Missouri points. KJ Jackson got intercepted by Trajen Greco on our third drive, and Missouri kicked a field goal. Next time out, a snap got away from Cam Settles, rolled into our end zone, and Missouri's Darris Smith fell on it, 10-0. After a 53-yard field goal made it 13-0, Max Gilbert's 52-yard try came up empty.

We found some fight before the half. Jackson capped an eight-play, 52-yard drive with a 2-yard keeper with 41 seconds left, 13-7, and the place was rocking. Then Missouri went 75 yards to open the third, and on our very next snap, Jackson got stripped and Missouri recovered at our 45. Jamal Roberts scored from 2 three plays later, 27-7.

The drive I'll tell my science class about Monday: 20 plays, 62 yards, 9:51. Antonio Jordan caught a 25-yard touchdown that came back on a penalty, and Settles scored from the 1 before a chop block wiped that off too. We settled for a 32-yarder from Gilbert, 27-10. Bradley Shaw recovered a Roberts fumble at our 16, and we gave it right back two plays later when Jordan was stripped at our 33. Missouri scored four plays after that, 34-10.

Jackson completed 20 of 34 throws for 229 yards and ran for our only touchdown. Jordan caught seven balls for 106 yards with a long of 37, and CJ Brown caught four for 37. Shaw made nine tackles and broke up two throws, Joker Johnson made eight with a tackle for loss, and Christian Harrison made seven. Our defense held Missouri to 179 yards through the air.

Honest lab report: 59 rushing yards on 36 carries, 8 of 17 on third down, a turnover on downs late, and seven penalties for 85 yards. We're 3-5 and 1-4 in the SEC, and we head to Auburn's Jordan-Hare Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 7. Call the Hogs anyway. Woooo, Pig, Sooie.

articles.title: Missouri vs Arkansas: Tigers Feast on Turnovers, Win 34-10
articles.matchup: Final: Missouri (6-2) 34, Arkansas (3-5) 10, Sat., Oct. 31, Donald W. Reynolds Razorback Stadium, Fayetteville. Next: vs. Texas, Sat., Nov. 7, Memorial Stadium, Columbia
articles.text:
Missouri 34, Arkansas 10, and breaking news from Fayetteville: the Tigers took the ball away four times and turned every one of those takeaways into points on Halloween night. Back in Columbia, the day started at 11 a.m. at the Missouri Theatre on South Ninth Street, where the Missouri Symphony played its Spooktacular family concert for kids in costume. By 6:45 Central, the only thing spooking anybody was our defense.

It started early. Trajen Greco intercepted KJ Jackson and brought it back 22 yards to the Arkansas 43, and Blake Craig kicked a 31-yarder. On Arkansas' next possession, a snap got away from Cam Settles, the ball rolled into the end zone, and Darris Smith fell on it for a touchdown, 10-0. Craig then capped a 16-play drive that chewed 8:14 with a 53-yard field goal, 13-0.

Arkansas got a 2-yard Jackson run with 41 seconds left in the half, 13-7, and that's as close as it got. We came out of the break and went 75 yards in eight plays, finished by Austin Simmons hitting Donovan Olugbode from 15 yards out, 20-7. On the very next snap, Nicholas Rodriguez forced a Jackson fumble and Santana Banner recovered at the Arkansas 45. On the third play after that, Jamal Roberts walked in from 2, 27-7. Breaking news, delivered live: that's two scores in 66 seconds.

The Hogs answered with a 20-play drive that ate 9:51, and our defense held them to a 32-yard field goal after two Arkansas touchdowns came back on penalties. Roberts fumbled at the Arkansas 16 midway through the fourth, but two plays into the next Arkansas drive, Dante McClellan forced a fumble right back, Jahlil Florence recovered at the 33, and Simmons found Roberts for a 10-yard score four plays later, 34-10.

Simmons completed 20 of 31 throws for 179 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions. Roberts ran for 138 yards on 23 carries with a 43-yard burst and caught three balls for 20 yards. Cayden Lee caught six for 78, Ahmad Hardy ripped off a 37-yarder among his three carries, and Craig went 2 for 2 and scored 10 points. Rodriguez and Banner each made nine tackles, and Greco added eight. We held Arkansas to 59 rushing yards on 36 carries.

Honest copy desk: nine penalties for 80 yards, 6 of 13 on third down and a lost fumble deep in Arkansas territory. Clean that up before Texas comes to Memorial Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 7. We're 6-2 and 3-2 in the SEC. M-I-Z.

articles.title: Florida State vs Clemson: Four Turnovers Sink Seminoles 36-24
articles.matchup: Final: Clemson (5-3) 36, Florida State (3-5) 24, Sat., Oct. 31, Doak Campbell Stadium, Tallahassee. Next: at Boston College, Sat., Nov. 7, Alumni Stadium (Chestnut Hill, MA), Chestnut Hill
articles.text:
Clemson 36, Florida State 24. The record will show that Doak Campbell Stadium did its part. Florida State rolled out Operation Garnet Storm for Halloween night, with festivities on Langford Green from 3 p.m., a salute to Seminoles legend Peter Warrick, the program's first-ever drone show and a stadium light show at the start of the fourth quarter. The lights came on, and so did our offense. Too late, but it came.

Let the minutes reflect the first three quarters. We trailed 29-10 after Nolan Hauser's fifth field goal early in the fourth. Ashton Daniels threw three interceptions, two to Elliot Washington II and one to Jerome Carter III, and fumbled at the Clemson 20 after a 10-yard run in the third quarter. Four turnovers. We went 1 of 10 on third down and ran for 65 yards. That bill dies in committee every time.

Then the floor opened. Daniels ran in from 13 and threw for the two-point conversion, 29-18. Next series, he found Jasen Lopez for 41 yards and a touchdown, and it was 29-24 with 5:30 left. Doak was shaking.

Motion to reconsider: denied. Tait Reynolds ran 79 yards for a touchdown on Clemson's next drive, and our last push ended when Washington intercepted Daniels in the end zone with 1:03 to go.

For the record, the playmakers showed up. Daniels threw for 350 yards on 21 of 33 with two touchdowns, and he ran for one. Micahi Danzy caught four balls for 108 yards, including a 46-yard touchdown in the first quarter. Jayvan Boggs had two catches for 64. CJ Richard Jr. made 13 tackles, Chris Jones made 10, and Ashlynd Barker added nine. We out-gained Clemson 415 yards to 351. The turnovers decided it.

We are 3-5 and 1-4 in the ACC. Next is Boston College at Alumni Stadium in Chestnut Hill on Saturday, Nov. 7, at noon ET. My amendment for Chestnut Hill is simple: protect the football. All in favor? The ayes have it.

articles.title: Clemson vs Florida State: Tigers Take Four Turnovers, Win 36-24
articles.matchup: Final: Clemson (5-3) 36, Florida State (3-5) 24, Sat., Oct. 31, Doak Campbell Stadium, Tallahassee. Next: at Syracuse, Sat., Nov. 7, JMA Wireless Dome, Syracuse, N.Y.
articles.text:
Clemson 36, Florida State 24, and well, hey there, y'all, the Tigers celebrated a birthday in Tallahassee. Clemson played its very first football game on Oct. 31, 1896, a win over Furman in Greenville, back when Professor Walter Riggs coached a bunch of cadets who had barely seen a football. One hundred thirty years later to the day, on Halloween night, we won again. Some traditions keep.

This one was won by a kicker and a secondary, and I have the choreography notes to prove it. Nolan Hauser went 5 for 5 on field goals for 18 points, from 35, 35, 50, 46 and 49 yards. The 50-yarder came with two seconds left in the first half and sent us to the locker room up 23-10. My orange rain boots Darlene did a full high step in the living room.

Now the defense, my kind of routine. Jerome Carter III intercepted Ashton Daniels and brought it back 26 yards, and he had a sack too. Late in the half, Sammy Brown hurried Daniels into a throw that Elliot Washington II intercepted. In the third, Jahiem Lawson jumped on a Daniels fumble at our 16 to end a 75-yard Seminole drive. Then, with Florida State driving late, Washington intercepted Daniels again in the end zone. Four takeaways, zero giveaways. I'm naming that formation the Halloween Hold.

Tait Reynolds steered it all. He went 18 of 32 for 189 yards with touchdown throws to Christian Bentancur from 18 and Olsen Patt-Henry from 4. Then, with Florida State back within 29-24, he kept it and ran 79 yards for the touchdown that ended the argument with 3:17 left. Tyler Brown caught five balls for 74 yards, and Corey Myrick made 10 tackles. Will Heldt had a sack and 2.5 tackles for loss.

I'll say it plainly, because I don't decorate facts. We were 4 of 17 on third down, and we let a 29-10 lead shrink to five in the fourth quarter. Field goals look great in the box score only when they don't keep the other team in it. We have to finish drives.

We are 5-3 and 3-2 in the ACC. Next is Syracuse at the JMA Wireless Dome on Saturday, Nov. 7, at noon ET. Orange is ready for Orange. Go Tigers.

articles.title: Iowa State vs Oklahoma State: Konrardy Wins It at 0:00, 51-49
articles.matchup: Final: Iowa State (4-4) 51, Oklahoma State (5-3) 49, Sat., Oct. 31, Jack Trice Stadium, Ames. Next: at Baylor, Sat., Nov. 7, McLane Stadium, Waco
articles.text:
Iowa State 51, Oklahoma State 49, and the forecast for Halloween night in Ames verified right at 0:00: Kyle Konrardy from 34 yards, good, ballgame. The Cyclones wore black, the athletics department told all of us to Pack the Jack and Wear Black, and Jack Trice Stadium looked like one giant storm cell on the radar from the opening kick. Costumes were welcome, masks were not, so every face in the place got to show exactly how loud it was.

Aiden Flora was the low-pressure system nobody could escape. He opened the scoring with a 29-yard run on our first drive and finished with 221 yards on 29 carries. His biggest gust came with 11:08 left: Oklahoma State had just pulled to 38-35, and Flora went 75 yards on the very next snap, 45-35.

Jaylen Raynor completed 18 of 28 throws for 309 yards and three touchdowns and ran in another from 8 yards out. Jamal Polite Jr. caught six balls for 171 yards, including a 43-yard score in the second quarter just 79 seconds after Raynor's 2-yard touchdown throw tied it 14-14. Cameron Pettaway hauled in a 40-yarder late in the third, 38-28.

The defense didn't have a clean night, but it brought the hail when it counted. Beau Goodwin intercepted Drew Mestemaker at the Oklahoma State 35 with 4:35 left in a 45-42 game, and Konrardy turned it into a 29-yarder, 48-42. Before the half, Caleb Schmidt jumped on a muffed punt at the Oklahoma State 36, and Konrardy hit from 39 with seven seconds left for a 24-21 lead. Sullivan Schlimgen led us with eight tackles and broke up two throws.

Then the front stalled right over Ames. Oklahoma State went 75 yards in 12 plays and scored with 53 seconds left, 49-48. A 15-yard unsportsmanlike flag on the Cowboys pushed their kickoff back, Raynor found Polite deep for 33 yards to the Oklahoma State 30, and Flora carried three straight times to the 16. Two seconds left. Konrardy, 34 yards, straight through. He went 3 for 3 and scored 15 points.

Honest radar check: we allowed 533 yards, Mestemaker threw five touchdowns, and Caleb Hawkins ran for 194. We answered with 581 yards, 272 rushing, held the ball for 34:47 and turned it over once.

We're 4-4 and 2-3 in the Big 12. Next up is Baylor at McLane Stadium in Waco on Saturday, Nov. 7. Seven-day outlook for Ames: sunshine in every kitchen. Go Cyclones.

articles.title: Oklahoma State vs Iowa State: Bucked Off at the Horn, 51-49
articles.matchup: Final: Iowa State (4-4) 51, Oklahoma State (5-3) 49, Sat., Oct. 31, Jack Trice Stadium, Ames. Next: at Kansas State, Sat., Nov. 7, Bill Snyder Family Stadium, Manhattan
articles.text:
Iowa State 51, Oklahoma State 49, and the Cyclones got the last ride on Halloween night in Ames when Kyle Konrardy split it from 34 yards as the clock hit zero. Back home in Stillwater, families spent 4:30 to 6:30 at the free community trick-or-treat on South Husband Street, with the Humane Society of Stillwater and Our Daily Bread among the groups handing out candy. Kickoff in Ames came at 6 Central, and what followed went the full eight seconds about nine times over.

Our offense rode hard all night. Drew Mestemaker completed 27 of 42 throws for 323 yards and five touchdowns. articles.title: USC vs Ohio State: Trojans Take Down the No. 2 Buckeyes 30-18
articles.matchup: Final: USC (7-2) 30, Ohio State (6-2) 18, Sat., Oct. 31, Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum, Los Angeles. Next: at Indiana, Sat., Nov. 14, Memorial Stadium (Bloomington, IN), Bloomington
articles.text:
USC 30, Ohio State 18, and the Coliseum got a Halloween premiere worth every ticket. It was Trojan Family Weekend, the USC ticket office had sold out, and the No. 2 team in the country came to Exposition Park for the casting call. They didn't get the part. Roll credits.

The opening scene took 39 seconds. Jayden Maiava found Trent Mosley for 69 yards and a touchdown on our second snap. Mosley then took a punt back 44 yards, a Buckeye personal foul added 15, and Waymond Jordan finished the short drive with a 9-yard run, 14-3.

The middle act turned into a kicking duel, and our kickers never blinked. Ryon Sayeri drilled a 54-yarder. Ohio State drove 13 plays to our 1 after King Miller lost a fumble, a false start pushed them back, and they took three instead of seven. Caden Chittenden banged one through from 36 with a second left in the half, 20-9.

Then the plot twist. The Buckeyes had the ball at our 31 in the third quarter when Desman Stephens II stripped Isaiah West and Floyd Boucard fell on it. Maiava went deep to Mark Bowman for 70 yards, and Miller punched it in from 1, 27-9. Cue the strings.

The finale got tense. Luke Fahey's 1-yard touchdown throw to Jeremiah Smith made it 27-18 with 2:12 left, and the two-point try failed. We smothered the onside kick, Miller ground out five yards, and Chittenden kicked a 32-yarder, 30-18. Ohio State still marched to our 12. Chasen Johnson broke up a deep throw on that drive, and the last four throws into the end zone hit nothing but grass.

Maiava went 15 of 22 for 222 yards and a touchdown. Mosley caught five balls for 101 yards and Bowman three for 79. Miller ran 13 times for 78 yards, and he and Jordan each found the end zone. Deven Bryant made 11 tackles and Stephens added nine. Honest review: the Buckeyes outgained us 464 yards to 338, kept the ball 39:28 to our 20:32, and we converted 4 of 10 third downs. The defense bent all night and gave up one touchdown. That's a director's cut I'll rewatch.

We're 7-2, 4-2 in the Big Ten and 5-1 at the Coliseum. After the open week, we head to Indiana on Saturday, Nov. 14. Fight On!

articles.title: Ohio State vs USC: Field Goals Can't Save Buckeyes 30-18
articles.matchup: Final: USC (7-2) 30, Ohio State (6-2) 18, Sat., Oct. 31, Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum, Los Angeles. Next: vs. Oregon, Sat., Nov. 7, Ohio Stadium, Columbus
articles.text:
USC 30, Ohio State 18, and this one stings all the way back to High Street. Columbus already did its trick-or-treat on Thursday, and on Saturday our hockey team hosted That Place at Value City Arena at 5 p.m. Not saying the name. No buckeye candy fine tonight. Out at the Coliseum, the football team walked straight into a haunted house.

The fright started on the second snap. Jayden Maiava hit Trent Mosley for 69 yards and a touchdown 39 seconds in. Connor Hawkins answered with a 39-yarder, then our punt team got torched: Mosley returned one 44 yards, a personal foul on us tacked on 15 more, and Waymond Jordan ran in from 9. 14-3.

We kept moving the ball and kept kicking. Hawkins hit from 34, Ryon Sayeri answered from 54, and then Kenyatta Jackson Jr. punched the ball out of King Miller's arms and Earl Little Jr. fell on it at our 42. We drove 13 plays to their 1, a false start shoved us back, and Hawkins kicked from 23. Caden Chittenden's 36-yarder with one second left made it 20-9 at the half.

The back-breaker came in the third. We were at their 31 when Isaiah West caught a short throw, Desman Stephens II knocked it loose, and Floyd Boucard fell on it. Mark Bowman's 70-yard catch set up Miller's 1-yard run, 27-9. Hawkins went four for four from 47, and Luke Fahey capped a 13-play, 80-yard drive with a 1-yard touchdown throw to Jeremiah Smith with 2:12 left. The two-point try failed, USC grabbed the onside kick, and Chittenden kicked from 32.

One last shot. Fahey found Chris Henry Jr. for 39, Bo Jackson for 15 and Smith for 20 to reach their 12 with a minute to go. Four straight throws into the end zone fell incomplete, and the ball went over on downs with 36 seconds left.

My Route Tree segment on this one writes itself, and it's ugly. We outgained USC 464 yards to 338, held the ball 39:28 and piled up 25 first downs. Jackson ran 21 times for 121 yards, Smith caught 10 for 83, and Fahey went 21 of 38 for 260. But 11 penalties for 71 yards, 7 of 16 on third down, a fumble that turned into seven points, and four field goals where we needed touchdowns. You can't trade threes for sevens with a team that scores in two snaps.

We're 6-2 and 4-1 in the Big Ten. No time to sulk: Oregon comes to Ohio Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 7. The press box hallway is open, and I'm running routes until this tape makes sense. Go Bucks.

articles.title: North Carolina vs Miami: Tar Heels Push No. 1 to the Wire 38-35
articles.matchup: Final: Miami (8-0) 38, North Carolina (4-4) 35, Sat., Oct. 31, Kenan Stadium, Chapel Hill. Next: at UConn, Sat., Nov. 7, Pratt & Whitney Stadium, East Hartford, Conn.
articles.text:
Miami 38, North Carolina 35, and I'm going to hold my head high in this costume. Chapel Hill threw a real Halloween for the No. 1 team in the country: our team handed out candy on the walk to Kenan Stadium, children trick-or-treated on the concourse before kickoff, and thousands filled Franklin Street with no street closures. Then the Tar Heels handed Miami its closest finish of the season.

As a kinesiologist, let me describe the force Billy Edwards Jr. generated. He went 28 of 34 for 341 yards and four touchdowns with no interceptions. Jelani Thurman caught two of them, both from 8 yards. Jordan Shipp took a 16-yarder in the third quarter to give us a 21-17 lead. Then Demon June went in from a yard out with 11:46 left, and Kenan was rocking at 28-24. We went 8 of 11 on third down, which is how you keep a No. 1 offense on the bench.

Two moments broke my heart. Early in the fourth, Benjamin Hall ran 12 yards into the end zone and a holding flag brought it back. We still scored on that drive, but it took 16 plays and 8:28. Later, trailing 31-28, Edwards was sacked by Marquise Lightfoot at our 37, the ball came out, and Miami turned it into a 38-28 lead in six plays.

Did we quit? Absolutely not. Edwards moved 75 yards in 55 seconds and hit Trech Kekahuna for 15 yards to make it 38-35 with 1:38 to go. We went for the onside kick three times. Two were erased by our own offside flags, and Miami grabbed the third. Painful.

Credit where it's due, and I'll say it graciously: Darian Mensah went 22 of 29 for 274 yards with three touchdowns and zero turnovers, and Mark Fletcher Jr. scored three times. Our run game was the problem, 66 yards on 30 carries. Derek McDonald made 11 tackles and Peyton Seelmann had a sack. Kenton Dopson III added eight tackles.

We are 4-4 and 2-3 in the ACC, and 1-3 at home. Next is UConn at Pratt & Whitney Stadium in East Hartford on Saturday, Nov. 7, at noon ET. Carolina blue skies will return, and from the look of that fourth quarter, soon. And no, I will not be taking questions from anyone eight miles down the road.

articles.title: Miami vs North Carolina: Canes Escape Chapel Hill 38-35
articles.matchup: Final: Miami (8-0) 38, North Carolina (4-4) 35, Sat., Oct. 31, Kenan Stadium, Chapel Hill. Next: at Notre Dame, Sat., Nov. 7, Notre Dame Stadium, Notre Dame, Ind.
articles.text:
Miami 38, North Carolina 35, and we are 8-0. Back home, the Miami Canes packed Lost Boy Dry Goods on East Flagler Street downtown for the official game watch in orange and green, and I promise that room was louder than Kenan Stadium every time Carolina tied it or took the lead. That happened four times. On Halloween. Rude.

Let me be honest, because The Breeze does not do spin. This was a street fight. Carolina's quarterback Billy Edwards Jr. went 28 of 34 for 341 yards and four touchdowns, and the Tar Heels went 8 of 11 on third down. We trailed 21-17 in the third and 28-24 early in the fourth after Demon June punched one in from a yard out.

Then the grown-ups took over. Down 28-24 with 11:46 to go, Darian Mensah hit Malachi Toney for 31 yards on a no-huddle march, and Mark Fletcher Jr. bulled in from 2 for his second rushing score. 31-28. Next series, Marquise Lightfoot sacked Edwards, the ball came loose, and Justin Scott jumped on it at the Carolina 37. Six plays later Mensah found Toney from 9 yards out. 38-28. Lightfoot, se acabó, the quarterback hit the ground, adiós!

Carolina scored with 1:38 left to make it 38-35, then tried three onside kicks. Two got wiped out by offside flags, and Ezekiel Marcelin Jr. grabbed the third. Mensah knelt, and the sunglasses stayed in my pocket.

The numbers. Mensah went 22 of 29 for 274 yards, three touchdowns and zero interceptions. Toney caught seven balls for 75 yards and two scores, Cooper Barkate added four for 71, and Fletcher scored three times, two on the ground and once on a 31-yard catch. Lightfoot had two sacks. Chase Smith, JJ Dunnigan and Mohamed Toure each made nine tackles. We turned it over zero times and went 6 of 11 on third down.

Now the part I won't hide. We let them throw for 341 yards and gave up 35 points to a 4-4 team. The defense has to tighten up, because the road gets harder.

We are 8-0, 6-0 in the ACC and 4-0 away from home. Next is Notre Dame at Notre Dame Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 7, at 7:30 PM ET. Arms up, make the U. Swag!

articles.title: Memphis vs Army: Stokes Throws Four, Tigers Roll 49-22
articles.matchup: Final: Memphis (7-2) 49, Army (5-3) 22, Sat., Oct. 31, Simmons Bank Liberty Stadium, Memphis. Next: at South Florida, Thu., Nov. 12, Raymond James Stadium, Tampa
articles.text:
Memphis 49, Army 22, and Homecoming at Simmons Bank Liberty Stadium got the full band treatment. Hero Day honored the military, veterans and first responders, the crowd was asked to wear black, and Tiger Lane ran a Tailgate and Treat before kickoff. Our Tigers honored the cadets the right way: by playing their very best.

Marcus Stokes was the lead guitar all night. He completed 29 of 35 throws for 371 yards and four touchdowns, no interceptions. Jermane Hayes caught nine balls for 86 yards and scored twice from 13 and 5. Jemyri Davis caught touchdowns of 15 and 26. Hunter Tipton grabbed five for 86, including a 51-yarder. I hummed a riff after every score until my neighbor asked me to take a set break.

Now, I won't play loose with the sour notes. Davis lost a fumble in the second quarter, and Army tied it 14-14 four plays later. Their option ran for 320 yards, Godspower Nwawuihe went for 100, and Zach Mundell broke a 68-yarder that set up a score to make it 35-22. That defense needs to tune a few strings.

But listen to the groove we found once it was tied. Jaylin Carter punched in a 1-yard run, Stokes found Davis with 35 seconds left in the half, and Davis scored again in the third. Three straight touchdowns, 35-14. We converted 11 of 15 third downs and gained 554 yards with just two penalties.

And the fourth quarter had the strangest solo of the night. Stokes kept it from the 1, fumbled at the 4, grabbed his own ball and still got in for a touchdown and a 42-22 lead. Right after, Chauncey Logan Jr. intercepted Cale Hellums, and Carter's 3-yard run made it 49-22. Ellis Ellis Jr. intercepted the last throw at our 2 to close the show. Mike Montgomery led us with nine tackles.

On my soul scale, Army's alma mater gets a full respectful bow. The scoreboard gets an amen.

We're 7-2, 4-1 in the American and 5-0 at home. Next up, we head to South Florida on Thursday, Nov. 12, at Raymond James Stadium. Go Tigers Go!

Their option ran for 320 yards, Godspower Nwawuihe went for 100, and Zach Mundell broke a 68-yarder that set up a score to make it 35-22. That defense needs to tune a few strings.

But listen to the groove we found once it was tied. Jaylin Carter punched in a 1-yard run, Stokes found Davis with 35 seconds left in the half, and Davis scored again in the third. Three straight touchdowns, 35-14. We converted 11 of 15 third downs and gained 554 yards with just two penalties.

And the fourth quarter had the strangest solo of the night. Stokes kept it from the 1, fumbled at the 4, grabbed his own ball and still got in for a touchdown and a 42-22 lead. Right after, Chauncey Logan Jr. intercepted Cale Hellums, and Carter's 3-yard run made it 49-22. Ellis Ellis Jr. intercepted the last throw at our 2 to close the show. Mike Montgomery led us with nine tackles.
On my soul scale, Army's alma mater gets a full respectful bow. The scoreboard gets an amen.
We're 7-2, 4-1 in the American and 5-0 at home. Next up, we head to South Florida on Thursday, Nov. 12, at Raymond James Stadium. Go Tigers Go!

articles.matchup: Final: Memphis (7-2) 49, Army (5-3) 22, Sat., Oct. 31, Simmons Bank Liberty Stadium, Memphis. Next: vs. Air Force, Sat., Nov. 7, Michie Stadium, West Point
articles.text:
Memphis 49, Army 22. Filing this field report from the Mid-South with a heavy pen. On Friday night back at West Point, the post ran its Trunk-or-Treat in H-Lot by the PX and then showed Ghostbusters on the soccer field. Saturday in Memphis, nobody in our secondary knew who to call.

Status of the ground war: green. We ran 51 times for 320 yards and held the ball 31:55. Godspower Nwawuihe carried 19 times for 100 yards, broke a 34-yarder and scored from 5 out to tie it 7-7. After Noah Nixon punched the ball loose from Jemyri Davis and Kody Harris-Miller recovered it, Cale Hellums threw 8 yards to Samari Howard for a 14-14 tie in the second quarter. Right item, right place, right time.

Status of the air defense: red. Marcus Stokes completed 29 of 35 throws for 371 yards and four touchdowns, and Memphis converted 11 of 15 third downs. They scored 21 straight to go up 35-14. Jermane Hayes caught two touchdowns, Jemyri Davis caught two more, and Hunter Tipton took one short throw 51 yards to set up a score. You can't win a time-of-possession war when the other side needs two minutes to go 75 yards.

We did not quit. Zach Mundell broke a 68-yard run to the Memphis 5, Hellums kept it from 2, and the two-point try was good to make it 35-22. Then Memphis marched 92 yards, and Stokes fumbled at our 4, grabbed it right back and got into the end zone anyway. That's a report I'll log under "status unknown," because I can't explain it. Hellums was intercepted on the next series, and Bryson Luter was intercepted at the Memphis 2 to end it.

Credit where it's due. Deion Miller made 10 tackles, and James Wagenseller boomed a 74-yard punt. Memphis played a sharp game and earned this one in front of a homecoming crowd.

We're 5-3 and 4-2 in the American, 2-2 on the road. The mission resets fast: Air Force comes to Michie Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 7, and that one is personal. Copy that, and beat Navy.

articles.title: Pittsburgh vs Georgia Tech: Ferguson Runs Over Jackets 34-11
articles.matchup: Final: Pittsburgh (6-3) 34, Georgia Tech (2-6) 11, Sat., Oct. 31, Acrisure Stadium, Pittsburgh. Next: vs. Florida State, Fri., Nov. 13, Acrisure Stadium, Pittsburgh
articles.text:
Pittsburgh 34, Georgia Tech 11, and yinz SEE that?! Halloween night on the North Shore was Hail to Heroes at Acrisure Stadium, with the military, veterans and first responders honored on the field, and the Panthers saluted them with a defense that played like it was on a mission. Costumes were welcome, masks weren't, and Georgia Tech's offense looked like it came dressed as a ghost.

My homemade whistle got a workout. Antonio Chadha opened the scoring with a 45-yard field goal. Then Damon Ferguson Jr. finished a 15-play, 86-yard march with a 3-yard touchdown run. That's a "yinz" grade on the whole drive, n'at. La'Vell Wright punched in a 1-yarder for 17-0.

Now the "yikes" column, because I'm honest. Carson Kent had the ball knocked loose at the Tech 2, and Justin Cook coughed one up late in the half to set up a Yellow Jacket field goal. Corey Dailey got intercepted in the fourth, and Georgia Tech scored a play later. Ten penalties for 95 yards. Three turnovers. That's a sandwich-in-silence list, even in a 23-point win.

But the defense? Textbook. Jeremiah Marcelin and Raion Strader each got a sack, Strader broke up two throws, and Alex Sanford Jr. led us with eight tackles. Alberto Mendoza fumbled four times, and Jaeden Moore pounced on the last one at the Tech 15 to end the third quarter. Zach Crothers recovered another at our 21 in the fourth. Tech went 3 of 18 on third down and finished with 238 yards.

Ferguson was the main course: 31 carries, 185 yards and two touchdowns, the last one from a yard out with 3:28 to go for 34-11. We ran for 281 and put up 461 yards. Holden Geriner went 13 of 30 for 180, hit Censere Lee for 44 yards, and dropped a 30-yard touchdown throw right into Cataurus Hicks's hands. Chadha didn't miss a kick all night.

Our last stand was the best tackle grade of the night. Georgia Tech drove 14 plays to our doorstep in the final minute, and the defense knocked away the fourth-down throw.

We're 6-3, 3-3 in the ACC and 5-1 at home. After the open week, Florida State comes to Acrisure Stadium on Friday, Nov. 13. H2P!

articles.title: Georgia Tech vs Pittsburgh: Fumbles Ground Yellow Jackets 34-11
articles.matchup: Final: Pittsburgh (6-3) 34, Georgia Tech (2-6) 11, Sat., Oct. 31, Acrisure Stadium, Pittsburgh. Next: vs. Louisville, Sat., Nov. 7, Bobby Dodd Stadium, Atlanta
articles.text:
Pittsburgh 34, Georgia Tech 11, and I have already re-run this simulation more times than I can count. Back home, Tech Square handed out candy to costumed trick-or-treaters from 5 to 8 p.m. on Saturday. Up on the North Shore at Acrisure Stadium, the Panthers handed us nothing but tricks, and our offense never left its launch pad.

Here is the bug report. Alberto Mendoza put the ball on the ground four times, every one of them in our own half. Pitt sacked him again and again, and the cruelest data point came on the final snap of the third quarter: an 11-yard loss, a fumble, and Jaeden Moore falling on it at our 15. Mendoza finished 16 of 25 for 81 yards. That trajectory never cleared the atmosphere.

The defense kept the orbit stable for a while. Pitt led 10-0 when Jonas Duclona took a touchdown off the board, punching the ball out of Carson Kent's hands at our 2 and recovering it in the end zone. Duclona made 10 tackles, and he was the best thing on our side of the field. Taje McCoy forced a Justin Cook fumble late in the half, Zachary Tobe recovered, and Aidan Birr hammered a 49-yard field goal with three seconds left. 17-3 at the break. Physics still had us in it.

Then Pitt's ground game ran the experiment over and over. Damon Ferguson Jr. carried 31 times for 185 yards and two touchdowns, and the Panthers rushed for 281. A 15-play, 83-yard drive ate 8:07 of the third quarter for a field goal, and Holden Geriner hit Cataurus Hicks for a 30-yard score, 27-3.

Grady Adamson came in and gave the graph a pulse. He ripped off a 36-yard run, and after Trae Stevenson Jr. intercepted a Pitt throw and returned it 22 yards, Adamson ran 18 yards for the touchdown and powered in the two-point try himself, 27-11. Our last drive went 14 plays to the Pitt doorstep and died on fourth down with 50 seconds left.

The final numbers: Pitt 461 yards, us 238. We converted 3 of 18 third downs. Pitt fumbled twice and threw an interception, and we still couldn't make it a game. Graph paper doesn't lie, and tonight it drew a straight slope downhill.

We're 2-6 and 1-4 in the ACC. Louisville comes to Bobby Dodd Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 7. Back to the wind tunnel. To Hell With Georgia, and back to work.

articles.title: Nebraska vs Washington: Late Huskies Strike Spoils Blackout 17-10
articles.matchup: Final: Washington (5-3) 17, Nebraska (5-3) 10, Sat., Oct. 31, Memorial Stadium (Lincoln, NE), Lincoln. Next: at Illinois, Fri., Nov. 6, Gies Memorial Stadium, Champaign
articles.text:
Washington 17, Nebraska 10, and that one is going to sit in my stomach longer than the Halloween candy they handed kids at the Cornhusker Kickoff in the Hawks Center. It was our Blackout game, the first Halloween game in Lincoln since 1998, and Memorial Stadium in black watched a 7-3 lead hold into the final two minutes before it got away.

Credit first, because a farm girl pays her debts. The Blackshirts were nasty. Washington ran 19 times for 32 yards. Kade Pietrzak dropped Elijah Brown for a 10-yard loss, Jahsear Whittington and Mason Goldman each had a sack, and Riley Van Poppel and Vincent Shavers Jr. split another. Owen Chambliss led us with seven tackles. Washington's first three quarters added up to one 50-yard field goal.

Our only touchdown was a beauty. Backed up at our own 5, we went 95 yards in 10 plays. Jamal Rule ripped off a 16-yarder, Mekhi Nelson ran for 19, and Anthony Colandrea dropped a 24-yard touchdown throw on Carter Nelson with 1:40 left in the first quarter. Rule finished with 72 yards on 13 carries, and Jacory Barney Jr. was everywhere: six catches for 65 yards, four punt returns for 46 and a 37-yard kick return.

Now the part I'd rather spike into the floor. Colandrea was intercepted on each of our first two drives, at the Washington 8 and the Washington 30. Early in the fourth, Barney's 31-yard catch put us at their 5. A delay of game, two incompletions and an 8-yard sack later, the 36-yard field goal try missed. That was the night, right there.

Washington went 81 yards in 12 plays, and even after our rush sacked Demond Williams Jr. twice in four snaps, he found Chris Lawson for a 25-yard touchdown with 1:30 left. Two snaps into our answer, Alex McLaughlin intercepted Colandrea and ran it back 48 yards. John Hohl's 42-yard field goal made it 17-10 with 31 seconds left. We outgained them 387 yards to 267 and turned it over three times to their zero. That math doesn't win Big Ten games.

We're 5-3 and 2-3 in the Big Ten, and three of our losses have come by a combined 13 points. Friday, Nov. 6, we're at Illinois. Those people in black deserved better tonight. Now go win one for them. Go Big Red!

articles.title: Washington vs Nebraska: McLaughlin Seals Halloween Win 17-10
articles.matchup: Final: Washington (5-3) 17, Nebraska (5-3) 10, Sat., Oct. 31, Memorial Stadium (Lincoln, NE), Lincoln. Next: vs. Penn State, Sat., Nov. 7, Husky Stadium, Seattle
articles.text:
Washington 17, Nebraska 10, and I am rowing home from Lincoln on pure adrenaline. Back in Seattle, U Village merchants spent Halloween Saturday handing out treats to trick-or-treaters. In Memorial Stadium, wrapped in black for Nebraska's Blackout game, the Huskies took the treat with 1:30 left and then grabbed a second helping 15 seconds later.

Let me be honest about the first three quarters, because this boat doesn't float on fibs. Our offense ran 19 times for 32 yards. Elijah Brown went 19 of 30 for 136 yards and got sacked twice, which no coxswain would allow. Nebraska went 95 yards on a 10-play drive in the first quarter and Anthony Colandrea hit Carter Nelson for a 24-yard touchdown. Tyler Robles drilled a 50-yard field goal with 41 seconds left in the half, and it sat 7-3 until deep in the fourth.

The defense kept us in the water all night. Rylon Dillard-Allen intercepted Colandrea at our 8 on Nebraska's opening drive and ran it back 20 yards. On Nebraska's next drive, Emmanuel Karnley intercepted him again at our 30. Early in the fourth quarter, Nebraska had first-and-goal at our 5, then a delay of game, two incompletions and Derek Colman-Brusa's 8-yard sack. The 36-yard field goal try missed. Zaydrius Rainey-Sale finished with 10 tackles and a sack.

Then Demond Williams Jr. took the oar. Starting from our 14 after a false start, he ran for 17 yards, found Chris Lawson for 22, and shook off two Blackshirt sacks in four snaps. With 1:30 left, he hit Lawson for a 25-yard touchdown. 10-7, Washington. Lawson caught 12 balls for 155 yards. That man earned a seat in the lead boat.

On Nebraska's next snap after an 11-yard catch, Alex McLaughlin jumped a Colandrea throw at the Nebraska 48 and ran it all the way back. Forty-eight yards, touchdown, 17-7 with 1:15 to go. A 42-yard field goal from John Hohl made it 17-10, and that was it. Hunter Green punted eight times for a 48.9-yard average with five inside the 20, the quiet hero of a long, muddy row.

Zero turnovers for us, three interceptions for Nebraska, and a Halloween win in a sea of black. We're 5-3, 2-3 in the Big Ten and 2-1 on the road. Penn State comes to Husky Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 7, and I'm sailing in. Bow Down to Washington!

articles.title: Fresno State vs Oregon State: Mandal Spooks the Beavers 38-22
articles.matchup: Final: Fresno State (5-3) 38, Oregon State (5-3) 22, Sat., Oct. 31, Valley Children's Stadium, Fresno. Next: at Utah State, Sat., Nov. 7, Maverik Stadium, Logan
articles.text:
Fresno State 38, Oregon State 22, and the Valley is buzzing like a raisin shed at harvest. The Red & White Lot turned into a Trunk or Treat for Halloween night, the Bulldogs went with a Blackout theme, and the visitors from Corvallis rolled in on a five-game win streak. They rolled out without it.

It didn't start pretty. Jayden Mandal got intercepted on our second snap, and Oregon State drove inside our 10. Our defense held, a false start wiped out a Beaver touchdown, and they turned it over on downs. After their 54-yard field goal, Mandal went to work: eight plays, 75 yards, and a 15-yard touchdown run. 7-3.

Bryson Donelson made the next statement. After Rayshon Luke ripped off 12 yards, Donelson broke loose for a 63-yard touchdown, 45 seconds after an Oregon State field goal. He finished with 108 yards on 16 carries. Mandal then hit Josiah Freeman for a 26-yard score, and with 18 seconds left in the half, Dylan Hampsten strip-sacked Braden Atkinson and Mordecai Hines fell on it at our 17. 21-9 at the break.

The third quarter was a full harvest: 17 points. Manaki Watanabe hit a 30-yard field goal. On the very next snap, Martin Owusu strip-sacked Atkinson and Maverick Noonan recovered at the Oregon State 19. Mandal ran it in from 3. articles.title: Oregon State vs Fresno State: Fumbles Fell Beavers' Streak 38-22
articles.matchup: Final: Fresno State (5-3) 38, Oregon State (5-3) 22, Sat., Oct. 31, Valley Children's Stadium, Fresno. Next: vs. Texas State, Sat., Nov. 7, Reser Stadium, Corvallis
articles.text:
Fresno State 38, Oregon State 22, and our five-game win streak got felled like an old Douglas fir in a windstorm. Back home, the Downtown Corvallis Organization ran Halloween on the Waterfront and Downtown Trick-or-Treat that afternoon, planning for 800 to 1,200 kids. By the time those kids were sorting candy, the Beavers were in Fresno learning a hard lesson about loose bark.

It started like a good growing season. Sailasa Vadrawale III intercepted Jayden Mandal on Fresno's second snap. We drove inside the Fresno 10, had a touchdown wiped out by a false start and turned it over on downs. Caleb Ojeda put us up 3-0 with a 54-yard field goal, a career long and our longest since Nov. 23, 2024. He made all three of his kicks.

Then the roots came loose. Mandal ran in from 15. Ojeda's 28-yarder made it 7-6, and 45 seconds later Bryson Donelson ran 63 yards for a touchdown. Ojeda hit from 29, but Mandal found Josiah Freeman for a 26-yard score. We reached the Fresno 17 before the half, and Dylan Hampsten strip-sacked Braden Atkinson with 18 seconds left. 21-9.

The third quarter is the stump I can't get past. Right after a Fresno field goal, Martin Owusu strip-sacked Atkinson on our first snap, and Fresno recovered at our 19. Mandal scored from 3 for 31-9. Cornell Hatcher Jr. answered with a 5-yard touchdown run, but Mandal hit Freeman from 31 and it was 38-16. Two lost fumbles: one killed a scoring chance before the half, and one handed Fresno a touchdown.

Credit where the sap runs true. Atkinson went 33 of 59 for 373 yards with no interceptions. That's his eighth straight 300-yard game, which breaks Sean Mannion's school record of seven. DeCorion Temple caught six balls for a career-high 97 yards, the most by an Oregon State tight end since 2013. Eric Olsen caught seven for 71, including a 9-yard touchdown with 1:45 left, and has caught a ball in 23 straight games. Jesse Legree added seven for 70.

But we ran for 77 yards, went 2 for 5 on fourth down and turned it over on downs twice in the fourth. Fresno ran for 190. We're 5-3 and still 3-1 in the Pac-12. Texas State comes to Reser Stadium next Saturday. Measure the damage, sharpen the saw and get back to work.

articles.title: UNLV vs Northern Illinois: Arnold Steals the Halloween Show 31-24
articles.matchup: Final: UNLV (5-3) 31, Northern Illinois (0-8) 24, Sat., Oct. 31, Allegiant Stadium, Paradise. Next: vs. Wyoming, Sat., Nov. 7, Allegiant Stadium, Paradise
articles.text:
UNLV 31, Northern Illinois 24, and the Rebels finally took a bow on Halloween night. October 31 is also Nevada Day, the day the Silver State joined the Union in 1864, and UNLV dressed the game up as Nevada Day & Halloween at Allegiant Stadium. The result was the program's first Halloween win since 1992 and the first win over NIU in six tries.

What an opening act. On the first snap of the night, Jackson Arnold dropped a 75-yard touchdown on Kayden McGee. Seventy-five yards, eleven seconds, curtain up. McGee finished with five catches for 112 yards, his first career 100-yard game.

Then the show wobbled. NIU answered with Telly Johnson Jr.'s 20-yard run. Ramon Villela's 20-yard field goal put us up 10-7, but Taron Dickens hit DeAree Rogers for a 12-yard score. Brady Kerperin intercepted Arnold to open the second quarter, and NIU kicked its way to a 17-10 lead.

Arnold doesn't do understudy nights. He found Keyan Burnett for a 31-yard touchdown to tie it. After NIU missed from 47, he went 71 yards in 11 plays, ran for 18 on the way and hit Taeshaun Lyons from 2 with 20 seconds left. That made it 24-17 at the half. Arnold went 20 of 30 for 269 yards and three touchdowns and ran 13 times for 86 yards. He also threw two interceptions, and I won't pretend those were part of the choreography.

Early in the third, Jai'Den Thomas delivered the move of the night: a 60-yard touchdown run for 31-17. He finished with 114 yards on 16 carries. NIU hit back with a 61-yard touchdown from Dickens to George Dimopoulos, and then the defense took over. Mumu Bin-Wahad intercepted Dickens at our 10 with 12:52 left and returned it 53 yards. It was his fourth interception of the season, and he added eight tackles. NIU's 54-yard field goal try missed at 2:06, Arnold ripped off a 27-yard run, and we knelt it out.

I'll be honest: NIU outgained us 493 yards to 473 and kept the ball for 35:09. But the Huskies didn't score for the final 24:31. Tony-Louis Nkuba made nine tackles, Elias Rudolph had a sack and Matt Choules averaged 51.7 yards on three punts.

We're 5-3, 3-1 in the Mountain West and 3-1 at home. Wyoming comes to Allegiant on Saturday, Nov. 7. Keep the lights on, Rebel fans. And that's a wrap!

articles.title: Northern Illinois vs UNLV: Huskies Take Rebels to the Wire 31-24
articles.matchup: Final: UNLV (5-3) 31, Northern Illinois (0-8) 24, Sat., Oct. 31, Allegiant Stadium, Paradise. Next: at San José State, Sat., Nov. 7, CEFCU Stadium, San Jose
articles.text:
UNLV 31, Northern Illinois 24, and this one stings like a hailstorm a week before harvest. Back in DeKalb, the city's official trick-or-treat hours ran 4 to 7 p.m. on Halloween. By the time the porch lights went off at home, our Huskies were out in the desert going toe to toe with UNLV, and we walked out of Allegiant Stadium still looking for the first win.

The night opened rough. Jackson Arnold hit Kayden McGee for a 75-yard touchdown on the very first snap. We didn't flinch. A 10-play, 75-yard drive ended with Telly Johnson Jr. bouncing outside on third-and-1 for a 20-yard score. Our defense made three stops inside the 5 to hold UNLV to a field goal, then Taron Dickens found DeAree Rogers for a 12-yard touchdown at 0:53 of the first. Brady Kerperin intercepted Arnold to open the second quarter, and JJ Schlenhardt's 27-yard field goal made it 17-10, Huskies.

Then the weeds crept in. Arnold tied it with a 31-yard throw to Keyan Burnett. Schlenhardt missed from 47, and UNLV went 71 yards to score on a 2-yard catch by Taeshaun Lyons with 20 seconds left. Jai'Den Thomas broke a 60-yard touchdown run early in the third for 31-17.

We answered fast. Dickens hit George Dimopoulos for a 61-yard touchdown at 9:31, and it was 31-24. Late in the third, Champ Smith III went up and intercepted Arnold at our 1. That's the kind of play you plant a whole season around.

The fourth quarter is the part I'll be staring at for a while. We had the ball, we had the clock, and we came up empty. Mumu Bin-Wahad intercepted Dickens at the UNLV 10 with 12:52 left. Schlenhardt's 54-yard try missed at 2:06. UNLV knelt it out.

Here's what the soil says. We outgained them 493 yards to 473, ran for 240 and held the ball for 35:09. Elijah Porter ran for a career-high 113 yards on 21 carries. Dimopoulos had a career-high 127 on seven catches, and Rogers added 96. Jack Murray and Jashawn Nelson made nine tackles each, and Amari Washington had a sack. Missed kicks and two late empty drives were the difference.

We're 0-8 and 0-4 in the Mountain West, and this team is still growing. San José State is next on Saturday, Nov. 7. Patience, Huskie fans. The crop is coming.

articles.title: Boise State vs Texas State: Cutforth Saves Halloween Night 46-45
articles.matchup: Final: Boise State (7-1) 46, Texas State (4-4) 45, Sat., Oct. 31, Albertsons Stadium, Boise. Next: at Colorado State, Sat., Nov. 7, Canvas Stadium, Fort Collins
articles.text:
Boise State 46, Texas State 45, and my blue car needed a full lap of the lot before my heart rate came down. It was the first Blue After Dark game, Halloween night, with trunk-or-treat in the tailgate lots and Kellen Moore back on The Blue for the unveiling of his 11-foot bronze statue at halftime. By the fourth quarter, the scariest thing in the stadium was the scoreboard.

The first half was pure Bronco football. A 13-play, 83-yard opening drive ended with Maddux Madsen running in from 6. Dylan Riley scored from 5, Madsen added a 1-yard run, and freshman Rasean Jones caught a 12-yard touchdown with four seconds left. It was 28-3 at the break, and the statue had a perfect view.

Then we fell asleep at the griddle. Brad Jackson hit Chris Dawn Jr. for 67 yards. Harry Stewart III fumbled, and Texas State turned it into a touchdown and a two-point run. Jackson ran 35 yards for another. He opened the fourth with a 44-yard strike to Beau Sparks, and at 8:58 Jayden Bradley intercepted Madsen and ran it 20 yards for a score. Thirty-six straight points, 39-28. I set my fork down.

Enter Max Cutforth. He hit Jones from 9 at 6:15. Mana Tuioti grabbed his first career interception and returned it to the Texas State 11, and on fourth down Cutforth found Jones again. 40-39. Texas State answered with a 72-yard bomb to Zechariah Sample. Cutforth went right back to Jones for 44 yards on the first snap, and six plays and 1:07 later he hit Akeem Wright for an 18-yard touchdown with 2:40 left. 46-45.

Jaden Mickey sealed it by breaking up a fourth-down throw at 1:55. Jones finished with nine catches for 117 yards and three touchdowns. He's the second Bronco freshman in the FBS era to catch three in one game. Wright had eight for 116, Cutforth went 8 of 13 for 131 yards and three scores, Riley ran 25 times for 86, and Boen Phelps made eight tackles.

We're 7-1, 4-0 in the Pac-12 and 4-0 at home, with seven straight wins. Next Saturday it's Colorado State in Fort Collins. Pancakes are on me, Bronco Nation. Keep it blue!

articles.title: Texas State vs Boise State: 36-Point Run Falls Short 46-45
articles.matchup: Final: Boise State (7-1) 46, Texas State (4-4) 45, Sat., Oct. 31, Albertsons Stadium, Boise. Next: at Oregon State, Sat., Nov. 7, Reser Stadium, Corvallis
articles.text:
Boise State 46, Texas State 45, and I have been floating in a daze ever since. Back home in San Marcos, Wonder World Cave & Adventure Park threw Boo Fest on Halloween afternoon, with kids trick-or-treating through Texas' only earthquake-formed cave. Up in Boise that night, our Bobcats threw the scariest second half on the schedule and still came home one point short.

The ugly part first, because this river doesn't run uphill. Boise held the ball for 37:01 and went 3 for 3 on fourth down. Maddux Madsen ran in from 6 yards and from 1, Dylan Riley scored from 5, and Rasean Jones caught a 12-yard touchdown with four seconds left in the half. Jacob Bonilla's 31-yard field goal was all we had. It was 28-3 at the break, and I was ready to drift off.

Then Brad Jackson went off. He hit Chris Dawn Jr. for a 67-yard touchdown at 9:21 of the third. Michael Patterson III forced a Harry Stewart III fumble, Cole Nilles fell on it, and Jackson found Ty Stamey from 3 before Beau Sparks ran in the two-point try. Then Jackson took off himself, 35 yards to the end zone. That made it 28-25, and the third quarter went to us 22-0.

Seventy-two seconds into the fourth, Jackson dropped a 44-yard touchdown on Sparks for a 32-28 lead. At 8:58, Jayden Bradley intercepted Madsen at the Boise 20 and took it back for six. That was 39-28, and 36 straight points. The Cats were eating.

Then it slipped away. Max Cutforth took over for Boise and hit Jones from 9. Mana Tuioti intercepted a Tucker Cusano throw and returned it to our 11, and Cutforth found Jones on fourth down for a 40-39 Boise lead. Jackson answered two plays later with a 72-yard strike to Zechariah Sample, 45-40 with 3:46 left. Boise needed 1:07 to go 75 yards, and Cutforth hit Akeem Wright from 18. On our last shot, fourth down at 1:55, Jaden Mickey broke up the throw to Dawn.

Jackson finished 23 of 38 for 327 yards and four touchdowns, plus 54 yards on the ground. Sample turned two catches into 89 yards. Patterson made 10 tackles, Bradley made nine, and Tymere Jackson had a sack. We're 4-4, 2-2 in the Pac-12 and 0-3 on the road, with a trip to Oregon State next Saturday. Going with the flow nearly stole one in Boise. Next week, we paddle harder. Eat 'em up, Cats!

On our last shot, fourth down at 1:55, Jaden Mickey broke up the throw to Dawn.

Jackson finished 23 of 38 for 327 yards and four touchdowns, plus 54 yards on the ground. Sample turned two catches into 89 yards. Patterson made 10 tackles, Bradley made nine, and Tymere Jackson had a sack. We're 4-4, 2-2 in the Pac-12 and 0-3 on the road, with a trip to Oregon State next Saturday. Going with the flow nearly stole one in Boise. Next week, we paddle harder. Eat 'em up, Cats!

summary.text: Boise State beat Texas State 46-45 on Saturday, Oct. 31, at Albertsons Stadium. The Bobcats are 4-4 and 2-2 in the Pac-12.
Texas State trailed 28-3 at halftime, then scored 36 straight points to lead 39-28, capped by Jayden Bradley's 20-yard interception return.
Brad Jackson threw for 327 yards and four touchdowns and ran 35 yards for another score.
We gave Boise the scare of its Halloween. The Broncos just got the last treat.
